state_program_name: Residential Care Facility (RCF), licensed by the Ohio Department of Health under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16; Medicaid via the Assisted Living Waiver (1915(c) HCBS waiver administered by the Ohio Department of Aging)

front_matter.purpose:
## Purpose

This Policy & Procedure Manual sets out how **[AGENCY NAME]** operates its Residential Care Facility (RCF) in Ohio. The RCF is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health (ODH) under Ohio Revised Code (ORC) Chapter 3721 and Ohio Administrative Code (OAC) Chapter 3701-16. The facility also participates in Medicaid through the Assisted Living Waiver, a 1915(c) Home and Community-Based Services (HCBS) waiver administered by the Ohio Department of Aging (ODA).

The manual is meant to:

- Turn the written-policy, plan and resident-document requirements of OAC Chapter 3701-16 and ORC 3721.13 into working procedures staff can follow.
- Protect residents' rights, health, safety and dignity.
- Give administrators, staff, surveyors and waiver reviewers one organized place to find how the facility meets each requirement.
- Support consistent practice in admission, assessment, personal care, medication, skilled nursing limits, dietary services, infection control, emergency preparedness and fire safety, staffing and training, and resident finances and discharge.

**This manual is a template and is not in force until it is customized and adopted.** Every [AGENCY NAME] placeholder, and every facility-specific detail (bed count, services offered, meals served, special care unit status, skilled-nursing scope, staffing pattern, and so on), must be completed to reflect actual operations. The manual must not describe services or practices the facility does not actually provide.
front_matter.how_to_use:
## How to Use This Manual

**Organization.** The manual follows the order of the Ohio rules (OAC Chapter 3701-16, then ORC 3721.13 residents' rights, then Assisted Living Waiver provisions). A surveyor or reviewer can therefore locate each policy by rule. This ordering is a practical choice, not an ODH requirement.

**Appendix A is the crosswalk.** Appendix A maps every official item to the specific policy in this manual that satisfies it. To check compliance with a rule paragraph, find it in Appendix A and go to the policy listed. To confirm a policy's regulatory basis, read the rule cite shown at the top of the policy.

**Who should use it**

- *Administrator and acting administrator:* Use it as the operating reference for daily management, coverage scheduling and survey readiness.
- *Nursing and medication staff:* Use the assessment, medication, dressing and skilled-nursing sections.
- *Direct care and support staff:* Use the sections on personal care, residents' rights, incident reporting, emergency response, infection control, dietary services and activities.
- *Governing body or owner:* Use it to review, adopt and oversee the facility's policies.

**Customizing the manual**

1. Replace every **[AGENCY NAME]** placeholder and complete all bracketed facility-specific fields.
2. Delete or revise any policy that does not match what the facility offers. Examples are the special care unit, dressings, enteral feedings, and care for residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness.
3. Confirm the final text against the current rules at the cited URLs before adoption.

**Adoption.** The manual must be formally adopted by the facility's governing body (owner, board or other authorized body). The adoption date and signature are recorded in the manual's adoption record.

**Keeping it current.** The manual must be kept current. Review it at least annually and whenever a rule, ODH or ODA guidance, or facility operations change. Record each revision with its date and the person who approved it. Keep superseded versions according to the facility's records policy.

**Staff training.** Staff must be trained on the manual. Training happens at orientation and when policies change. The orientation, resident-rights, fire and evacuation, and other training deadlines are set out in the policies that implement OAC 3701-16-06 and OAC 3701-16-13. Keep training records, including staff acknowledgment that they have read and understood the manual, available for surveyors.

*Notes on the rules:*

- Rule 3701-16-07(F)(2) refers to the smoking policy at 3701-16-13(W), but the current rule places smoking at 3701-16-13(U). This manual uses (U). Confirm with ODH if there is any question.
- The individual rule text of OAC Chapter 5160-33 was not reviewed in preparing this manual. Check the current chapter and ODA provider certification requirements before relying on the waiver sections.
- Rule text was condensed in preparing this manual. Always consult the full current rule at https://codes.ohio.gov.

### Regulators and contacts

| Regulator | Role | Contact |
|---|---|---|
| **Ohio Department of Health (ODH), Bureau of Regulatory Operations (Licensure Unit)** | Licenses and inspects RCFs under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16; issues initial and renewal licenses | Phone: (614) 466-7713; Email: liccert@odh.ohio.gov; Web: https://odh.ohio.gov/know-our-programs/residential-care-facilities-assisted-living |
| **Ohio Department of Aging (ODA)** | Administers the Assisted Living Waiver day to day and certifies waiver providers; also administers PASSPORT | Web: https://aging.ohio.gov/care-and-living/care-options/assisted-living (no phone or email on file) |
| **Ohio Department of Medicaid (ODM)** | Single state Medicaid agency; provider enrollment and revalidation, EVV program, interagency agreement with ODA for the waiver | Web: https://medicaid.ohio.gov/resources-for-providers/enrollment-and-support/provider-enrollment/support/support (no phone or email on file) |
| **State Fire Marshal or approved local fire department** | Pre-license and at least every-15-month fire inspections (ORC 3721.02) | Contact the State Fire Marshal or your local fire department; see https://codes.ohio.gov/ohio-revised-code/section-3721.02 (no phone or email on file) |

Add the facility's local contacts (assigned ODH surveyor or region, ODA waiver contact, local fire department) in the spaces provided in the customized manual: **[AGENCY NAME] regulator contact sheet**.

### How the state reviews this manual

ODH does not appear to publish a single policy checklist, plan of operation or policy-review form for Ohio RCFs, and it does not appear to review a policy manual at licensure. Compliance with the written-policy requirements is evaluated during on-site surveys. ODH states that these include at least one unannounced survey in each 9- to 15-month cycle. ODH inspects at least every 15 months (30 months if clean-record conditions are met), and the fire marshal or approved fire department inspects at least every 15 months (ORC 3721.02).

Because there is no single checklist, the official documents used to review this manual are the rules themselves, chiefly the items in OAC Chapter 3701-16 that require written policies, plans or resident-facing documents. They are:

- OAC 3701-16-03: Initial, renewal and change of operator license applications. Its application items are administrative and are not policy content. The closure-notice plan in paragraph (M) is policy content.
- OAC 3701-16-06: Qualifications and health of personnel
- OAC 3701-16-07: Resident agreement; other information to be provided upon admission; risk agreements
- OAC 3701-16-09: Personal care services; medication administration; resident medications; application of dressings; supervision of therapeutic diets
- OAC 3701-16-12: Changes in residents' health status; incidents; infection control; tuberculosis control plan
- OAC 3701-16-13: Building, plumbing, fire and carbon monoxide safety requirements
- The **Residential Care Facility Initial License Packet** (ODH Bureau of Regulatory Operations, Licensure Unit; file dated April 2026; no form number found). It was not opened in preparing this manual, so no items are taken from it. Check it by hand at https://odh.ohio.gov/wps/portal/gov/odh/know-our-programs/residential-care-facilities-assisted-living/resources/rcfinitallicensepacket for any additional policy items.

**Appendix A maps every official item to the policy that satisfies it.** Each item is identified by its rule paragraph number and cite. Use it as the facility's self-review checklist before licensing, at renewal, and ahead of unannounced surveys.

### Maintaining compliance

- **Customize** the manual: replace all [AGENCY NAME] placeholders and facility-specific fields.
- **Adopt** it through the facility's governing body and record the adoption.
- **Keep it current** through at least annual review and prompt updates when rules or operations change.
- **Train staff** on the manual at orientation (within three working days under OAC 3701-16-06(I)), annually, and whenever policies change, and keep the training records.

This manual supports compliance but is not legal advice. Where this manual and the current text of a rule differ, the rule controls.

citations.title: Residential care facility definitions
citations.requirement: Defines an RCF in two prongs: 17+ unrelated residents with personal care for 3+, or 3+ residents with personal care for 3+ and skilled nursing for 1+. Also defines skilled nursing care and the resident call system (par. FF).

citations.title: General provisions and prohibitions
citations.requirement: An RCF may not admit or retain residents who need skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011 limits. Par. (D) sets the services an RCF may provide, and 3701-16-07(A) bars admission beyond it.

citations.title: Initial, renewal and change of operator license applications
citations.requirement: Initial application due at least 60 days before opening. Needs CPA-signed 3-month solvency statement, certificate of occupancy (R-4, I-1 or I-2), fire and heating reports. Renewal needs application and fee. Change of operator due 60 days ahead.

citations.title: Procedures for inspecting and licensing homes; fees
citations.requirement: Non-refundable fee of $320 per 50 beds or part thereof. ODH inspects at least every 15 months (30 months if clean-record conditions are met). Fire marshal or approved fire department inspects at least every 15 months.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: administrator
citations.requirement: Administrator is responsible for daily operation and must provide at least 20 hours per week on site between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. An acting administrator (21+) is designated for absences. Administrator must be reachable at other times.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staff on duty and on call
citations.requirement: At least one qualified personal care staff member on duty at all times. The overnight person may be on call only if call system rules in 3701-16-14(B)(5) are met. When only one person is on duty, designate another qualified staff member on call.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: sufficient staff, evacuation, first aid
citations.requirement: Staff enough to meet assessed care, supervision and emotional needs, dietary, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and activities. Staff needed for the evacuation plan are present at all times. A first-aid-trained personal care staff member is on site at all times.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staffing basis and clinical consultant
citations.requirement: Staffing need not count needs met by third parties or refused by the resident, if documented. A facility admitting late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs or serious mental illness residents must have a psychologist or physician on staff or consulting.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: RN supervision of skilled nursing
citations.requirement: A facility providing skilled nursing beyond special diets, dressings or medication must employ or contract an RN for onsite supervision, have a licensed nurse on call, and have enough nursing staff.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: coverage schedule; residents not to work
citations.requirement: Operator or administrator sets a coverage schedule that includes vacations, emergencies and long absences. Residents may not be mandated, coerced or persuaded to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: medication, diet, dressing and skilled-care staffing
citations.requirement: A facility that administers medication needs an RN, a medication-course LPN (acting at an RN or physician direction), a physician, or another person authorized by law on duty. Dietitian needed for therapeutic diets. Enough nurses for dressings or skilled care.

citations.title: Personnel requirements: staffing records; admission limit
citations.requirement: Keep personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms. Do not admit more residents than the facility can serve with consistent nursing coverage and other appropriate staffing for resident volume and needs.

citations.title: Personnel health: communicable disease, impairment, pre-employment exam
citations.requirement: Staff with a transmissible disease may not work while communicable unless duties are modified. Staff may not be impaired by alcohol or drugs. Every paid worker is examined within 30 days before starting or on day one. Retain exam copies.

citations.title: Staff age and language requirements
citations.requirement: Personal care staff are 16+ (under 18 need on-site supervision by an adult over 18). Administrator is 21+. Staff assisting with medication must read, write and understand English. Activity planners need training for cognitive and mental illness populations.

citations.title: Personal care staff: first aid and competency
citations.requirement: First-aid training within 60 days of hire (Red Cross, AHA, or equivalent). Before working unsupervised, staff must complete RN or LPN-taught personal care training, an ODH-approved aide program, or Medicare home health aide training.

citations.title: Special-population training, annual CE and therapeutic diet training
citations.requirement: Cognitive impairment and serious mental illness care: 2 hrs initial within 14 days and 4 hrs CE yearly (4 and 8 hrs if both groups are served). All personal care staff: 8 hrs CE yearly. Dietitian training before therapeutic diets.

citations.title: Administrator qualifications and continuing education
citations.requirement: Administrator holds a nursing home administrator license, or has 3,000 hours of operational responsibility, 100 credit hours in gerontology or health care, a bachelor's degree, or a licensed health professional credential. 9 hrs CE yearly.

citations.title: Orientation within three working days
citations.requirement: Each staff member completes orientation within 3 working days: physical layout, job duties, policies and procedures, how to secure emergency help, and resident rights. No staff member is alone with residents until orientation and fire training are complete.

citations.title: Professional licensure and annual resident-rights training
citations.requirement: Professionals used by the facility hold current Ohio licenses where required. Annual (calendar-year) staff training on each ORC 3721.13(A) right and on comparable service for residents with similar needs, plus as needed.

citations.title: Disqualifications for direct-care employment
citations.requirement: Do not employ in direct care anyone with a disqualifying offense under ORC 3721.121(C)(1), who fails forms or fingerprints, or who has an abuse, neglect or misappropriation finding on the Ohio or another state's nurse aide registry or a license action for the same.

citations.title: Admission prohibitions and sex offender search
citations.requirement: Search the Ohio sex offender registry before admission. Do not admit or retain (except hospice) residents needing skilled nursing beyond ORC 3721.011, 8+ hrs/day or 40+ hrs/week, restraints, bedridden, stage III/IV pressure ulcers, or unstable conditions.

citations.title: Written resident agreement
citations.requirement: Signed, dated agreement before residency, with a copy and explanation provided. It covers charges and deposits, 30-day written notice of a rate change, refund policy, services, skilled nursing limits and mandatory discharge if limits are exceeded.

citations.title: Pre-admission policy disclosures and risk agreements
citations.requirement: Before admission, give and explain the rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR (not a condition of admission), disability accommodation and special care unit policies. Written risk agreements need the resident's consent and a signed acknowledgment; rights waivers are void.

citations.title: Initial resident health assessment
citations.requirement: Written assessment within 48 hours of admission (items (C)(11)-(12) within 14 days). An assessment done within 90 days before admission may be used. Covers preferences, diagnoses, falls risk, medications, diet, function and self-administration. Offer flu and pneumococcal vaccines yearly.

citations.title: Annual reassessment and change in condition
citations.requirement: Reassess health at least annually, within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner when a change in condition or function warrants new services or equipment. Document diagnoses, diet, weight, medications and function.

citations.title: Special care unit placement; unmet needs; transfer or discharge
citations.requirement: Secured special care unit admission requires a licensed professional's determination, an updated agreement, and cannot rest on diagnosis alone. If needs exceed services, hold a resident meeting, discuss waiver options, and discharge under ORC 3721.16 and OAC Ch. 3701-61 if needed.

citations.title: Personal care services
citations.requirement: State the extent and types of personal care in policies and agreements and provide it to residents who need it, unless refused or covered by a risk agreement. Care must meet accepted standards, be given by trained staff, and match the assessment.

citations.title: Medication self-administration and administration
citations.requirement: Medications are self-administered except as authorized. Staff may only remind, hand over, open containers or assist physically impaired residents; they may not fill pill organizers. Administration is limited to an RN, a qualified LPN, a physician, or another authorized person, on a prescriber's order.

citations.title: Medication orders, storage, labeling, records, disposal
citations.requirement: Telephone orders go to a licensed nurse only and are signed within 14 days. Keep all prescription drugs locked. Do not repackage or relabel. Keep a medication list and administration record. Send medications with the resident or destroy them with consent. Prevent controlled-substance theft.

citations.title: Application of dressings
citations.requirement: A facility that provides dressings must write down which dressings it manages, have written procedures, use only authorized individuals, evaluate each such resident at least every 7 days for transfer, document in the record, and have a nurse coordinate care.

citations.title: Prohibition on restraints and isolation
citations.requirement: Physical, chemical and isolation restraints are forbidden (includes locked room doors and geriatric chairs). Secured special care units are allowed only if individualized, reviewed at each reassessment, code compliant, and not based solely on diagnosis.

citations.title: Skilled nursing: 120-day limit and extended-care agreement
citations.requirement: Part-time intermittent skilled nursing is capped at 120 days per 12 months. Beyond that, a written agreement with the resident and physician is required, with re-determination at least every 30 days (hospice: every 15 days).

citations.title: Skilled nursing by facility staff; enteral feedings
citations.requirement: Written procedures, authorized providers only, evaluation at least every 7 days for transfer, orders signed within 14 days, and a coordinating nurse. Part-time intermittent enteral feedings also require written types, weight documentation and a dietitian.

citations.title: Dietary services; supervision of therapeutic diets
citations.requirement: Specify meals offered (0-3 daily). Max 16 hours between supper and breakfast, evening snack, menus planned a week ahead and kept 3 months, a week of staples and 2 days of perishables, always-available drinking water, and a dietitian for therapeutic diets.

citations.title: Activities, pets and laundry
citations.requirement: Provide or arrange varied activities (daily newspaper or community brochures, community activity and transport information). Written pet protocol after a veterinarian consult. Specify laundry services in the resident agreement.

citations.title: Resident finances and guardianship
citations.requirement: Do not coerce assignment of assets. Managing funds needs a witnessed written authorization. Funds over $1,000 go in a separate interest-bearing account, with a surety bond and a final accounting. Staff may not be guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related.

citations.title: Change in health status and incidents
citations.requirement: On a significant adverse change, get immediate intervention, note it in the record, give information to the treating party, and notify the sponsor. For incidents, investigate and keep a separate incident log with time, place, date, description and action.

citations.title: Infection prevention and control; TB plan; water management
citations.requirement: Written infection program with a trained designee reported to ODH within 10 days of any change, a TB control plan (3701-15-03), a surveillance plan, isolation, hand hygiene and laundry rules, and a legionella water management program.

citations.title: Building, plumbing, egress and electrical safety
citations.requirement: Certificate of occupancy, Ohio plumbing code, thermostatic mixing devices on bathing fixtures, Ohio fire code compliance, clear egress, door hold-opens only if they release on power loss or alarm, and safe electrical systems and appliances.

citations.title: Written disaster preparedness plan
citations.requirement: Written plan, kept on site and electronically off-site. Covers evacuation (impaired mobility, transport to receiving facilities), fire watch, missing residents with law enforcement notification, severe weather, and telling ODH of any business interruption.

citations.title: Fire and disaster drills and records
citations.requirement: 12 fire drills a year (one per shift every 3 months), each staff member in one a year, residents evacuated in 2 drills per shift yearly, 2 disaster drills yearly (one tornado drill March-July). Keep written records 3 years.

citations.title: Evacuation maps, systems, fire training, monthly inspection
citations.requirement: Post floor plans on each floor. Automatic sprinklers and fire alarms, with records kept. Fire and evacuation training within 3 working days, annual fire prevention training, resident emergency training, monthly fire safety inspection (kept 3 years), and CO detectors.

citations.title: Smoking and oxygen safety
citations.requirement: Smoking and vaping only in designated areas. No smoking or flame where oxygen is stored or used, with signs posted. Take reasonable precautions for smoking residents, use non-combustible ash receptacles, and provide shelter in bad weather.

citations.title: Fire reporting and transfer agreements
citations.requirement: Report any fire, fire damage, or fire or smoke illness, injury or death to the State Fire Marshal and ODH within 24 hours on their forms. Keep written transfer agreements with facilities that can meet residents' needs.

citations.title: Space requirements
citations.requirement: New units: 100 sq ft single, 80 sq ft per person shared, max 4 per room. Resident-activated call system in rooms and bathrooms. One toilet, sink and tub or shower per 8 residents. Hot water 105-120 F where facility controlled.

citations.title: Residents' rights: care, dignity, privacy, restraints, communication
citations.requirement: Rights include freedom from abuse, informed consent, record confidentiality, privacy, freedom from restraint except by physician order (12-hour emergency limit), choice of pharmacist and physician, unrestricted communication, and civil rights. Waiver is void ((C)).

citations.title: Residents' rights: charges, finances, property, room changes
citations.requirement: Written notice of basic rate and extra charges; 30 days' notice of rate change; itemized monthly bill; freedom from financial exploitation; quarterly accounting if funds are delegated; access to deposited property; notice before room or roommate change.

citations.title: Residents' rights: transfer and discharge; hospice choice
citations.requirement: Discharge allowed only for listed reasons (needs unmet, improved, safety, nonpayment, license loss, etc.). Needs adequate preparation and a destination that can meet needs. The resident may choose a licensed hospice.

citations.title: Residents' rights: grievances and sponsor notice
citations.requirement: Residents may voice grievances to staff, ODH or others of their choice without reprisal, including access to a residents' rights advocate. Make a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of a significant health change within 12 hours.

citations.title: HCBS waivers: assisted living
citations.requirement: Governs administration and reimbursement of the Assisted Living Waiver. Residents must live in an ODH-licensed RCF, and the maximum rates are in Appendix A. Services only, not room and board.

citations.title: Assisted living HCBS waiver program
citations.requirement: Assisted Living Waiver provider rules: ODH-licensed RCF plus ODA waiver provider certification, and a three-tier unit rate model. Individual rule text not fetched in this pass.

policies.title: Organization, Governing Body and Administrator Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: Operator/governing body, administrator, acting administrator, all staff and residents
policies.purpose: To define who is accountable for the operation of [AGENCY NAME], a Residential Care Facility (RCF) licensed by the Ohio Department of Health (ODH) under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16. This policy sets out administrator presence, absence coverage and the limits on resident involvement in operations.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is governed by its operator/governing body, which appoints an administrator and holds that person accountable for compliance with OAC Chapter 3701-16. Under OAC 3701-16-05(A)-(B), the administrator is responsible for the daily operation of the facility. The administrator is on site at least 20 hours per week between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. and is reachable at all other times. An acting administrator, age 21 or older, is designated for every absence. Under OAC 3701-16-05(E), the operator or administrator maintains a written coverage schedule that addresses vacations, emergencies and long absences. The administrator must be at least 21 years old. Personal care staff must be at least 16, and any staff member under 18 works under on-site supervision by an adult over 18. Staff who assist with medication must read, write and understand English (OAC 3701-16-06(D)). Residents are never mandated, coerced or persuaded to supervise other residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility.

definitions.definition: The person or entity that holds the RCF license and is legally responsible for the facility and for appointing the administrator.
The individual responsible for the daily operation of the facility, who meets the age and on-site requirements of OAC 3701-16-05 and 3701-16-06(D).
A designated individual, age 21 or older, who assumes the administrator's responsibilities during the administrator's absence.
The written schedule that names who is responsible for the facility during the administrator's vacations, emergencies and long absences.

procedures: The operator/governing body appoints the administrator in writing and records the appointment, the start date and the administrator's age verification in the administrator's personnel record.
The administrator carries out daily operation: staffing, resident care oversight, budget, regulatory compliance, resident and family communication, and policy enforcement.
The administrator works at least 20 hours per week on site between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. and records on-site hours on a weekly administrator hours log kept at the front office.
The administrator stays reachable by phone at [PHONE] outside on-site hours. The after-hours contact number is posted at the staff station and given to every shift.

The operator designates an acting administrator, age 21 or older, and records the name, age verification and contact information. The acting administrator is oriented to this manual, the emergency plan and reporting duties before serving.
The operator or administrator prepares and maintains a written coverage schedule. It covers vacations, emergencies and long absences and names the acting administrator for each period.
For any planned absence, the administrator updates the coverage schedule at least [NUMBER] days ahead and briefs the acting administrator on open issues, pending reports and resident concerns.
For an unplanned or emergency absence, the administrator or the operator activates the coverage schedule the same day and notifies all shifts of who is in charge.

For an extended absence, the operator reviews whether the acting administrator can keep meeting the 20-hour on-site requirement and takes action if not, including appointing a replacement administrator.

The administrator verifies at hire that personal care staff are at least 16. Any staff member under 18 is scheduled only when an adult over 18 is on site to supervise, and the supervisor is named on the schedule.

The administrator verifies that every staff member who assists with medication can read, write and understand English before the person is assigned that task, and documents the verification in the personnel file.

Staff may not ask, require, pressure or encourage any resident to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility. Any report of this practice is investigated by the administrator within 24 hours and corrected.
The governing body meets at least quarterly with the administrator to review operations, staffing, compliance and QA results (see GOV-04). Minutes are kept.
The administrator reviews this policy annually as part of document control (see GOV-03).

responsibilities.duty: Appoints the administrator and acting administrator, approves the coverage schedule, and reviews operations at least quarterly.
Runs daily operation, works the required on-site hours, stays reachable, maintains the coverage schedule and verifies staff age and language qualifications.
Assumes administrator duties during absences and keeps records of actions taken.
Know who is in charge on every shift and never ask residents to perform staff functions.

documentation: Administrator appointment letter and age verification
Weekly administrator on-site hours log
Acting administrator designation and age verification
Written coverage schedule and updates
Staff age and English-language verification in personnel files
Governing body meeting minutes

policies.title: Licensure, Posting and Regulatory Compliance
policies.applies_to: Operator, administrator and all staff
policies.purpose: To ensure [AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health before accepting residents, stays licensed, and is ready for ODH and fire inspections.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] operates only under a current ODH residential care facility license issued under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16 (never OAC Chapter 3701-17, which governs nursing homes). Under OAC 3701-16-01, an RCF is a home that either (1) serves 17 or more unrelated individuals and provides personal care to at least 3 of them, or (2) serves 3 or more unrelated individuals and provides personal care to at least 3 and skilled nursing care to at least 1. The initial application is filed at least 60 days before the proposed opening. It includes a CPA-signed statement showing 3 months of solvency, a certificate of occupancy (R-4, I-1 or I-2), and fire and heating reports (OAC 3701-16-03). The license fee is $320 per 50 beds or part thereof (ORC 3721.02) and is non-refundable. It is due with the initial application and with each renewal application. [AGENCY NAME] holds one license per building, except that buildings on the same lot operated as one facility may be licensed together. No resident is admitted before the license is issued. The license is posted where residents and visitors can see it.

definitions.definition: The Ohio Department of Health, Bureau of Regulatory Operations (Licensure Unit), which licenses and inspects RCFs. Contact: liccert@odh.ohio.gov, (614) 466-7713.

A facility meeting one of the two prongs of OAC 3701-16-01: 17 or more unrelated residents with personal care for at least 3; or 3 or more unrelated residents with personal care for at least 3 and skilled nursing for at least 1.
An assignment or transfer of the facility's operation to a new operator, which requires a license application to ODH.
A statement signed by a certified public accountant showing the financial ability to operate the facility for 3 months.

procedures: The operator confirms before applying that the facility meets the RCF definition in OAC 3701-16-01 and that the planned capacity and services match the license category sought.

The operator assembles the initial application packet: ODH application, CPA-signed 3-month solvency statement, certificate of occupancy (R-4, I-1 or I-2), fire report, heating report and the fee. The packet is checked against the current ODH form before submission.

The operator calculates the fee at $320 per 50 beds or part thereof of licensed capacity (for example, 51 beds is two units) and pays it with the application. The operator understands the fee is non-refundable.
The operator files the initial application with ODH at least 60 days before the proposed opening date and keeps proof of the filing date.
The administrator coordinates the pre-license inspection by the State Fire Marshal or approved local fire department and any ODH inspection. Deficiencies are corrected before the opening date.
No resident is admitted and no personal care or skilled nursing is provided until ODH has issued the license. The administrator verifies this before the first admission.
Upon receipt, the administrator posts the license in a conspicuous public area and keeps a copy in the administrator's file. The posting is checked monthly.
The administrator calendars the license expiration date and the renewal application and fee due date. A renewal application with the fee is submitted before the license expires.

The facility keeps one license per building. If more than one building sits on the same lot and is operated as one facility, the administrator confirms the licensing arrangement with ODH before opening or changing the arrangement.

ODH inspects at least every 15 months. It may extend the cycle to 30 months if the clean-record conditions in ORC 3721.02 are met. The fire marshal or approved fire department inspects at least every 15 months. [AGENCY NAME] treats all inspections as unannounced and stays survey-ready at all times (see GOV-04).
During any inspection, the administrator or acting administrator accompanies surveyors, provides requested records promptly, and keeps notes of findings discussed.
Within the deadline stated on any statement of deficiencies, the administrator submits a written plan of correction and keeps evidence of each correction.
If a change of operator is planned, the proposed operator files a change-of-operator application with ODH at least 60 days before the proposed assignment or transfer (see GOV-06).
The administrator directs licensing questions to the ODH Licensure Unit at liccert@odh.ohio.gov or (614) 466-7713 and records the date, topic and response.
All policy and survey references use OAC Chapter 3701-16 and ORC Chapter 3721. The administrator corrects any reference to OAC Chapter 3701-17 found in forms or materials.

responsibilities.duty: Files initial, renewal and change-of-operator applications, pays fees and ensures solvency.
Maintains the license, posts it, tracks renewal and inspection dates, hosts surveys and submits plans of correction.
Cooperate with surveyors and refer all regulator contacts to the administrator or acting administrator.

documentation: Initial application packet with proof of filing date
CPA-signed solvency statement, certificate of occupancy, fire and heating reports
Fee payment records
Current license and posting log
Renewal calendar and renewal applications
ODH and fire inspection reports, statements of deficiencies and plans of correction
ODH correspondence log

policies.title: Policy Review and Document Control
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body and all staff
policies.purpose: To keep every policy current, version-controlled and traceable to the Ohio rule it implements, especially the policies that must be given to residents before admission.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] reviews every policy at least annually and whenever OAC Chapter 3701-16 or ORC Chapter 3721 changes. Policies given to residents before admission must be current. These are the resident rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR, disability accommodation and special care unit policies required by OAC 3701-16-07(F)-(H), together with the written resident agreement required by OAC 3701-16-07(D)-(E). Each is version-controlled so that the version a resident received is always identifiable. Staff sign an acknowledgment of each policy change. The annual calendar-year training on each resident right (OAC 3701-16-06(K)) uses the current rights policy. A citation index maps each policy to its OAC or ORC section.

definitions.definition: A system of numbering, dating and archiving policy versions so the version in effect on any date can be shown.
A table mapping each policy to the OAC/ORC section it implements.
The rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR, disability accommodation and special care unit policies that must be given and explained before admission.

procedures: The administrator keeps a master policy list showing each policy ID, title, version number, effective date, last review date, next review date and owner.
The administrator reviews every policy at least once every 12 months and records the review date, reviewer and outcome (no change or revised) on the master list.
The administrator checks the ODH website and the Ohio Revised and Administrative Codes at least quarterly for changes to ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16 and records the check.
When a rule changes, the administrator identifies affected policies through the citation index, revises them within [NUMBER] days of the rule's effective date and obtains governing body approval.
Each revised policy receives a new version number and effective date. The prior version is archived, not deleted, and kept at least 3 years.
The administrator keeps the citation index current. Each entry lists the policy ID and the exact OAC or ORC section, and entries are added or changed whenever a policy is revised.

Before any resident is admitted, the admissions staff member confirms that the resident-rights, smoking, advance directive/DNR, disability accommodation, special care unit and resident agreement documents in the admission packet are the current versions.
Each admission packet records the version numbers of the documents given. The resident's signed acknowledgment is filed in the record so the version the resident received can be proven.

When a pre-admission policy changes, the administrator gives current residents the revised policy and explains the change. Where the resident agreement is affected, the administrator follows RR-04, including 30 days' written notice of any rate change.
Within [NUMBER] days of any policy change, staff read the change and sign an acknowledgment. The administrator tracks completion and follows up with anyone outstanding.
The annual calendar-year training on each resident right is built from the current rights policy (RR-01). The training date, content version and attendance sign-in are recorded (see STF-03).
Obsolete forms are removed from the admission area and staff stations. The administrator verifies at each quarterly audit that no outdated version is in use (see GOV-04).
Current policies are kept in a binder or electronic folder that all staff can reach during every shift and that is available to surveyors on request.

responsibilities.duty: Approves new and revised policies.
Runs the annual review, monitors rule changes, maintains the master list and citation index, and ensures admission packets are current.
Use only current versions and record the versions given to each resident.
Read and acknowledge policy changes and follow current policy.

documentation: Master policy list with version and review dates
Citation index
Archived prior versions
Staff acknowledgment of policy changes
Admission packet version record and resident acknowledgments
Rule-change monitoring log

policies.title: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement
policies.applies_to: Governing body, administrator, designated infection preventionist and all department leads
policies.purpose: To monitor compliance with OAC Chapter 3701-16, find problems early, and correct them with documented follow-up.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] runs a quality assurance and performance improvement (QA/PI) program. A quarterly internal audit measures operations against OAC Chapter 3701-16, as a facility standard. ODH inspects at least every 15 months, so [AGENCY NAME] assumes every inspection is unannounced and may occur at any time. The program reviews three data streams for trends: the incident log kept under OAC 3701-16-12(B), the infection surveillance data required by OAC 3701-16-12(C)-(E), and the evaluations of fire and disaster drills required by OAC 3701-16-13(K)-(M). Problems found in drills are investigated and corrected, and the written drill evaluation is kept 3 years. The governing body reviews QA results and corrective actions at least quarterly.

definitions.definition: Quality Assurance and Performance Improvement: the planned, recurring review of facility performance and correction of problems.
The separate log of incidents recording time, place, date, description and action taken (OAC 3701-16-12(B)).
Ongoing tracking of resident and staff infections, as required under the facility's written infection prevention program (OAC 3701-16-12(C)-(E)).
A written plan with an owner, steps and due date to fix an identified problem.

procedures: The administrator builds a QA calendar with one internal audit each quarter and assigns a lead for each audit area (records, medications, staffing, environment, infection control, drills, resident rights).

Each quarter, the administrator or a designee audits the facility against a checklist drawn from OAC Chapter 3701-16 and the citation index (see GOV-03). The audit includes a walk-through of the building and a review of a sample of resident and personnel records.
The auditor documents each finding as compliant or not compliant, with the evidence reviewed, and opens a corrective action plan for each non-compliant finding.

The administrator reviews the incident log at least quarterly for patterns by type, resident, location, time of day and staff member. The review confirms that each entry has the time, place, date, description and action taken (OAC 3701-16-12(B)) and that each incident was investigated.

The administrator reviews significant changes in resident health status to confirm that immediate intervention, record entries, information to the treating party and notification of the sponsor were completed (OAC 3701-16-12(A); see HLT-04).

The designated infection preventionist presents quarterly infection surveillance data. The administrator confirms that the TB control plan, isolation, hand hygiene, laundry and legionella water management program are being followed and documented (see SAF-07).

The administrator reviews each fire and disaster drill record. The review checks that the required number of fire drills per year, staff participation, resident evacuation drills and disaster drills (including one tornado drill from March through July) were completed and recorded (see SAF-06).

When a drill reveals a problem, such as slow evacuation, missing staff or a blocked exit, the administrator investigates the cause, writes a corrective action and completes it. A repeat drill is held where needed to confirm the fix.
Written drill records and evaluations are kept for 3 years.
Each corrective action plan names a responsible person and a due date. The administrator verifies completion and records the date and the evidence.
The administrator also reviews grievances (RR-02), resident and family feedback, staff training completion and staffing levels as part of QA.

The administrator presents a written QA report to the governing body at least quarterly, covering audit results, trends, open and closed corrective actions and any regulator findings. The governing body's directions are recorded in the minutes.
QA findings are used to update policies and training (see GOV-03 and STF-03).
QA records are kept at least [NUMBER] years and are available to the governing body. They are not a substitute for any report required by regulation (see REC-02).

responsibilities.duty: Reviews QA results and corrective actions at least quarterly and provides resources to correct problems.
Schedules and leads audits, reviews the incident log and drill records, opens and closes corrective actions and reports to the governing body.
Collects and reports infection surveillance data and confirms infection control practices.
Assist with audits and complete assigned corrective actions on time.

documentation: QA calendar and quarterly audit checklists
Corrective action plans with completion evidence
Incident log review notes
Infection surveillance summaries
Fire and disaster drill records and evaluations (kept 3 years)
Quarterly QA report and governing body minutes

policies.title: Corporate Compliance, Fraud and Billing Integrity
policies.applies_to: Operator, administrator, billing staff and all staff who document services
policies.purpose: To make sure that [AGENCY NAME] bills the Assisted Living Waiver accurately, only for services actually delivered, and responds correctly to Medicaid enrollment and revalidation requirements.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] participates in the Ohio Assisted Living Waiver, a 1915(c) home and community-based services waiver administered by the Ohio Department of Aging (ODA) under an interagency agreement with the Ohio Department of Medicaid (ODM). Under OAC 5160-1-06.5 and OAC Chapter 5160-33, waiver residents must live in an ODH-licensed RCF and the facility must be a certified waiver provider. The waiver pays for services only, not room and board. [AGENCY NAME] bills only for services that were authorized, delivered and documented. It uses billing codes, unit definitions and rates provided by ODA/ODM, including Appendix A maximum rates, and never bills from unverified or secondhand rate information. This policy applies together with applicable federal Medicaid requirements (including 42 USC 1396b(l)). Staff may report suspected fraud, waste or billing errors without retaliation.

definitions.definition: Ohio's 1915(c) home and community-based services waiver that pays for assisted living services (not room and board) for eligible residents of ODH-licensed RCFs.
Billing for services not delivered, upcoding, falsifying records, billing for room and board under the waiver, or other practices that result in improper payment.
The periodic process by which ODM requires enrolled providers to confirm and update their enrollment information.
Electronic Visit Verification. Its application to Assisted Living Waiver claims is unconfirmed and must be confirmed in writing by ODA/ODM.

procedures: The operator designates a compliance officer, who may be the administrator, and records the designation. The compliance officer is the contact for billing questions and compliance concerns.

The compliance officer completes provider enrollment with ODM through the electronic enrollment system. Paper applications are not used. The organizational application fee of $750 is paid unless a waiver applies, in which case proof of a payment to Medicare or another state's Medicaid within the past 2 years is attached.
The administrator confirms with ODA that the facility holds current waiver provider certification before any waiver resident is accepted (see GOV-07).

Billing staff obtain the current billing codes, unit definitions and Appendix A maximum rates from ODA/ODM. Each source and its date is kept in a billing reference file. Rates are not taken from unverified sources.

The compliance officer obtains written confirmation from ODA/ODM on whether EVV applies to Assisted Living Waiver claims and files the response. If EVV applies, the facility implements it before billing.

Services are billed only if they are authorized in the resident's service plan, actually delivered, and documented by the staff member who provided them. Billing staff reconcile each claim to the documentation before submission.
The facility does not bill the waiver for room and board and does not charge residents for anything the waiver has paid. Charges follow the resident agreement (see RR-04).
The compliance officer reviews a sample of claims against the service plan and documentation at least quarterly, records errors and corrects and repays any overpayment promptly.

The compliance officer keeps ODM contact information current. When a revalidation notice arrives (ODM sends notices at least 90 days before the deadline), the officer calendars the deadline, completes the revalidation and keeps proof of submission.
New employees receive compliance training at hire and annually thereafter. It covers accurate documentation, prohibited billing practices, and how to report concerns. Attendance is recorded.

Staff may report concerns to the compliance officer or administrator, or, if the concern involves them, to the operator. Reports may be made anonymously at [PHONE]. No staff member is retaliated against for a good-faith report.
The compliance officer investigates each report within [NUMBER] business days, documents the findings and corrective action and reports substantiated issues to the governing body.
Before hire and monthly after, the facility screens staff against applicable exclusion databases (see STF-02). Excluded individuals are not employed or billed for.
Billing and compliance records are kept as long as required by ODM/ODA rules and the facility's retention schedule (see REC-01).

responsibilities.duty: Designates the compliance officer and receives compliance reports.
Manages ODM enrollment and revalidation, confirms EVV status, audits claims, investigates reports and arranges training.
Submit claims only from verified rates and documented, authorized services.
Document services accurately and truthfully and report suspected fraud or billing errors.

documentation: Compliance officer designation
ODM enrollment application, fee or waiver proof and revalidation records
ODA/ODM written responses on EVV and rate sources
Billing reference file with codes, units and Appendix A rates
Quarterly claim audit records and repayment records
Compliance training attendance
Compliance report and investigation files

policies.title: Closure, Change of Operator and Resident Relocation Plan
policies.applies_to: Operator, administrator, social services/resident care staff and all staff
policies.purpose: To protect residents if [AGENCY NAME] closes or is transferred to a new operator, by giving timely notice, planning safe relocation, and meeting ODH requirements.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 3701-16-03(M)(1)-(3) (closure notice to the ODH director). If [AGENCY NAME] plans to close, the operator gives written notice to the ODH director at least 90 days ahead where practicable, and never less than 60 days ahead. The notice states (1) an address where the operator can be reached, (2) a plan for the transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and (3) assurances that each resident will go to the most integrated and appropriate setting, considering the resident's needs, choice and best interests. If the facility is to be assigned or transferred to a new operator, a change-of-operator application with the non-refundable fee is filed at least 60 days before the proposed assignment or transfer (OAC 3701-16-03). Any resident discharge or transfer resulting from closure follows ORC 3721.16 and OAC Chapter 3701-61, including adequate preparation and a destination that can meet the resident's needs (ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33)). Residents keep the right to choose a licensed hospice (ORC 3721.13(A)(36)).

definitions.definition: Permanent cessation of operation of the RCF, in whole or in part, requiring relocation of residents.
Assignment or transfer of facility operation to a new operator, which requires a license application to ODH.
The setting that best meets the resident's needs while respecting the resident's choice and best interests, as stated in OAC 3701-16-03(M)(3).
The written plan for transferring each resident safely to a setting that can meet the resident's needs.

procedures: When the operator decides to close, the operator informs the administrator and governing body in writing and sets a target closure date at least 90 days away where practicable. A date less than 60 days from the notice is never used.

The administrator prepares the written closure notice to the ODH director. It includes (1) an address where the operator can be reached after closure, (2) the plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and (3) assurances that residents will move to the most integrated and appropriate setting considering their needs, choice and best interests.
The operator sends the notice to the ODH director at least 90 days ahead where practicable and no later than 60 days ahead, and retains proof of delivery.

The administrator builds the relocation plan with a list of every resident, current needs from the latest assessment and service plan (ADM-04, ADM-05), payer source, sponsor/representative and physician.

The administrator informs residents, sponsors and representatives in writing and in person. The notice follows ORC 3721.16 and OAC Chapter 3701-61. The administrator confirms the required notice period and content with ODH or counsel before sending, and does not rely on an unverified time period.
The administrator holds a resident and family meeting soon after notice. It explains the timeline, answers questions, describes options and tells residents how to reach the Ombudsman (RR-03).

Social services or care staff meet individually with each resident and sponsor to identify preferred settings. Options include other RCFs and, for waiver residents, other waiver settings and service options discussed with the Ohio Department of Aging and the resident's case manager.

Staff help each resident visit or learn about candidate settings. Placement honors the resident's choice and best interests. The resident's choice of a licensed hospice is respected for any resident receiving hospice (HLT-08).

Before any move, staff confirm that the destination can meet the resident's needs, and prepare the resident, including a pre-transfer discussion, packing and transport, with an adequate orientation to the new setting.

Staff send the receiving provider a transfer packet: current assessment and service plan, medication list and orders, physician contact, advance directive/DNR status, recent incident or change-of-condition notes and sponsor contact. Medications and personal property are returned or transferred under HLT-01 and RR-05.
The administrator refunds deposits and prepaid fees, and returns resident funds with a final accounting, as set out in the resident agreement (RR-04, RR-05).
The administrator tracks each resident's relocation on a closure log recording the date, destination, who accepted the transfer and any follow-up. The log is updated at least weekly.
The administrator keeps staffing and services at licensed levels until the last resident has been safely relocated. Staff are told the closure timeline so that care is not disrupted.

If the facility is to be sold or the operation transferred, the proposed new operator files a change-of-operator application and the non-refundable fee with ODH at least 60 days before the proposed assignment or transfer. Residents and sponsors are told in writing of the change and their rights remain unchanged (RR-01).
Resident records are retained after closure under REC-01. The operator names a custodian and gives the ODH notice address where records can be requested.
After the last resident has left, the administrator notifies ODH in writing and returns or surrenders the license as ODH directs.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on closure or transfer, signs and sends the notice to the ODH director, files the change-of-operator application and pays the fee.
Prepares the notice and relocation plan, leads resident meetings, oversees transfers and refunds and keeps the closure log.
Assist each resident and sponsor in choosing a setting and prepare transfer packets.
Approves the closure plan and monitors progress.

documentation: Written closure notice to ODH director with proof of delivery
Relocation plan and closure log
Resident and sponsor notices and meeting records
Transfer packets and receiving-provider confirmations
Refund and resident-funds final accounting
Change-of-operator application and fee payment record
Records custody designation

policies.title: Assisted Living Waiver Provider Participation and HCBS Settings Requirements
policies.applies_to: Administrator, governing body, admissions and billing staff, all direct care staff, and any resident enrolled in or applying for the Ohio Assisted Living Waiver
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] participates in the Assisted Living Waiver only when it holds the required licensure and certification, bills only as the program allows, and runs its setting so that waiver residents keep the rights and freedoms the federal home and community-based services (HCBS) settings rule requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health (ODH) as a residential care facility under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16. We will accept residents funded by the Assisted Living Waiver only while we also hold the Ohio Department of Aging (ODA) waiver provider certification and the Medicaid provider enrollment required by the Ohio Department of Medicaid (ODM). The waiver is administered by ODA under an interagency agreement with ODM, and we follow OAC 5160-1-06.5 and OAC Chapter 5160-33 (C54, C55). A waiver resident must live in an ODH-licensed RCF. The waiver pays for services only, not room and board, and our maximum waiver rates are those in Appendix A to OAC 5160-1-06.5. We use the three-tier unit rate model. We will not claim a memory care tier or critical access status until ODA has confirmed in writing that we meet the criteria. Waiver residents receive the same rights, care and dignity as every other resident. In line with 42 CFR 441.301(c), we honor each waiver resident's choice, privacy, dignity, freedom from coercion, and control of their own schedule and visitors. We keep a written first-come waiver waitlist and verify slot availability with ODA before offering a placement. Any limit on a resident's HCBS setting rights must be justified, documented in the resident's service plan with informed consent, and allowed by the federal rule. A limit may never be imposed for staff convenience.

definitions.definition: Ohio's 1915(c) HCBS waiver that pays for assisted living services for eligible Medicaid residents living in an ODH-licensed residential care facility. It does not pay for room and board.
Federal requirements in 42 CFR 441.301(c) that a home and community-based setting protect the resident's choice, privacy, dignity, freedom from coercion, and control over daily schedule and visitors.
The Assisted Living Waiver payment structure under OAC Chapter 5160-33 that sets a unit rate by service tier. Maximum rates are in Appendix A to OAC 5160-1-06.5.
The person designated through the waiver program who coordinates the resident's waiver eligibility and service plan with the facility.

procedures: The Administrator confirms before any waiver admission that the ODH license is current (see GOV-02) and records the license number and expiration date in the waiver participation file.

The Administrator confirms the facility holds ODA waiver provider certification and an active ODM Medicaid provider enrollment, including any enrollment fee and revalidation due dates. The Administrator files the confirmations and diaries every renewal and revalidation date.

The Administrator requests written confirmation from ODA of the service tier(s) for which [AGENCY NAME] is certified, including whether memory care tier certification and critical access criteria apply to us. Staff do not describe the facility as offering these in marketing or agreements until the written confirmation is on file.

The Administrator keeps current copies of OAC 5160-1-06.5 and OAC Chapter 5160-33 in the waiver file. The Administrator reviews them at least annually and whenever ODA or ODM issues a notice of change, and records the review date.

Billing staff check every waiver rate against Appendix A to OAC 5160-1-06.5 before billing. The facility never bills a waiver resident or the program above the maximum rate. See GOV-05 for billing integrity.

The Admissions Coordinator maintains a written waiver waitlist in first-come order. Each entry shows the date and time of the request, the person's name, and the contact person. Entries are not reordered except to follow a written ODA instruction, which is filed with the list.

When a waiver-eligible bed opens, the Admissions Coordinator contacts ODA or the resident's waiver case manager to verify slot availability before offering the unit. The Coordinator offers the unit to the next person on the list who is eligible and appropriate under ADM-01, and records the verification.

The Admissions Coordinator completes the standard pre-admission screening (ADM-01) for waiver applicants. Payer source is not a basis for refusing a resident who otherwise meets admission criteria, except where unit availability is limited as described above.

The admission agreement for each waiver resident states that the waiver pays for services only, identifies what the resident owes for room and board and any non-covered items, and explains who is responsible for each payment (see RR-04). The Administrator reviews each such agreement before signing.

The Administrator trains all staff at orientation and annually on HCBS setting requirements. The training covers the resident's right to choose, to have privacy, to be treated with dignity, to be free from coercion, to set their own schedule (waking, meals within available options, activities, outings), and to receive visitors. Attendance is recorded under STF-03.

Staff may not enforce facility-wide rules that restrict a waiver resident's schedule, visitors or privacy beyond what applies to all residents for safety. Visiting hours are not restricted for waiver residents except where the resident has agreed to a documented limit.

If a resident's safety needs call for an individual limit on any HCBS setting right, the Director of Nursing or designee documents the specific assessed need, the less restrictive options tried, the proposed limit, a review schedule, and the resident's or representative's informed written consent. This is recorded in the service plan (ADM-05). The Administrator approves it before it takes effect, and it is reviewed at every reassessment. Restraints are governed separately by SAF-04.

The Administrator cooperates with the waiver case manager's visits and reviews and with ODA and ODM monitoring. Records requested by these agencies are provided within the time stated in the request, subject to RR-07.

The Administrator notifies ODA and the resident's waiver case manager promptly of events that affect waiver services. These include a significant change in condition (HLT-04), a planned discharge or transfer (ADM-07), a death (HLT-09), a loss or suspension of license or certification, and any closure or change of operator (GOV-06).

The Quality Assurance committee reviews waiver participation at least quarterly (GOV-04). It looks at the waitlist, waiver complaints, HCBS setting concerns, and billing audit results, and records corrective actions.

The Administrator reports to the governing body at least annually on waiver status, including certification, enrollment, tier status, and any ODA or ODM findings, and documents the governing body's response.

responsibilities.duty: Authorizes waiver participation, ensures resources to meet waiver requirements, and reviews the Administrator's annual waiver report.
Maintains licensure, ODA certification and ODM enrollment; obtains written tier confirmation from ODA; oversees waitlist, HCBS compliance and agency communication.
Keeps the waitlist, verifies slot availability with ODA, and completes screening and agreements for waiver applicants.
Bills only within Appendix A maximum rates and only for services delivered and documented.
Documents any individually justified limit on a setting right in the service plan, with consent, and reviews it at reassessment.
Honor each waiver resident's choice, privacy, dignity, schedule and visitors, and report concerns to the Administrator.

documentation: Waiver participation file: ODH license, ODA certification, ODM enrollment and revalidation dates
Written ODA confirmation of tier, memory care tier and critical access status
Copies of OAC 5160-1-06.5 and OAC Chapter 5160-33 with annual review log
Waiver waitlist with dated entries and slot-availability verification notes
Waiver resident admission agreements and payer responsibility statements
HCBS settings training attendance records
Individual limit documentation and consent, filed in the service plan
QA committee minutes and annual governing body waiver report

policies.title: Resident Rights and Responsibilities
policies.applies_to: All residents and their sponsors and representatives; Administrator and all staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident knows, understands and can exercise the rights guaranteed by ORC 3721.13, and that staff are trained to respect them.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 3701-16-07(F)(1): Policy to give residents before admission: the residents' rights policy and procedures required by ORC 3721.12. [AGENCY NAME] gives each prospective resident, and the sponsor where applicable, the written residents' rights policy and procedures before admission and explains them (C23). The rights are those in ORC 3721.13(A) (C46, C47, C48, C49). They include freedom from abuse, informed consent, privacy, confidentiality of records, freedom from restraint except by physician order (with a 12-hour limit for emergencies), choice of physician and pharmacist, unrestricted communication, and civil and religious rights. They also include written notice of charges, 30 days' notice of a rate change, an itemized monthly bill, freedom from financial exploitation, notice before a room or roommate change, discharge only for the reasons the law lists, and the right to choose a licensed hospice. Residents may voice grievances without reprisal, and we make a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of a significant change in health within 12 hours. A waiver of these rights is void under ORC 3721.13(C), and no admission agreement or risk agreement may waive them. Staff receive annual calendar-year training on each right under ORC 3721.13(A) and on comparable service for residents with similar needs (C19). Waiver residents receive the same rights, and we also honor the HCBS setting protections in 42 CFR 441.301(c) (see GOV-07). Residents also have responsibilities, which are explained in the same packet and which do not limit their rights.

definitions.definition: An adult, such as a relative, friend or legal representative, who has an interest in or responsibility for the resident's welfare and who acts for the resident when the resident cannot.
The resident's agreement to care or treatment after receiving an understandable explanation of its nature, benefits, risks and alternatives.
A person or organization, including the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman program, that helps residents exercise their rights.

procedures: The Admissions Coordinator gives the written residents' rights policy and procedures required by ORC 3721.12, along with the list of rights in ORC 3721.13(A), to the prospective resident and sponsor before admission (OAC 3701-16-07(F)(1)). This is done as part of the disclosure packet in ADM-02.

The Admissions Coordinator or Administrator reads and explains the rights in plain language, in the resident's preferred language and format as required by RR-08. The resident is given time and an opportunity to ask questions.

The resident, or the sponsor if the resident cannot understand, signs and dates an acknowledgment that the policy was received and explained. A copy goes to the resident and the original to the resident record (REC-01). Signing is not a waiver of any right.

Staff will not ask any resident to sign any document that waives a right under ORC 3721.13. The Administrator reviews every admission and risk agreement (ADM-03) for such language before use, and any such language is void and removed.
The Administrator posts the residents' rights summary and the grievance procedure where residents and visitors can see them, with the ODH and ombudsman contact information (RR-02, RR-03).

Staff obtain informed consent before care and treatment and respect the resident's refusal. The nurse documents consent and refusals in the record, and the resident's physician is notified of refusals that affect health (HLT-04).

Staff protect privacy during personal care, in treatment, in communications and in bedrooms. They knock and wait for permission before entering resident rooms except in an emergency. Records and information are kept confidential under RR-07.

Residents may choose their own physician and pharmacist, as well as a licensed hospice. Staff provide the list of options and do not steer residents to particular providers. Any pharmacy-related limits are explained before admission (HLT-01, HLT-08).
Staff do not restrict or monitor residents' mail, phone, visitors or outside communication. Restraints are used only as set out in SAF-04.

The Administrator or the Director of Nursing notifies the sponsor with reasonable effort within 12 hours of a significant change in the resident's health, and documents the attempt, time and result (HLT-04).
Charges, rate changes, itemized monthly bills, room and roommate changes, and discharges follow RR-04, RR-05 and ADM-07, including the required notices.

Staff report any suspected violation of rights to the Administrator immediately. Suspected abuse, neglect or exploitation is reported under SAF-01. Retaliation against any resident or staff member who raises a rights concern is prohibited.

The Administrator provides rights training to all new staff during orientation and to all staff every calendar year. Training covers each right under ORC 3721.13(A) and comparable service for residents with similar needs. Additional training is given when a need is identified (OAC 3701-16-06(M)). Attendance sheets are kept under STF-03.
The Administrator checks that professionals the facility uses hold current Ohio licenses where required (OAC 3701-16-06(J)) and keeps the verification in the personnel or contractor file.
The Administrator reviews rights complaints and incidents quarterly through the QA program (GOV-04) and records corrective actions.

The resident's responsibilities are explained in the admission packet: to follow the written house rules that apply to all residents, to pay charges as agreed, to treat others with respect, to share relevant health information, and to give notice of changes as the agreement states. Failure to meet a responsibility does not remove any right.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures the rights policy is given and explained before admission, trains staff annually, and corrects rights violations.
Delivers and explains the rights policy and obtains the signed acknowledgment.
Obtains informed consent, notifies the sponsor within 12 hours of significant health changes, and documents refusals.
Respect each right, complete annual training, and report suspected violations immediately.
Review the rights policy, ask questions, and raise concerns without fear of reprisal.

documentation: Residents' rights policy and procedures (ORC 3721.12) and signed acknowledgment of receipt and explanation
Informed consent and refusal entries in the resident record
Sponsor notification log showing time and result
Annual rights training curriculum and attendance records
Professional license verifications
Rights complaint and corrective action records

policies.title: Grievances and Complaints
policies.applies_to: All residents, sponsors, families and staff; Administrator
policies.purpose: To give residents a clear, safe way to voice grievances, to make sure each is investigated and answered in writing, and to protect residents from reprisal.
policies.policy: Residents have the right under ORC 3721.13(A) to voice grievances to staff, to the Ohio Department of Health (ODH), or to any other person of their choice, without reprisal, and to have access to a residents' rights advocate (C49, C46). [AGENCY NAME] welcomes grievances. We will not discourage, delay, screen or punish any complaint made to us or to an outside party. Each grievance made to us is logged, investigated promptly by someone not involved in the matter where possible, and answered in writing. A resident or sponsor may go to ODH, the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman, ODA or the waiver case manager at any time, whether or not they have first used our procedure. Retaliation in any form is prohibited and is itself a violation of residents' rights. This policy applies equally to residents funded by the Assisted Living Waiver (42 CFR 441.301(c)).

definitions.definition: Any complaint or concern, oral or written, about care, treatment, staff, other residents, charges, the environment or the facility's policies.
Any adverse action or threat taken because a person raised a grievance, including a change in staff attitude or care, room change, discharge threat, or reduced privileges.
A person or program, including the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman, that helps residents understand and exercise their rights.

procedures: At admission, and annually, staff explain the grievance procedure to each resident and sponsor in plain language and in the resident's preferred language (RR-08). It is included in the disclosure packet (ADM-02).

The Administrator posts the grievance procedure in a place residents can see it, along with the ODH complaint hotline number [ODH COMPLAINT HOTLINE NUMBER] and the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman number [OMBUDSMAN PHONE NUMBER]. The Administrator verifies these numbers against ODH and ombudsman publications before posting and re-verifies them at least annually.
The posting also lists how to reach the Administrator, [ADMINISTRATOR NAME], at [PHONE], and says that residents may complain to anyone they choose, with no need to go through the facility first.

Any staff member who receives a grievance, oral or written, listens respectfully and records it on the Grievance Form the same day. The staff member gives it to the Administrator or designee by the end of the next business day. Residents may submit grievances anonymously.
Staff help any resident who needs assistance to write, voice or send a complaint, and provide privacy and, on request, access to a residents' rights advocate.
The Administrator or designee enters each grievance in the grievance log with the date, complainant, summary, persons involved, and assigned investigator.
The Administrator acknowledges the grievance to the resident or sponsor within two business days.
The investigator interviews the resident, staff and witnesses, reviews relevant records, and writes findings. The investigator may not be a person named in the grievance.
If a grievance alleges abuse, neglect, exploitation or misappropriation, the Administrator begins SAF-01 reporting immediately and does not wait to complete the grievance process.
If the grievance involves a possible medical or safety risk, the Director of Nursing assesses the resident the same day and takes protective steps. Physician and sponsor notification follow HLT-04.

The Administrator gives the resident or sponsor a written response within [GRIEVANCE RESPONSE DAYS] days of receiving the grievance. It states the findings, any action taken, and the right to take the concern to ODH, the ombudsman or another person of their choice, with contact information.
If the resident is not satisfied, the Administrator offers to meet and, on request, to include an advocate or ombudsman representative. The resident's outside rights remain regardless of the outcome.
The Administrator checks for reprisal 30 days after each grievance closes by speaking to the resident and reviewing the resident's care, room, and discharge status. Findings are logged.
Any staff member found to have retaliated is subject to discipline up to termination under STF-06.
The Administrator reviews the grievance log quarterly with the QA committee for trends and corrective action (GOV-04), and keeps grievance files for the period required by REC-01.

If ODH or another agency contacts the facility about a complaint, the Administrator cooperates fully, provides requested records subject to RR-07, and does not seek to learn or act on the identity of the complainant in any adverse way.

responsibilities.duty: Owns the grievance process, ensures investigation and written response, prevents reprisal, and reports trends to QA.
Conducts a fair, prompt investigation and documents findings.
Assesses any resident at risk and coordinates care and notifications.
Accept and record every grievance, help residents voice concerns, and never retaliate.

documentation: Grievance Form and grievance log
Investigation notes and findings
Written response to the resident or sponsor
Post-grievance reprisal check record
Posting verification record for ODH and ombudsman numbers
QA committee review of grievance trends

policies.title: Ombudsman Access
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator and all staff; ombudsman representatives
policies.purpose: To protect each resident's right to communicate freely with a residents' rights advocate or ombudsman, and to give ombudsman representatives access to residents and, with consent, to records.
