policies.policy: Under ORC 3721.13(A), residents may communicate without restriction with a residents' rights advocate or ombudsman and may voice grievances to persons of their choice without reprisal (C49, C46). [AGENCY NAME] will not interfere with, screen, delay, monitor or discourage any such contact, and will not retaliate against a resident or staff member for it. We post current ombudsman contact information where residents can see it, and we allow ombudsman representatives access to residents. Access to resident records is allowed with the resident's or authorized representative's consent. Waiver of these rights is void.

definitions.definition: A representative of the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman program who advocates for residents of long-term care facilities, including residential care facilities.
A person legally authorized to act for the resident in consenting to the release of records, such as a guardian or an agent under a valid power of attorney.

procedures: The Administrator posts the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman name and phone number [OMBUDSMAN PHONE NUMBER] and the regional ombudsman contact [REGIONAL OMBUDSMAN CONTACT] where residents, families and visitors can see them. The Administrator verifies the numbers against the current published information before posting and at least annually afterward.

Staff explain the ombudsman's role to each resident and sponsor at admission and give them the contact information in the disclosure packet (ADM-02). The explanation is repeated in resident council meetings or at least annually.

Staff help any resident who asks to contact the ombudsman by providing a private phone, a place for a private visit, or help writing or mailing a letter. Staff do not ask why the resident wants to call or what was said.
Outgoing and incoming mail, calls and messages to and from the ombudsman are never opened, read, screened, delayed or logged by staff.

When an ombudsman representative arrives, staff admit the person promptly and escort them to the Administrator or the person in charge. Staff verify identification by asking for the representative's badge or credentials, but do not require an appointment or advance notice.

The ombudsman representative may meet with any resident in private, with the resident's agreement. Staff do not sit in on the meeting and do not question the resident or ombudsman afterward about its content.

The ombudsman may review a resident's record only with the resident's consent or that of the authorized representative, or as otherwise provided by law. Staff confirm and document the consent, and provide the record promptly. See RR-07 for the privacy rules.

Where a resident cannot give consent and has no authorized representative, the Administrator consults the ombudsman about the legal basis for access before releasing any records, and documents the decision.
The Administrator gives the ombudsman representative a reasonable place to work and the opportunity to speak to residents who want to meet, including at resident council meetings.
The Administrator cooperates with ombudsman complaint investigations, responds to inquiries promptly and in writing when asked, and does not discourage residents from taking part.
Staff report any attempt by another employee to interfere with ombudsman access to the Administrator at once. Interference or retaliation is a serious violation and leads to discipline under STF-06.

The Administrator reviews ombudsman contacts and findings at the quarterly QA meeting (GOV-04), maintaining a log of visits and any follow-up actions, without recording what individual residents said in confidence.

responsibilities.duty: Posts and verifies ombudsman information, ensures access for residents and ombudsman representatives, and prevents interference or reprisal.
Confirms consent and arranges record access with the resident record staff.
Help residents reach the ombudsman, admit ombudsman representatives, and never screen or discourage contact.

documentation: Posting verification record with date of last check of ombudsman numbers
Consent for ombudsman access to records, in the resident record
Ombudsman visit log (date, representative, follow-up requested)
Acknowledgment of ombudsman information in the disclosure packet
QA committee minutes noting ombudsman activity

policies.title: Admission Agreement, Fees, Deposits and Refunds
policies.applies_to: Prospective residents, residents, sponsors; Administrator, admissions and business office staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident or sponsor receives, understands and signs a complete written agreement before residency begins, with charges, refunds, services and skilled nursing limits stated clearly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will not allow anyone to move in until a written resident agreement has been signed and dated by the resident (or sponsor if the resident cannot understand it) and by the facility. We give them a copy and explain it (C22). The agreement meets OAC 3701-16-07(E) as follows. E(1) — Agreement section on charges: explains all charges to the resident, including security deposits if applicable. E(2) — states that all charges, fines or penalties assessed against the resident are included in the agreement. E(3) — states that the basic rate will not change without 30 days' written notice to the resident or, if the resident cannot understand it, to the sponsor. E(4) — explains the policy for refunding charges on absence, discharge or transfer, and the policy for refunding security deposits. E(5) — explains the services offered, the types of skilled nursing care we provide or allow, the authorized providers, and the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care. E(6) — explains the extent and types of services we will provide and who is responsible for payment. E(7) — states that we must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified under E(5). We also follow ORC 3721.13(A)(25)-(29): written notice of basic and extra charges, 30 days' notice of a rate change, an itemized monthly bill, and notice before a room or roommate change (C47). The skilled nursing limits stated in the agreement reflect OAC 3701-16-09.1: part-time intermittent skilled nursing may last no more than 120 days in a 12-month period, and any longer period requires a written agreement with the resident and physician with re-determination at least every 30 days (every 15 days for hospice) (C32). The agreement may not waive any right under ORC 3721.13 (see RR-01).

definitions.definition: The regular periodic charge for room, board and the services included for all residents, as stated in the agreement.
Charges for services or items not included in the basic rate, listed in the agreement or fee schedule.
Money held by the facility at admission as security, which must be accounted for and refunded under the policy in the agreement.
Skilled nursing care that is not continuous, which for an RCF is limited to 120 days per 12 months unless an extended-care agreement is in place.
An adult with an interest in the resident's welfare who acts for the resident if the resident cannot understand the agreement or notices.

procedures: The Admissions Coordinator prepares the resident agreement on the facility's approved form. The Administrator reviews the form at least annually and whenever rates, services or the law change (see GOV-03), so that it contains each element described under E(1) through E(7).

E(1) — The agreement lists every charge: the basic rate, what it includes, each extra charge and its price, and any security deposit with its amount. The Admissions Coordinator explains each item to the resident and sponsor line by line.

E(2) — The agreement states that all charges, fines or penalties assessed against the resident are included in the agreement. No charge, fine or penalty not listed may be billed. The Administrator approves any new charge before it is added, and 30 days' written notice is given before it applies.

E(3) — The agreement states that the basic rate will not change without 30 days' written notice to the resident or, if the resident cannot understand it, to the sponsor. The Administrator issues each rate-change notice in writing with the effective date, delivers it by hand with a signed receipt or by a documented method, and keeps a copy in the resident record.

E(4) — The agreement explains the refund policy for absence, discharge or transfer, including how the amount is calculated, the date by which a refund will be paid [REFUND TIMEFRAME], and how it is paid. It also explains the security deposit refund policy, including any lawful deductions and the itemized statement given with the refund.

E(5) — The agreement explains the services offered, the types of skilled nursing care the facility provides or allows, the authorized providers (for example, a home health agency or hospice the resident chooses), and the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care. It states the 120-days-per-12-months limit on part-time intermittent skilled nursing and the written extended-care agreement and 30-day (hospice 15-day) re-determination that apply beyond that limit. The Director of Nursing confirms that the nursing section matches HLT-03.

E(6) — The agreement explains the extent and types of services the facility will provide and who is responsible for payment: the resident, a sponsor, an insurer, hospice, home health, or, for a waiver resident, the Assisted Living Waiver for services only (not room and board). See GOV-07.

E(7) — The agreement states that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified under E(5). The Admissions Coordinator explains this and the notice and planning steps in ADM-06 and ADM-07.

Before residency begins, the Admissions Coordinator gives the resident and sponsor the complete agreement, with the disclosure packet (ADM-02), and explains it in plain language and in the resident's preferred language (RR-08). The resident or sponsor is given time to ask questions and to consult family or counsel.

The resident, or the sponsor if the resident cannot understand, signs and dates the agreement, and the Administrator signs for the facility. No move-in occurs and no charges begin until the agreement is fully signed. Any rights waiver language is void and is not used.

The Admissions Coordinator gives a complete copy of the signed agreement to the resident or sponsor, and records the date and manner of delivery on the agreement. The original is placed in the resident record (REC-01).

The business office issues an itemized bill each month listing the basic rate and each extra charge. A copy is kept in the resident record. Billing questions are referred to the Administrator and handled under RR-02 if the resident wishes to file a grievance.

Security deposits are held and recorded as required by RR-05 and refunded under the stated policy. The business office issues the refund and the itemized statement by the stated deadline and keeps a copy.
The Administrator gives written notice before any room or roommate change, as required by ORC 3721.13(A)(25)-(29), and obtains the resident's views before the change except in an emergency.

When a resident's care needs approach the stated skilled nursing limits, the Director of Nursing notifies the Administrator, who reviews the agreement with the resident and sponsor and starts any extended-care agreement or planning for discharge under ADM-06 and ADM-07.
Any change to the agreement during residency, other than the 30-day rate notice, is made in writing, signed by the same parties, and copied to the resident.

responsibilities.duty: Approves the agreement form and every charge, signs agreements, issues rate-change notices, and ensures no admission without a signed agreement.
Explains and obtains signatures on the agreement, delivers the copy, and records delivery.
Prepares itemized monthly bills, handles deposits and refunds, and bills only charges stated in the agreement.
Confirms the skilled nursing section and limits are accurate and monitors residents approaching the limits.
Reads the agreement, asks questions, and signs before residency begins.

documentation: Signed and dated resident agreement with record of delivery of a copy and explanation
Fee schedule and extra-charge list
30-day rate-change notices with proof of delivery
Itemized monthly bills
Security deposit receipt, refund statement and refund record
Room or roommate change notices
Extended-care agreements and re-determination records where applicable

policies.title: Resident Funds and Personal Property
policies.applies_to: All residents and sponsors; Administrator, business office staff and all staff who handle resident funds or property
policies.purpose: To protect residents from financial exploitation by safeguarding any funds and property the facility holds or manages, and by prohibiting coercion and conflicts of interest.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will never coerce or pressure a resident to assign assets to the facility or its staff (C36). We manage a resident's funds only with the resident's witnessed written authorization. Resident funds over $1,000 are kept in a separate interest-bearing account, covered by a surety bond, and a final accounting is given when the funds end. If funds are delegated to us, we provide a quarterly accounting. Each resident receives an itemized monthly bill and remains free from financial exploitation, and keeps access to property deposited with us (C47). No staff member may serve as a resident's guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related to the resident by blood or marriage. Staff may not accept gifts, loans, or bequests, or borrow or buy from residents. Residents' personal property is protected, inventoried on request, and returned when they leave.

definitions.definition: Money belonging to a resident that the facility holds, safeguards or manages at the resident's written request.

A signed and dated statement by the resident or the person legally authorized to act for the resident allowing the facility to manage funds, signed by a witness who is not the person receiving the funds.
A bond purchased by the facility that protects residents' funds against loss or misuse.
A person who holds a power of attorney to act for the resident in legal or financial matters.

procedures: Staff do not ask, require or suggest that any resident assign, give or leave any asset to the facility, its owners or staff. No admission, service or continued stay depends on such an assignment. Any report of such pressure goes to the Administrator at once and is investigated under SAF-01.

A resident who wants the facility to hold or manage funds must sign a written authorization naming the funds and the services requested. A witness who is not the staff member managing the funds also signs and dates it. Residents may withdraw the authorization at any time.

Before accepting funds, the Administrator or business office manager explains to the resident how funds are held, how withdrawals are made, how often an accounting is given, and the resident's right to access funds. This is documented.

The business office keeps an individual ledger for each resident, recording every deposit and withdrawal with date, amount, purpose, the resident's signature or authorization and the staff member's initials. Residents' funds are never combined with the facility's operating funds or used for facility expenses.

Where a resident's funds exceed $1,000, the business office places them in a separate interest-bearing account in the resident's name or in a trust account identifying the resident. Interest earned belongs to the resident and is credited on the ledger.

The Administrator obtains and maintains a surety bond covering the amount of resident funds held and keeps the bond and renewal dates in the business file. The Administrator reviews coverage each time total resident funds change significantly and at least annually.

The business office gives each resident, or the sponsor, an itemized monthly bill and a written accounting of funds held at least quarterly, as ORC 3721.13(A)(25)-(29) requires for delegated funds. The resident or sponsor signs a receipt, or the delivery method is documented.

Residents or authorized representatives may withdraw funds on request during normal business hours. Staff provide the funds within [FUNDS ACCESS TIMEFRAME] and record the withdrawal on the ledger with the resident's signature.

Staff do not borrow from, lend to, buy from, sell to, or accept gifts or gratuities, or any benefit from a resident. Staff may not witness a resident's will or financial document in which they have an interest. Violations are reported to the Administrator and result in discipline under STF-06.

No employee may serve as a resident's guardian or attorney-in-fact unless the employee is related to the resident. The Administrator checks each new authorization or power of attorney on file for this conflict and addresses any conflict in writing with the resident and sponsor.

When a resident's funds were deposited or delegated to us, a final accounting is prepared when the resident is discharged, transferred or dies. The business office delivers the accounting and any remaining funds to the resident, or to the resident's legal representative or estate, within [FINAL ACCOUNTING TIMEFRAME], and obtains a signed receipt.

Residents may keep personal property, and valuables may be deposited with the facility. Staff record each deposit on a signed receipt, store the items in a locked area, and return them on request. Residents keep access to their deposited property. Staff do not enter a resident's belongings without the resident's permission except in an emergency or as the resident has agreed.

At admission, staff prepare a list of the resident's belongings at the resident's request, and update it with additions and removals. The resident or sponsor signs the list. On discharge or death, staff inventory the property with the resident or representative present or confirming, and release it with a signed receipt.

The Administrator reconciles each resident's ledger against bank records monthly, signs the reconciliation, and has a person other than the one who keeps the ledger review it quarterly. Discrepancies are investigated at once and, if exploitation is suspected, reported under SAF-01 and REC-02.

Missing property or funds reported by a resident are recorded as incidents (SAF-02), searched for promptly, investigated, and reported to law enforcement or the proper agency where theft is suspected. The resident and sponsor receive a written outcome.
The Administrator reviews funds and property handling during the annual QA review (GOV-04) and annual audit under GOV-05.

responsibilities.duty: Approves all fund management, keeps the surety bond, prohibits coercion and conflicts of interest, and reviews reconciliations.
Maintains separate accounts and ledgers, produces monthly bills and quarterly accountings, and handles withdrawals and final accounting.
Observes the resident's signing of the authorization and signs it; may not be the person who will manage the funds.
Do not take or ask for resident assets, gifts or loans; safeguard property; report any suspected exploitation or loss.
Decide whether the facility manages funds, review accountings, and raise any concern.

documentation: Witnessed written authorization for each resident whose funds are managed
Resident fund ledger and receipts
Separate interest-bearing account statements for funds over $1,000
Surety bond and renewal records
Quarterly accounting and itemized monthly bills with receipts
Final accounting and receipt on discharge, transfer or death
Personal property inventory and deposit receipts
Monthly reconciliations and reviewer signatures
Staff conflict-of-interest and gift reports

policies.title: Advance Directives
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admissions staff, nursing and personal care staff, medication-authorized staff, all employees who may find a resident in an emergency
policies.purpose: To make sure every prospective resident is told, before admission, how [AGENCY NAME] handles advance directives and Do Not Resuscitate (DNR) orders and what rights the resident has under Ohio law. The policy also keeps these documents from being used as a condition of admission and makes sure valid directives on file are honored.
policies.policy:
This policy meets OAC 3701-16-07(F)(3) (Policy to give residents before admission: policies on advance directives and DNR orders, with an explanation of the resident's rights under state law; an advance directive or DNR order cannot be required as a condition of admission).

[AGENCY NAME] gives each prospective resident or sponsor this Advance Directive and DNR Policy, with a plain-language explanation of the resident's rights under Ohio law, before admission. The policy is part of the Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet (ADM-02). Staff explain it and answer questions, and the resident or sponsor signs an acknowledgment.

The facility will never require a resident to have, sign, complete, change or revoke an advance directive or DNR order as a condition of admission or continued residence. Residents have the right to make their own health care decisions, including the right to accept or refuse treatment, and rights under ORC 3721.13(A) (informed consent and participation in care decisions) cannot be waived (ORC 3721.13(C)). A copy of any advance directive or DNR order the resident provides is placed in the resident record and honored under the procedures below. The facility does not give legal advice and does not draft or witness advance directive documents for residents. It refers residents to their physician or an attorney of their choice.

The staff emergency-response procedure in this policy is to be reviewed and confirmed by [LEGAL COUNSEL NAME] before the facility opens and whenever Ohio law on directives or DNR orders changes. Statutory references for the DNR and directive process are to be supplied by counsel and are not stated in this manual.

definitions.definition: A written document, such as a living will or health care power of attorney, in which a resident states health care wishes or names someone to make health care decisions if the resident cannot.
A physician's order, in the form recognized under Ohio law, directing that resuscitation not be attempted if the resident's heart or breathing stops.
A person or entity who assists or acts for the resident in dealing with the facility, such as a family member, guardian or authorized representative.
A person who has applied for admission and has not yet moved in.

procedures: Before admission, and before the admission agreement is signed, the Admissions Coordinator gives the prospective resident or sponsor a written copy of the Advance Directive and DNR Policy as part of the disclosure packet (ADM-02).

The Admissions Coordinator explains the policy aloud in plain language, including: the resident's right to make health care decisions under Ohio law; the right to accept or refuse treatment; the right to make, change or revoke a directive or DNR at any time; and that no directive or DNR is required for admission.
The Admissions Coordinator uses interpreter or translated materials when needed (RR-08) and offers a reader or other accommodation for residents with sensory or cognitive disabilities.

The Admissions Coordinator asks, without pressure, whether the resident already has an advance directive or DNR order, and records the answer on the Advance Directive Status Form [FORM NAME]. A resident who declines to answer or has no directive is documented as such, with no effect on admission.

The resident or sponsor signs the acknowledgment that the policy was received and explained. A resident who declines to sign is documented with the date, the staff member's name and the reason given if any, and admission is not delayed or denied for that reason.

If the resident has a directive or DNR order, the Admissions Coordinator obtains a copy no later than the day of admission and places it in the resident record in the section labeled 'Advance Directives', and flags it on the face sheet and the emergency information sheet.

The Administrator or designee verifies that any DNR order appears valid on its face (signed, dated, and issued in the form recognized under Ohio law) and, if there is a question, contacts the resident's physician and [LEGAL COUNSEL NAME] for guidance.

The Administrator or designee records the order, the date the copy was received and the name of the physician or agent in the service plan (ADM-05), and asks the resident's physician to confirm the order's current status when the resident moves in.
The Administrator trains all staff on this policy at orientation and at least annually (STF-03), including how to find a resident's directive or DNR status quickly and how to respond in an emergency.

When a resident is found unresponsive or not breathing, the first staff person present immediately checks the emergency information sheet or record for a directive or DNR, summons help, and calls 911 without delay. Staff then follow the written Emergency Response Procedure [EMERGENCY RESPONSE PROCEDURE ID] approved by counsel. Staff do not ignore, override or interpret a valid order beyond that procedure.
The Administrator or designee notifies the physician and the resident's sponsor or agent of the event as soon as possible, and documents it as an incident (SAF-02).

The Nurse or Administrator reviews each resident's directive status at admission, at every reassessment (ADM-04), after any hospitalization and after any significant change of condition (HLT-04), and asks whether the resident wants to review or change it.

If a resident or agent revokes or changes a directive or DNR order, the staff member who receives the request notifies the Administrator the same day, obtains the written update or physician order, replaces the copy in the record, and updates the emergency information sheet and service plan.

When a resident is transferred to a hospital or other provider, staff send a copy of the directive or DNR with the transfer paperwork and ensure the receiving provider is told it exists (HLT-04, ADM-07).

Staff never ask a resident, family member or sponsor to sign or remove a directive in exchange for admission, retention, a room assignment or services. Any such report is investigated by the Administrator under the grievance policy (RR-02).
The Administrator audits a sample of resident records quarterly to confirm acknowledgments, copies of directives and flags are complete, and reports results to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures this policy is implemented, staff are trained, counsel confirms the emergency response procedure, and audits are completed.
Provides and explains the policy before admission, obtains the signed acknowledgment and files copies of directives.
Verifies orders with physicians, updates the service plan, and reviews status at reassessment and change of condition.
Know how to locate directive status and follow the emergency response procedure.
Confirms the staff response procedure and the Ohio legal references used in resident materials.

documentation: Signed acknowledgment of receipt and explanation of the policy (kept in the admission record)
Advance Directive Status Form [FORM NAME]
Copy of advance directive or DNR order in the resident record
Face sheet and emergency information sheet flags
Service plan entry
Incident report for any emergency event
Staff training sign-in sheets
Quarterly audit results

policies.title: Privacy, Confidentiality and HIPAA
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers and students with access to resident information
policies.purpose: To protect the privacy and confidentiality of each resident's personal and health information, as required by Ohio's residents' rights law and, where [AGENCY NAME] is a HIPAA covered entity, by federal privacy rules.
policies.policy:
Confidentiality of records and privacy are resident rights under ORC 3721.13(A), and they cannot be waived (ORC 3721.13(C)). [AGENCY NAME] keeps all resident information confidential, discloses it only with the written authorization of the resident or sponsor or as required or permitted by law, and protects residents' privacy in personal care, treatment, visits, telephone calls and mail.

HIPAA duties apply if the facility is a covered entity, for example because it transmits claims electronically to Medicaid as a waiver provider. The Administrator, with counsel, makes and documents a covered-entity determination before opening and reviews it annually. If the facility is a covered entity, it complies with 45 CFR Part 160 and the administrative requirements in 45 CFR 164.530. It designates a privacy official, trains its workforce, maintains safeguards, provides a complaint process, applies sanctions and documents these actions. Where HIPAA does not apply, the facility still follows the confidentiality standards of this policy as a matter of Ohio resident rights.

definitions.definition: Any information, in any form, that identifies a resident and relates to the resident's care, condition, payment, finances or personal affairs.
A health care provider that transmits health information electronically in connection with a transaction covered by HIPAA, such as billing Medicaid, or another entity defined in 45 CFR Part 160.
The person designated to develop and implement privacy policies and receive complaints under 45 CFR 164.530.
A signed, dated written permission from the resident or authorized representative to release specified information to a specified person for a stated purpose.

procedures: Before opening, the Administrator and counsel determine whether [AGENCY NAME] is a HIPAA covered entity and document the determination, then repeat it annually and whenever billing practices change.

If the facility is a covered entity, the Administrator designates a privacy official in writing ([PRIVACY OFFICIAL NAME AND TITLE]) and posts the contact information for privacy questions and complaints.

At hire and before any access to resident information, each workforce member is trained on this policy, signs a confidentiality statement, and receives refresher training at least annually and when policies change. Training is recorded in the personnel record (STF-03, STF-05).

Staff access only the information needed to do their jobs. Resident records are stored in locked cabinets or in password-protected electronic systems with individual user IDs. Staff never share passwords.

Staff do not discuss residents in hallways, dining rooms or other public areas, on social media or with anyone not involved in the resident's care. Staff do not photograph or record residents without written consent.
Charts, medication administration records and sign-in sheets are kept out of view of visitors and other residents, and screens are locked when unattended.

Staff provide personal care, treatment and examinations in private, close doors and curtains, and knock before entering a resident's room. Residents may have private telephone calls and receive mail unopened (RR-01).

Staff release resident information only (a) with a signed authorization from the resident or sponsor, or (b) as required or permitted by law, such as to the Ohio Department of Health, the Department of Aging or its agents, the Long-Term Care Ombudsman, adult protective services, law enforcement or in an emergency to treating providers. The Administrator approves all other releases.

Before any release, staff verify the requester's identity and authority, release only the minimum necessary information when required by law, and record the release (date, recipient, information released, authority) in the record's disclosure log.
If the facility is a covered entity, it provides a Notice of Privacy Practices at or before admission, requests a signed acknowledgment, and makes the notice available on request and at the facility.

Residents or their authorized representatives may review their records and request copies under the facility's records access procedure (REC-01). The Administrator responds within the time required by law and explains any permitted fee.

Any resident, sponsor or employee may complain about a privacy matter to the privacy official or Administrator without retaliation. Complaints are logged, investigated within [NUMBER] business days and the outcome is recorded (RR-02).

If an unauthorized use or disclosure is discovered, the staff member notifies the Administrator or privacy official immediately. The Administrator investigates, mitigates harm, consults counsel on any notification obligations under federal and Ohio law, and documents the event.
Employees who violate this policy are subject to sanctions up to termination, applied consistently and documented in the personnel file (STF-06).

The Administrator reviews this policy, the covered-entity determination, the disclosure logs and complaint log at least annually and reports to the QA committee (GOV-04). Privacy documentation is retained for the period set in REC-01 and, if covered, at least six years.

responsibilities.duty: Makes the covered-entity determination, ensures safeguards and training, approves non-routine releases and investigates breaches.
If HIPAA applies, develops privacy procedures, receives complaints and oversees the Notice of Privacy Practices.
Protect resident information, follow access and release rules and report violations immediately.
Maintains records security, the disclosure log and handles records requests.

documentation: Covered-entity determination memo
Privacy official designation
Signed confidentiality statements
Training records
Disclosure log and signed authorizations
Notice of Privacy Practices and acknowledgments (if covered)
Privacy complaint log and investigation notes
Sanction records
Annual policy review

policies.title: Nondiscrimination and Language Access
policies.applies_to: Administrator, admissions staff, all employees
policies.purpose: To make sure all prospective and current residents are treated without discrimination, that people with disabilities are given a clear explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate them, and that residents with limited English proficiency can understand and take part in their care and in facility decisions.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] protects each resident's civil rights, as required by ORC 3721.13(A), and these rights cannot be waived (ORC 3721.13(C)). The facility does not discriminate in admission, care, services, room assignment, discharge or any other aspect of residence on the basis of race, color, national origin, language, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, marital status, or source of payment, including Medicaid Assisted Living Waiver participation, except as the licensing rules require the facility to decline residents whose needs it cannot lawfully serve (ADM-06).

As a business serving the public and a participant in Medicaid, the facility follows the Americans with Disabilities Act (42 USC 12101 et seq. and 28 CFR Part 36) and, as a recipient of federal financial assistance, Title VI of the Civil Rights Act (42 USC 2000d). Under OAC 3701-16-07(F), each prospective resident receives, before admission, an explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabled or potentially disabled residents and its policy on transferring residents to units that accommodate disabilities (see ADM-02). The facility makes reasonable accommodations and modifications for disability unless doing so would fundamentally alter its services or pose an undue burden or a direct threat, as determined by individualized assessment and documented.

The facility gives qualified interpreters or translated materials to residents and sponsors with limited English proficiency at no cost to them. Staff who assist with medication must be able to read, write and understand English so that labels, orders and records are handled safely (HLT-02).

definitions.definition: A limited ability to speak, read, write or understand English well enough to take part fully in care decisions and facility life.

A change to a policy, practice, service or physical feature that allows a person with a disability an equal opportunity to use and enjoy the facility, unless it would fundamentally alter the service or cause undue burden.

A person who can interpret accurately, impartially and with appropriate vocabulary; a family member is used only at the resident's informed request and never for sensitive matters when a qualified interpreter is available.

procedures: The Administrator designates a Nondiscrimination Coordinator ([NAME AND TITLE]) who receives questions and complaints about discrimination, language access and accommodation requests, and posts the coordinator's contact information.

At the first inquiry, admissions staff ask how the prospective resident prefers to communicate (language, hearing, vision, reading ability) and record the answer on the pre-admission screening form (ADM-01).

Admissions staff screen applicants on the same criteria for everyone (ADM-01). They record the specific licensing or care-need reason for any denial, and the Administrator reviews every denial for discrimination risk before it is communicated.

Before admission, staff give each prospective resident or sponsor the written explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabled or potentially disabled residents and its policy on transfers to units that accommodate disabilities, and explain it verbally (ADM-02).

When a resident or applicant requests an accommodation, the staff member records the request the same day and forwards it to the Nondiscrimination Coordinator, who meets with the requester within [NUMBER] business days to discuss options.

The Coordinator and Administrator decide on the request by individualized assessment, document the decision and reasons, and give the resident a written response. Approved accommodations are added to the service plan (ADM-05). If a request is denied, the Coordinator offers an alternative and explains the grievance process (RR-02).

For residents with LEP, staff use a qualified interpreter (in person, by telephone or by video service [INTERPRETER SERVICE NAME]) for admission, rights explanations, consents, service planning, risk agreements, grievances, change-of-condition conversations and discharge notices.

The facility provides written materials (rights, policies, admission agreement, grievance procedure) translated into the languages commonly used by residents in our area, or provides oral interpretation of them with documentation of the interpretation.
Staff post a notice, in languages commonly encountered, telling residents they may request interpreter services and aids at no charge.
Staff may use family members or friends as interpreters only when the resident requests it, after being offered a qualified interpreter, and this choice is documented.

The Administrator confirms before hire and annually that every staff member who assists with medication can read, write and understand English, and documents this in the personnel record (STF-03, STF-05, HLT-02).

Staff communicate effectively with residents who have hearing, vision, speech or cognitive disabilities by using auxiliary aids such as written notes, large print, amplification or assistive technology, and record the aids used in the service plan.
The facility does not charge residents extra fees for accommodations, interpreters or auxiliary aids required by law.

Staff treat residents, visitors and coworkers with respect, and report discriminatory or harassing conduct to the Coordinator or Administrator. Retaliation against anyone who reports is prohibited and is grounds for discipline (STF-06).
The Coordinator keeps a log of accommodation requests, interpreter use and discrimination complaints, and the Administrator reviews it quarterly and reports to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures nondiscrimination and language access, approves denials and accommodation decisions and reviews the log.
Receives requests and complaints, arranges accommodations and interpreter services.
Identifies communication needs, delivers the accommodation explanation before admission and applies admission criteria consistently.
Treat residents without discrimination, use interpreters appropriately and report concerns.

documentation: Pre-admission communication needs entry
Signed disclosure acknowledgment (accommodation explanation)
Accommodation request forms and written decisions
Interpreter log (date, language, interpreter, topic)
Translated materials list
Staff English proficiency verification in personnel files
Discrimination complaint log
Quarterly review notes

policies.title: Pre-Admission Screening and Admission Criteria
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Admissions Coordinator, Nurse / Resident Care Director
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] admits only people whose needs it can safely and lawfully meet as a licensed Ohio residential care facility, and that each is screened, including a sex offender registry search, before admission.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is licensed by the Ohio Department of Health as a residential care facility under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16. As defined in OAC 3701-16-01, an RCF provides accommodations and personal care services, and may provide limited skilled nursing care within the limits of ORC 3721.011. Under OAC 3701-16-02 and OAC 3701-16-07, the facility may not admit or retain a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond ORC 3721.011 limits. The rule provides that this includes needing skilled nursing care 8 or more hours a day or 40 or more hours a week.

Every applicant goes through the same pre-admission screening. Before admission, the facility searches the Ohio sex offender registry and keeps the result in the record (OAC 3701-16-07). The facility does not admit, and does not retain except for hospice residents as the rule permits, a person who needs restraints, is bedridden, has a stage III or IV pressure ulcer, or has an unstable medical condition. The facility also does not admit more residents than it can serve with consistent nursing coverage and other staffing appropriate for the volume and needs of residents (OAC 3701-16-05(K)-(L)). Admissions decisions are made on these criteria and not on discriminatory grounds (RR-08).

definitions.definition: As defined in OAC 3701-16-01; services that require the skills of a licensed nurse, and, where applicable, that are limited by ORC 3721.011 for residents in an RCF. The current rule text is reproduced in the pre-admission packet (ADM-02).
Assistance with activities of daily living and other personal needs as defined in the rules and described in the admission agreement (OAC 3701-16-09).

A medical condition that is changing or fluctuating in ways that require frequent licensed-nurse assessment or intervention beyond what the facility may provide, as determined by the Nurse / Resident Care Director with the resident's physician.
A person or entity who assists or acts for a resident in dealing with the facility.

procedures: The Admissions Coordinator takes each inquiry and completes the Pre-Admission Screening Form [FORM NAME], recording the applicant's diagnoses, medications, mobility, cognitive status, behaviors, therapies and treatments, and any history that bears on safety.

The Admissions Coordinator confirms the facility has a vacancy within its licensed capacity and that current staffing and nursing coverage allow it to admit one more resident without compromising care (OAC 3701-16-05(L)). The Administrator signs off on this capacity check for each admission.
The Admissions Coordinator obtains the applicant's physician information and current orders, medication list, and any hospital or other discharge records needed to evaluate care needs.

The Nurse / Resident Care Director meets the applicant in person (or reviews records if the applicant is in a hospital or other setting) and completes a pre-admission clinical evaluation of care needs, comparing them with the facility's service capability and with admission prohibitions.

The Nurse determines whether the applicant needs, or is likely to need, skilled nursing care. Any need for skilled nursing is compared with the ORC 3721.011 limits, including the 8-hours-a-day and 40-hours-a-week thresholds, and documented with the reasoning. If the need exceeds the limits, the applicant is not admitted.

The Nurse also determines whether the applicant needs restraints, is bedridden, has a stage III or IV pressure ulcer, or has an unstable condition. If so, the applicant is not admitted. Hospice exceptions apply only to retention of an existing resident in accordance with the rule (ADM-06, HLT-08).

The Admissions Coordinator searches the Ohio sex offender registry for the applicant before admission, prints or saves the result with the date and the staff member's name, and files it in the admission record.

If the registry search shows a match, the Admissions Coordinator immediately notifies the Administrator, who reviews the circumstances, consults counsel as needed, and documents the decision and any safeguards for other residents before proceeding. The facility does not reveal the result to anyone other than as required or authorized by law.

The Nurse confirms the facility can provide the personal care the applicant needs in accordance with accepted standards, using trained staff, in line with the assessment (OAC 3701-16-09), and identifies any care the applicant may refuse or that would be addressed in a risk agreement (ADM-03).
If the applicant would live in a memory care or special care area, staff apply the additional criteria in HLT-05 before admission.

If the applicant intends to pay through the Assisted Living Waiver, the Administrator confirms with the waiver case management agency that the applicant is enrolled or being enrolled and that the facility is a participating provider (GOV-07).

The Administrator reviews the completed screening, makes the admission decision, and signs the Admission Decision Form [FORM NAME] stating the criteria applied. The Administrator reviews any denial for consistency and non-discrimination (RR-08).

The Admissions Coordinator notifies the applicant or sponsor of the decision in writing within [NUMBER] business days. For a denial, the notice states the reason (such as a need beyond licensed capability) and, where possible, suggests other resources.

For an approved applicant, the Admissions Coordinator provides the pre-admission policy disclosure packet before admission (ADM-02), and the Nurse completes the initial assessment and service plan under ADM-04 and ADM-05 consistent with timeframes there.

The Administrator reviews staffing and nursing coverage with each new admission and at least quarterly, adjusts admissions accordingly and reports findings to the QA committee (GOV-04). Screening records, registry results and decision forms are kept in the resident record or admissions file under REC-01.

responsibilities.duty: Makes final admission decisions, verifies capacity and staffing, and reviews denials and registry matches.
Completes screening, conducts the sex offender registry search and files the results, and communicates decisions.
Evaluates clinical needs against skilled nursing limits and prohibited conditions.
Provides current orders, diagnoses and information to support the evaluation.

documentation: Pre-Admission Screening Form
Clinical evaluation by the Nurse
Dated sex offender registry search result
Capacity and staffing sign-off
Admission Decision Form with criteria applied
Written notice of decision to applicant or sponsor
Physician orders and hospital records received

policies.title: Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet
policies.applies_to: All prospective residents and their legal representatives or designated contacts; Administrator, admissions staff and any staff who conduct move-in. Applies to private-pay residents and Assisted Living Waiver participants alike.
policies.purpose: To make sure every prospective resident receives, and has explained to them, the facility's required written policies before admission. This lets the person make an informed choice about moving in and lets [AGENCY NAME] show a surveyor a signed record that the disclosures were made.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME], a residential care facility licensed by the Ohio Department of Health under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16, gives every prospective resident (and the resident's legal representative, if any) a written Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet and explains it in a way the person can understand BEFORE admission. The packet is given before the admission agreement is signed and in every case before the resident moves in. A signed acknowledgment of receipt and explanation is kept in the resident record.

This policy meets the following official checklist items under OAC 3701-16-07(F):

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(1) (item F(1)): The packet includes the facility's residents' rights policy and procedures required by ORC 3721.12 (see RR-01 and RR-02). Any attempt to have a resident waive those rights is void, and the facility will not ask for one.

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(2) (item F(2)): The packet includes the facility's smoking policy (see SAF-08). The smoking content of the rule is found at OAC 3701-16-13(U), although rule -07(F)(2) refers to paragraph (W). The policy states that smoking and vaping are allowed only in designated areas; that no smoking or open flame is allowed where oxygen is stored or used, with signs posted; that the facility takes reasonable precautions for residents who smoke; that non-combustible ash receptacles are used; and that shelter is provided in bad weather.

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(3) (item F(3)): The packet includes the facility's policies on advance directives and do-not-resuscitate (DNR) orders, with an explanation of the resident's rights under Ohio law (see RR-06). The packet states plainly that an advance directive or DNR order is NOT required as a condition of admission.

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(4) (item F(4)): The packet includes the definition of "skilled nursing care" exactly as written in OAC 3701-16-01, and a plain-language explanation of what that means for the services the facility may provide and the limits on admitting or keeping residents who need skilled nursing care (see HLT-03 and ADM-06).

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(6) (item F(6)): The packet includes a written explanation of the facility's ability to accommodate disabled or potentially disabled residents, and the facility's policy on transferring residents to units that accommodate disabilities.

• OAC 3701-16-07(F)(7) (item F(7)): The packet includes any other facility policies that residents must follow (house rules), listed in the packet's House Rules section.

Any special care unit policy that must be disclosed before admission is provided under HLT-05 and is added to the packet when the prospective resident is being considered for that unit. Written risk agreements are handled separately under ADM-03; they require the resident's consent and a signed acknowledgment, and no risk agreement may waive a resident right.

The disclosures are not conditions of admission beyond the facility's lawful admission criteria in ADM-01. The facility does not use the packet to screen out a person because of disability, payer source, or the existence or absence of an advance directive.

definitions.definition: The set of written policies and statements listed in this policy that the facility gives to and explains to a prospective resident before admission.
As defined in OAC 3701-16-01. The facility reproduces the current rule definition in the packet and does not paraphrase it in place of the rule text.
A person with legal authority to act for the resident, such as a guardian or an agent under a durable power of attorney for health care or finances, within the scope of that authority.
An area identified by the Administrator where smoking and vaping are permitted, equipped with non-combustible ash receptacles and, in bad weather, shelter.
A living will, health care power of attorney, or DNR order that states a person's wishes about medical treatment. It may never be required as a condition of admission.
The signed and dated form on which the resident or legal representative confirms that each packet item was given and explained, and that questions were answered.

procedures: Admissions staff add the Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet to every admission file at the first serious inquiry, and the Administrator confirms the packet is current at each policy review under GOV-03.

The packet contains, as separately labeled sections: (1) Residents' Rights Policy and Procedures, including the grievance procedure and Ombudsman contact information (RR-01, RR-02, RR-03); (2) Smoking Policy; (3) Advance Directive and DNR Policy; (4) the OAC 3701-16-01 definition of skilled nursing care with plain-language explanation; (5) Disability Accommodation Statement and Transfer Policy; (6) House Rules and other policies residents must follow; (7) the Acknowledgment of Receipt and Explanation form.

The Administrator keeps the OAC 3701-16-01 definition of skilled nursing care in the packet as the exact current rule text, and re-checks it against the Ohio Administrative Code at least annually and whenever the rule is amended.

The Administrator (or a designee trained on this policy) gives the full packet to the prospective resident and, with the resident's permission or where legally required, to the legal representative, before the admission agreement is presented for signature.

Before giving the packet, staff ask about language, vision, hearing, reading level or cognitive barriers and arrange interpreters, large print, reading aloud or other aids under RR-08. The explanation is given in the person's preferred language and format.

Rights: staff go over the residents' rights policy and procedures, explain how to file a grievance and who to contact, including the Ohio Long-Term Care Ombudsman, and state that rights cannot be waived.

Smoking: staff explain whether the facility permits smoking and vaping, where the designated areas are, that smoking and flame are prohibited where oxygen is stored or used, that signs are posted, how the facility supervises residents who smoke and protects them in bad weather, and that residents who use oxygen must follow the safety rules in SAF-08.

Advance directives: staff explain the resident's rights under Ohio law to make, change or revoke an advance directive or DNR order, state that the facility will ask whether the resident has one but will not require one, and offer to place copies in the record under RR-06. Staff never suggest that admission depends on having or not having a directive.

Skilled nursing: staff read or hand over the rule definition, explain in plain language what the facility provides and what it cannot provide, and describe the limits on admission and retention of residents needing skilled nursing care (HLT-03, ADM-06).

Disability accommodation: staff give the Disability Accommodation Statement completed by the Administrator, which describes the physical plant features, services and supports that are available, and any units or areas that are not accessible. Staff explain that the facility will make reasonable accommodations and describe the facility's policy on transferring a resident to a unit that accommodates a disability, including the resident's participation in the decision and the notice process in ADM-07.

House rules: staff go over each other policy the resident must follow (for example visiting, pets, meals, quiet hours, use of the resident call system, alcohol, transportation, medication self-administration, and fees under RR-04) and state which are required by law and which are facility preferences.

Staff invite questions throughout, answer them, and note unresolved questions for the Administrator to follow up in writing. Residents are given a reasonable time to review the packet, and are told they may take it home or have family, an Ombudsman or an advisor review it before deciding.

The resident or legal representative signs and dates the Acknowledgment of Receipt and Explanation, listing each packet section. The staff member who gave the explanation also signs and dates. If the resident cannot sign, the legal representative signs; if no one can sign, staff document the reason and the witnessed verbal acknowledgment, and the Administrator reviews the record.
Staff give the resident a complete copy of the packet and the signed acknowledgment, and place the original acknowledgment in the resident record before the move-in date (REC-01).
If a risk agreement is proposed, it is handled under ADM-03 as a separate document with the resident's consent and signed acknowledgment, and it may not waive any resident right.

If any packet policy changes after admission, the Administrator gives the changed policy to each affected resident in writing, explains it, and obtains a new signed acknowledgment; the update is filed in each record.

The Administrator reviews a sample of new admission files each quarter to confirm the packet and acknowledgment are present, signed, and dated before the admission agreement and move-in, and reports results through GOV-04. Missing acknowledgments are corrected immediately.

responsibilities.duty: Adopts this policy and the contents of the packet, and ensures resources for language access and accessibility aids.

Keeps the packet current, completes the Disability Accommodation Statement, verifies the skilled nursing definition against OAC 3701-16-01, trains admissions staff, audits files quarterly, and answers unresolved resident questions.
Delivers and explains the packet before the admission agreement is signed, obtains signatures, provides copies, and files the acknowledgment.
Assists in explaining the skilled nursing definition, advance directive and DNR policy, and accommodation limits when clinical questions arise.
Reviews the packet, asks questions, and signs the acknowledgment. Signing confirms receipt and explanation, not a waiver of rights.

documentation: Pre-Admission Policy Disclosure Packet (current dated version with version control per GOV-03)
Signed and dated Acknowledgment of Receipt and Explanation, filed in the resident record before move-in
Disability Accommodation Statement and transfer policy given to the resident
Record of interpreter, translation or alternative-format services used (RR-08)
Notes of unresolved questions and written follow-up
Updated acknowledgments for any policy changes after admission
Quarterly admission file audit results (GOV-04)
Copy of the current OAC 3701-16-01 skilled nursing definition and the date it was last verified

policies.title: Risk Agreements
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Admissions Coordinator, Nurse / Resident Care Director, resident case staff
policies.purpose: To set out when and how [AGENCY NAME] may enter into a written risk agreement with a resident, so that the resident's informed choices are respected, the agreement is voluntary and documented, and no resident right or admission limit is waived.
policies.policy:
This policy meets OAC 3701-16-07(H) (see also (G)): if the facility has a policy of entering into risk agreements, it gives each prospective resident or sponsor a written explanation of the policy and of the provisions a risk agreement may contain, and keeps a signed acknowledgment on file.

[AGENCY NAME] has a policy of entering into risk agreements. A risk agreement is a written agreement, made with a resident's consent, in which the resident chooses to decline or modify a service or practice the facility would otherwise provide, and acknowledges the risk. Under OAC 3701-16-09, the facility provides personal care to residents who need it unless the resident refuses it or it is covered by a risk agreement.

A risk agreement requires the resident's consent and a signed acknowledgment (OAC 3701-16-07(G)). A risk agreement may not waive any resident right; any waiver of rights is void (ORC 3721.13(C)). A risk agreement is not used to admit or keep a resident whose needs the facility is prohibited from serving under OAC 3701-16-07 (ADM-06), and it does not relieve the facility of its duty to meet accepted standards of care for all other care. Care or services covered by a risk agreement are documented in the service plan (ADM-05).

definitions.definition: A written agreement, entered into with the resident's consent, that documents the resident's informed choice to decline or modify a service, or to engage in an activity, that carries identified risks.
A person or entity who assists or acts for the resident in dealing with the facility.
A decision made by a resident who has been told, in terms the resident can understand, the nature of the choice, the risks, the benefits and the alternatives.

procedures: Before admission, the Admissions Coordinator gives each prospective resident or sponsor the written Risk Agreement Policy Explanation [FORM NAME], and explains it, as part of the disclosure packet (ADM-02).

The written explanation states: that the facility may enter into risk agreements; that they are voluntary; that the resident must consent; the kinds of provisions an agreement may contain (such as the specific service declined or modified, the identified risks, the alternatives offered, the facility's responsibilities, and the date of review); and that a risk agreement cannot waive any resident right.
The resident or sponsor signs an acknowledgment that the explanation was received and understood. The Admissions Coordinator files the signed acknowledgment in the resident record (REC-01).

When a resident declines a service or requests an arrangement that carries risk, the Nurse / Resident Care Director meets with the resident (and the sponsor, if the resident wishes) to discuss the choice, the risks, the likely consequences and available alternatives.

The Nurse confirms the resident understands the choice. If there is a question about the resident's ability to understand, the Nurse consults the resident's physician and the Administrator before proceeding. A risk agreement is not signed by a sponsor alone in place of the resident unless counsel has confirmed the person has legal authority to act for the resident.

The Nurse checks that the requested arrangement is not one the facility is prohibited from permitting under OAC 3701-16-07, such as retaining a resident who needs restraints, is bedridden, has a stage III or IV pressure ulcer or needs skilled nursing beyond the statutory limit, and not a rights waiver. If so, no risk agreement is offered, and the Administrator explains alternatives (ADM-06).

The Nurse drafts the Risk Agreement [FORM NAME] in plain language, identifying the specific service or activity, the risks, the alternatives offered, what the facility will continue to do, and a date to review. The draft is reviewed by the Administrator and, if it is unusual, by counsel.

The resident gives consent, signs and dates the agreement, together with the acknowledgment. The staff member who explained it signs as witness. If the resident chooses not to sign, no risk agreement is in effect and the facility documents the refusal and continues to offer the service.

The Nurse gives the resident a copy and files the original in the resident record. The Nurse also records the covered care or service, and the resident's choice, in the service plan (ADM-05), and informs the direct care staff who need to know.
Staff continue to offer the declined service, respect the resident's choice, and watch for changes. They report any change or increased risk to the Nurse (HLT-04).

The Nurse reviews each risk agreement at the review date, at each reassessment (ADM-04) and after any change of condition, with the resident. The agreement is continued, revised or ended based on the resident's wishes and condition, and the decision is documented.
A resident may withdraw from a risk agreement at any time by telling any staff member. Staff notify the Nurse the same day, and the service plan is updated promptly.

If a risk agreement leads to a risk that the facility cannot manage within its licensed scope, the Administrator evaluates the situation under ADM-06 and, if needed, begins the discharge process under ADM-07.

The Administrator audits all active risk agreements quarterly for consent, signatures, service plan entries, reviews and any language that could be read as a rights waiver, and reports to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approves the risk agreement policy and forms, confirms agreements are not rights waivers or prohibited arrangements, and audits agreements.
Delivers the written explanation before admission and files the signed acknowledgment.
Counsels the resident, drafts and reviews agreements, updates the service plan, and reviews at reassessment.
Makes the choice, consents and signs; may withdraw at any time.
Reviews the form and any non-routine agreement, and confirms legal authority of any representative.

documentation: Risk Agreement Policy Explanation and signed acknowledgment on file
Signed Risk Agreement with resident's consent
Service plan entry for covered care
Review notes and revisions
Withdrawal records
Quarterly audit results

policies.title: Resident Assessment and Reassessment
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, assessing nurse or other designated qualified assessor, direct care staff, and medication staff
policies.purpose: To make sure every resident has a written health assessment on admission, that it is reviewed at least once a year and whenever the resident's condition changes, and that services, equipment and the service plan always match the resident's current needs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] completes a written initial health assessment for each resident within 48 hours after admission. The items in OAC 3701-16-08(C)(11)-(12) are completed within 14 days after admission. An assessment completed within the 90 days before admission may be used if it is current and complete for the required content. The assessment covers the resident's preferences, diagnoses, falls risk, medications, diet, functional status, and ability to self-administer medications. The facility reassesses each resident at least annually, within 30 days of the resident's anniversary date, and sooner whenever a change in condition or function suggests new services or equipment are needed. The facility offers influenza and pneumococcal vaccines to residents every year. This policy implements OAC 3701-16-08(A)-(C) and OAC 3701-16-08(D)-(E).

definitions.definition: The written health assessment completed within 48 hours after admission (with the (C)(11)-(12) items completed within 14 days) under OAC 3701-16-08(A)-(C).
The calendar date on which the resident was admitted, used to calendar the annual reassessment.
A change in the resident's health, function, behavior, or cognition that may require new or different services, equipment, or a different level of care.
The nurse or other person the Administrator designates in writing, based on training and licensure, to complete assessments.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing the qualified assessor(s) for [AGENCY NAME] and keeps the designation in the personnel and policy file.

Before admission, the Administrator or designee asks for any assessment the resident has had in the last 90 days (from a hospital, physician, home health agency, or the waiver case manager) and files it with the pre-admission screening (ADM-01).

On the day of admission, the qualified assessor starts the initial assessment. The assessment must be complete and signed within 48 hours of admission, and the time of admission is recorded on the form.

If a prior assessment is within 90 days of admission, the assessor reviews it with the resident, confirms it is accurate, updates anything that has changed, and records the date and source. The facility completes any content the earlier assessment lacks within the 48-hour period.

The assessment records the resident's preferences (routines, food, activities, privacy, who to notify), diagnoses, falls risk, current medications, diet and any therapeutic diet order, functional abilities and need for help with daily activities, and whether the resident can self-administer medications.
The assessor completes the items in OAC 3701-16-08(C)(11)-(12) within 14 days of admission and records the completion date on the assessment form.
The assessor records the resident's ability to self-administer medications. The result drives the medication assistance level in HLT-02 and the risk agreement in ADM-03, if one is used.
The assessor identifies any need that suggests the resident may exceed the facility's skilled nursing limits (ADM-06) and notifies the Administrator the same day.
Within the 48-hour period, the assessor and the resident (or representative) review the findings and the assessor gives them to the staff who will write the service plan (ADM-05).

At admission and every year after, the facility offers the influenza vaccine and the pneumococcal vaccine to each resident or representative. The offer, the acceptance or refusal, and the date are recorded in the resident record.
The Administrator keeps an anniversary-date tracking calendar. Annual reassessments are scheduled and completed within 30 days of the resident's anniversary date.
At each annual reassessment, the assessor documents diagnoses, diet, weight, medications, and functional status, and compares them with the prior assessment.

Staff report any change in condition or function to the nurse or Administrator the same shift. The assessor performs a reassessment promptly when the change may require new services or equipment, and the physician is notified under HLT-04.
After each reassessment, the assessor identifies new or discontinued services and equipment, and the service plan is revised under ADM-05 within the same period.
The assessor reviews findings with the resident or representative, and the resident's response and any refusals of service are documented.
The Administrator reviews the monthly assessment calendar and reports any late or missed assessments to the governing body for correction (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Designates qualified assessors, keeps the assessment calendar, verifies timeliness, and ensures follow-through on findings.
Completes initial assessments within 48 hours, completes the 14-day items, performs annual and change-in-condition reassessments, and documents findings.
Report changes in condition or function and give observations that inform the assessment.
Take part in the assessment, share preferences and history, and accept or refuse vaccines.

documentation: Initial written health assessment with admission date/time and completion dates
Prior assessment (within 90 days) with review notes, if used
Completion record for items in OAC 3701-16-08(C)(11)-(12)
Annual and change-in-condition reassessments
Influenza and pneumococcal vaccine offers, acceptances and refusals
Anniversary-date tracking calendar
Written designation of qualified assessors

policies.title: Service / Care Plan
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, nurse or assessor, direct care staff, and for waiver residents the ODA-certified case management team
policies.purpose: To make sure each resident receives the personal care and other services he or she needs, delivered by trained staff to accepted standards, and matched to the resident's written assessment and preferences.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] states the extent and types of personal care it offers in its policies and in the resident agreement (RR-04). It provides personal care to every resident who needs it, unless the resident refuses it or a risk agreement (ADM-03) covers the need. Care meets accepted standards of practice, is given by staff trained to give it, and matches the resident's assessment (ADM-04). Needs that are met by third parties, such as family, home health, or hospice, and needs the resident refuses are documented in the service plan. The plan is updated at each reassessment and on any change in condition. For residents enrolled in the Assisted Living Waiver, the plan is coordinated with the person-centered service plan required by 42 CFR 441.301(c) and reflects the resident's choices and goals. Where [AGENCY NAME] admits residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs, or serious mental illness, it maintains a psychologist or physician on staff or as a consultant, as required by OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)-(5). This policy implements OAC 3701-16-09(B)-(D), OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)-(5) and OAC 3701-16-08(A)-(C).

definitions.definition: The written plan that lists the resident's needs found in the assessment, the services to be given, who gives them, how often, and the resident's preferences.

Assistance with activities of daily living such as bathing, dressing, grooming, toileting, mobility, eating, and medication assistance, as described in the facility's policies and the resident agreement.
A service delivered to the resident by someone other than facility staff, such as a family member, home health agency, or hospice.
For waiver residents, the plan developed under 42 CFR 441.301(c) that reflects the resident's goals, preferences, and chosen services.

procedures: The Administrator lists the types and extent of personal care [AGENCY NAME] provides in the Pre-Admission Disclosure Packet (ADM-02) and in the resident agreement (RR-04). The list is reviewed whenever services change.

Within the 48-hour assessment period, the nurse or assessor and the resident (or representative) use the initial assessment to draft the service plan. The plan states each need, the service to be given, the staff role responsible, frequency, and the resident's preferences.

For each need on the assessment, the plan states one of the following: the service the facility will provide; a service a third party will provide; a service the resident refuses; or a need covered by a signed risk agreement (ADM-03).
The resident or representative reviews the plan and signs and dates it, or the refusal to sign is documented. A copy is offered to the resident or representative.

For Assisted Living Waiver residents, the Administrator or nurse gets the waiver service plan from the case management agency, makes sure facility services match it, and keeps both in the record. The facility takes part in team meetings requested by the case manager.
The Administrator makes the plan available to direct care staff on each shift in an accessible and confidential format (for example, a task sheet), and staff are shown how to use it.
Before assigning a task, the Administrator or nurse checks that the assigned staff member has been trained and is competent for it (STF-03). Staff do not give care they have not been trained to give.
Staff provide care according to accepted standards of practice and the plan, and record completion or refusal of care for the shift according to facility procedure.

When a resident refuses a service, staff respect the refusal, explain the possible consequences, notify the nurse or Administrator, and document the refusal and the explanation. Repeated refusals that affect safety trigger a reassessment (ADM-04) and, when appropriate, a risk agreement (ADM-03).

When a third party provides a service, staff record who provides it, how often, and how the facility and the provider communicate. The Administrator confirms that the service is actually delivered and tells the provider about any problems seen.

When the facility admits residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs, or serious mental illness, the Administrator keeps the written agreement or contract with a psychologist or physician for staffing or consultation and makes the consultant's recommendations available for plan development.

The nurse or assessor updates the service plan at each annual reassessment and whenever a change in condition is identified (ADM-04, HLT-04). Updates are completed promptly and reviewed with the resident or representative.
The Administrator checks the service plans of any resident who has fallen, lost weight, or shown skin changes within seven days of the event to confirm interventions are in place (HLT-06, HLT-07).
The Administrator audits a sample of service plans every quarter against assessments and daily care records and reports results to the QAPI committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures services listed in policy and agreement are actually provided, assigns trained staff, and oversees plan updates and audits.
Drafts and updates the plan based on assessments, documents refusals and third-party services, and trains staff on plan content.
Provide care according to the plan, document completion or refusal, and report changes.
Advises on care for residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs, or serious mental illness when applicable.
Help develop the plan, state preferences, and accept or refuse services.

documentation: Signed and dated service plan for each resident
Documentation of refused services and third-party services
Waiver person-centered service plan and case manager contacts (waiver residents)
Staff training and competency records for assigned tasks
Daily care/task records
Consultant agreement or contract (where applicable)
Quarterly service plan audit results

policies.title: Retention Limits and Conditions the Facility Cannot Serve
policies.applies_to: All applicants and residents; Administrator, nurse or assessor, and admissions staff
policies.purpose: To make clear to applicants, residents, and staff what level of skilled nursing care [AGENCY NAME] can provide, what conditions it cannot serve, and what happens when a resident's needs go beyond those limits.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] is licensed as a residential care facility under OAC Chapter 3701-16 and does not admit or retain residents who need skilled nursing care beyond the limits in ORC 3721.011, except as allowed for hospice. This policy meets the following checklist items. OAC 3701-16-07(E)(5): the resident agreement explains the services offered, the types of skilled nursing care the facility provides or allows, the authorized providers, and the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care (see procedures 2-4). OAC 3701-16-07(E)(7): the resident agreement states that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified under (E)(5) (see procedures 5 and 11). OAC 3701-16-07(F)(4): before admission the facility gives the resident the definition of skilled nursing care from OAC 3701-16-01 (see procedure 1). Part-time, intermittent skilled nursing care is limited to 120 days in any 12-month period. After 120 days, care may continue only under a written agreement with the resident and the resident's physician, with re-determination at least every 30 days (every 15 days for hospice).
