Except for residents receiving hospice, the facility does not admit or retain residents who need skilled nursing care for 8 or more hours a day or 40 or more hours a week, who require restraints, who are bedridden, who have stage III or IV pressure ulcers, or whose conditions are unstable. The facility searches the Ohio sex offender registry before admission. This policy implements OAC 3701-16-01, OAC 3701-16-02, OAC 3701-16-07(A)-(C), OAC 3701-16-07(D)-(E), and OAC 3701-16-09.1(A), (D).

definitions.definition: As defined in OAC 3701-16-01; the full rule definition is given to every applicant before admission.
Skilled nursing that is not continuous and falls within the statutory limits; capped at 120 days in a 12-month period unless an extended-care agreement is in place.

The written agreement among the resident, the resident's physician, and the facility allowing skilled nursing to continue past 120 days, subject to re-determination at least every 30 days (hospice every 15 days).
A person or agency allowed by law to deliver skilled nursing care in the facility, such as a licensed nurse employed by the facility, a home health agency, or a hospice.
A condition that is changing or unpredictable and needs frequent assessment or adjustment of treatment by a nurse or physician.

procedures: Before admission, the Administrator or designee gives each applicant or representative a copy of the definition of skilled nursing care in OAC 3701-16-01 (as the Pre-Admission Disclosure Packet, ADM-02) and documents the date it was given. This meets OAC 3701-16-07(F)(4).

The Administrator completes and keeps a current written description of the skilled nursing care [AGENCY NAME] provides or allows: [LIST OF SKILLED NURSING SERVICES THE FACILITY PROVIDES OR ALLOWS, e.g., dressing changes by a facility RN or by a home health agency]. This description is part of the resident agreement.

The resident agreement (RR-04) names the authorized providers of skilled nursing care: [AUTHORIZED PROVIDERS, e.g., facility RN, [HOME HEALTH AGENCY NAME], [HOSPICE NAME]]. This meets OAC 3701-16-07(E)(5).

The resident agreement states the limits on the type and duration of skilled nursing care: part-time intermittent care for no more than 120 days in a 12-month period, and the other exclusions in this policy (8 or more hours a day or 40 or more hours a week; restraints; bedridden; stage III or IV pressure ulcers; unstable conditions), with hospice excepted. This meets OAC 3701-16-07(E)(5).

The resident agreement states that the facility must discharge or transfer a resident who needs skilled nursing care beyond the limits identified in the agreement. The Administrator explains this statement to the applicant and a signed, dated copy is given before residency. This meets OAC 3701-16-07(E)(7).

At pre-admission screening (ADM-01), the Administrator or nurse reviews the applicant's needs against these limits, searches the Ohio sex offender registry, and denies admission when the applicant needs care the facility cannot provide or cannot retain.

When skilled nursing begins for any resident, the nurse records the start date and type of care, and enters the resident on the Skilled Nursing Day Log. The log counts calendar days of part-time intermittent care in the 12 months preceding each day.
The nurse reviews the Skilled Nursing Day Log monthly and notifies the Administrator when a resident reaches 90 days in the 12-month period.

Before the 120th day, the Administrator meets with the resident or representative and the physician to decide whether care will continue. If it will, a written agreement among the resident, the physician, and the facility is signed before day 120.

While an extended-care agreement is in place, the nurse arranges re-determination by the physician at least every 30 days (every 15 days for a resident on hospice) and documents each determination in the record.

If a resident needs skilled nursing beyond the limits (including 8 or more hours a day, 40 or more hours a week, restraints, bedridden status, stage III or IV pressure ulcers, or an unstable condition) and is not on hospice, the Administrator holds a resident meeting, reviews options including waiver services (ADM-07), and starts discharge or transfer under ADM-07 if needs cannot be met.
A resident on hospice may be retained beyond the limits when the hospice and the facility have a coordinated plan of care (HLT-08), and the facility can safely meet the resident's needs.
The Administrator reviews each new restraint request, pressure ulcer finding, or change to bedridden status the same day and decides on retention (SAF-04, HLT-07).
The Administrator reports retention reviews and any discharges for limit exceedance to the QAPI committee each quarter (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Keeps the skilled nursing description and limits current, gives the definition before admission, makes retention decisions, and starts discharge when required.
Tracks skilled nursing days, screens for excluded conditions, coordinates with physicians and hospices, and documents re-determinations.
Give the packet and signed agreement before residency and record dates.
Takes part in extended-care agreements and re-determinations.
Review and sign the agreement, take part in meetings about unmet needs, and decide on options.

documentation: Record of delivery of the OAC 3701-16-01 definition of skilled nursing care before admission
Resident agreement with skilled nursing description, authorized providers, limits, and discharge statement
Sex offender registry search result
Skilled Nursing Day Log
Written extended-care agreements and 30-day (hospice 15-day) re-determinations
Resident meeting notes and retention decisions
Quarterly QAPI summary

policies.title: Discharge, Transfer and Relocation Notice
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, nurse, social services staff, and business office
policies.purpose: To make sure any discharge or transfer from [AGENCY NAME] happens only for reasons allowed by law, with proper notice and planning, and to a destination able to meet the resident's needs.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] discharges or transfers a resident only for the reasons listed in ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33), such as the resident's needs cannot be met by the facility, the resident has improved and no longer needs the facility's services, the safety of other residents or staff is endangered, nonpayment, or loss of the facility's license. The facility makes sure the resident is adequately prepared and the destination can meet the resident's needs. When a resident's needs exceed the services the facility offers, the Administrator holds a resident meeting and discusses options, including waiver services, before any discharge is decided. The facility follows ORC 3721.16 and OAC Chapter 3701-61 for notice and process. The resident has the right to choose a licensed hospice. This policy implements OAC 3701-16-08(F)-(G) and ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33), (36).

definitions.definition: Permanent release of a resident from the facility to another location, whether voluntary or involuntary.
Movement of a resident to another facility, room, or level of care, including move to a special care unit where applicable.
A meeting with the resident, representative, Administrator, nurse, and (for waiver residents) the case manager, held to discuss unmet needs and options.
A written plan for the resident's move, including destination, transportation, medications, records, belongings, and follow-up.

procedures: The Administrator is the only person who may decide to start an involuntary discharge or transfer, and the Administrator confirms that a reason in ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33) applies before any notice is given. The reason is written in the record.
When the resident's needs appear to exceed the services the facility offers, the nurse completes a reassessment (ADM-04) and gives the Administrator a written summary of unmet needs.

Before any discharge is decided, the Administrator schedules a resident meeting. The resident, representative, and (for waiver residents) the case manager are invited, and the Ombudsman may be invited at the resident's request (RR-03).

At the meeting, the group discusses the unmet needs, what additional services or equipment could meet them, other options including Assisted Living Waiver services and home health or hospice, and any other alternatives. Notes of the meeting are placed in the record.
The Administrator offers the resident choice of a licensed hospice where applicable, and the resident's choice is documented (HLT-08).

If discharge or transfer is still required, the Administrator prepares a written notice stating the reason, the effective date, the resident's right to appeal or to a hearing as provided by law, and the Ombudsman contact (RR-03). The Administrator checks the current text of ORC 3721.16 and OAC Chapter 3701-61 at each use to confirm the notice period, delivery method, and content before issuing the notice.
The notice is delivered to the resident and representative in the manner required by law, and delivery is documented. A copy goes to the waiver case manager for waiver residents.

The Administrator and nurse identify a destination that can meet the resident's needs and confirm in writing, with the receiving provider, that it can accept the resident and meet the needs identified in the assessment.

The nurse writes a relocation plan covering transportation, medication supply and orders (HLT-01), a current medication list, a summary of the resident's condition, diet, equipment, and arrangement for follow-up. Medications go with the resident or are destroyed with consent as provided in HLT-01.
The Administrator arranges for the resident's funds, valuables, and personal property to be returned or accounted for with a signed receipt (RR-05).
The business office issues a final accounting and any refund owed under the resident agreement within the timeframe stated in the agreement (RR-04).

On the day of discharge, the nurse or designee gives the resident or representative the transfer paperwork and confirms the receiving provider has received it. Staff document the time, mode of transport, and condition of the resident.

For emergency transfers to a hospital, staff follow HLT-04. If the resident cannot return because needs exceed the facility's limits, the Administrator follows this policy and gives notice as required.
The Administrator follows up with the resident, representative, or receiving provider within [NUMBER] days after discharge to check the transition and records the contact.
The Administrator reviews every involuntary discharge with the governing body and the QAPI committee (GOV-04) to find ways to prevent avoidable ones.

responsibilities.duty: Decides on discharge, holds the resident meeting, issues notice, and oversees relocation.
Reassesses needs, prepares the clinical relocation plan and medication transfer.
Final accounting, refunds, and return of funds.
Reviews options with the resident and helps with transition for waiver residents.
Take part in meetings and planning and choose a destination or hospice.

documentation: Written statement of the reason under ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33)
Reassessment and unmet-needs summary
Resident meeting notes and options discussed
Discharge/transfer notice and proof of delivery
Receiving provider acceptance and relocation plan
Medication transfer or destruction record
Property and funds receipt and final accounting
Post-discharge follow-up note

policies.title: Medication Management, Storage and Disposal
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, nurses, medication staff, and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To make sure all medications at [AGENCY NAME] are ordered, stored, labeled, recorded, and disposed of safely and lawfully.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps all prescription drugs locked. It does not repackage or relabel medications. It keeps a medication list and a medication administration record for each resident. Telephone orders are taken only by a licensed nurse and are signed by the prescriber within 14 days. When a resident leaves, medications go with the resident, or are destroyed with the consent of the resident or representative. The facility takes steps to prevent theft of controlled substances (HLT-10). Medications are self-administered by the resident unless the resident is authorized to receive medication administration under HLT-02. Staff may not fill pill organizers. This policy implements OAC 3701-16-09(H)-(I) and OAC 3701-16-09(E)-(H).

definitions.definition: The record of each medication given or taken, showing drug, dose, route, time, and who gave or observed it, or the resident's refusal.
The current list of all prescription and over-the-counter medications and supplements for a resident, with dose, route, frequency, and prescriber.
Moving medication from its original dispensing container into another, or changing the pharmacy label. Not permitted.
A medication order given by a prescriber by telephone, accepted only by a licensed nurse.

procedures: All prescription drugs, including those used by residents who self-administer, are kept locked. The Administrator decides which keys and codes each person may hold, and keeps a list of who holds access.

Residents who self-administer may keep medications locked in their own rooms where the assessment (ADM-04) shows it is safe and the medication is secured. Where the resident cannot lock the medications, they are stored in the facility's locked medication area.
Refrigerated medications are kept in a locked container or locked refrigerator used only for medication, and the temperature is checked and recorded daily.
Medications are received only in the original container with the pharmacy or manufacturer label. Staff do not repackage, relabel, split into other containers, or alter labels.

Staff do not fill pill organizers for residents. A resident, a family member, or a licensed nurse authorized to do so may fill one. Where facility staff are not permitted to do so, the facility asks the pharmacy for resident-specific packaging.

On admission, the nurse completes the medication list from the prescriber's orders, the resident's containers, and the physician, pharmacy, or hospital list, and checks it with the prescriber when something is unclear.

The facility keeps a current medication list for every resident, updated whenever a medication is added, changed, or stopped. The list goes to the physician, hospital, or any receiving provider when requested.

The facility keeps a medication administration record (or a record of assistance) for each resident. Authorized staff record each dose when it is given or taken or when refused, and do not record in advance.

Telephone orders are accepted only by a licensed nurse. The nurse writes the order, reads it back, and sends it to the prescriber for signature. The signed order must be in the record within 14 days. The nurse follows up on unsigned orders at day 7.
Staff report a medication error, missed dose, refusal, or reaction to the nurse or Administrator right away. The nurse notifies the physician as needed and documents it (HLT-04, SAF-02).
Controlled substances are counted at each shift change by two staff and the count is signed. Any discrepancy goes to the Administrator immediately and is handled under HLT-10.
The Administrator or nurse checks medication storage, labeling, expiration dates, and records each month and records the results.
When a resident is discharged or transferred, all of the resident's medications that belong to the resident go with the resident or representative, with a signed receipt (ADM-07).

When a resident dies or a medication is discontinued, expired, or unclaimed, the nurse asks the resident or representative to consent to destruction in writing. Two staff witness destruction, which is done in a way that makes the medication unusable and unrecoverable, and sign the destruction record. Controlled substances are destroyed according to HLT-10.
A medication is never given to or used by another resident.

responsibilities.duty: Controls access to medications, oversees monthly checks, and makes sure storage and disposal follow this policy.
Takes telephone orders, maintains medication lists, reviews records, and follows up on unsigned orders.
Store, assist with, and record medications as authorized (HLT-02) and report errors.
Consent to medication destruction and to the medication list, and report concerns.

documentation: Medication list for each resident
Medication administration record or assistance record
Telephone order log with signed orders within 14 days
Refrigerator temperature log
Controlled substance counts
Medication destruction record with consent and witness signatures
Receipt for medications sent with resident
Monthly medication storage check

policies.title: Medication Administration and Staff Authorization
policies.applies_to: All residents; Administrator, nurses, authorized medication staff, and direct care staff
policies.purpose: To state who may help with or give medications at [AGENCY NAME], what each person may and may not do, and how authorization is verified.
policies.policy: Residents self-administer medications unless authorized otherwise. Staff who are not authorized to administer medications may only remind residents, hand over medication, open containers, or physically assist a resident who is physically impaired. Staff may not fill pill organizers. Medication administration by the facility is limited to a registered nurse, a licensed practical nurse who has completed an approved medication course and acts at the direction of an RN or physician, a physician, or another person authorized by law, and only on a prescriber's order. The authorized person remains on duty long enough to observe the resident accept the medication and for any reaction. A facility that administers medications must have one of these authorized persons on duty. Staff who assist with medication must read, write, and understand English. This policy implements OAC 3701-16-09(E)-(H), OAC 3701-16-05(F)-(I), and OAC 3701-16-06(D).

definitions.definition: The resident takes his or her own medication, with only reminders or physical help from staff as allowed.
Reminding, handing medication to the resident, opening containers, or physically assisting a physically impaired resident to take it.
Giving a medication directly to a resident or deciding and controlling how it is given, which may be done only by a person authorized by law.
An RN, an LPN with an approved medication course working at the direction of an RN or physician, a physician, or another person authorized by law.

procedures: At admission and each reassessment (ADM-04), the nurse determines the resident's ability to self-administer and records whether the resident self-administers, needs assistance only, or needs administration by an authorized person.

The Administrator keeps a roster naming each person authorized to administer medications at [AGENCY NAME] with license type and number, medication course completion (for LPNs), and expiration. The Administrator verifies each license with the Ohio licensing board before the person administers and at each renewal.
The Administrator checks before each shift schedule is posted that an authorized person is scheduled for every shift on which residents receive facility-administered medications.
Before a resident's medication is administered or assisted, staff confirm there is a prescriber's order for it, and compare the order, medication list, label, and administration record.

For residents who self-administer, staff may remind, hand the medication to the resident, open containers, or physically assist a resident whose physical impairment prevents opening or handling. Staff do not decide when, how much, or whether to give a medication.
Staff do not fill pill organizers for any resident, and do not pour, crush, split, mix, or inject medications unless the person is an authorized person and the order allows it.

When facility administration is needed, only an authorized person gives the medication. The authorized person follows the order for drug, dose, route, and time; verifies the resident's identity; and stays with the resident long enough to see the resident accept the medication and watch for a reaction.
The authorized person records each administered dose on the medication administration record right after giving it and records any refusal, held dose, or reaction with the reason.
An LPN acts only at the direction of an RN or physician. The Administrator keeps the written direction or physician order on file, and the LPN's supervising RN or physician is named on the roster.
Staff who assist with medications must read, write, and understand English. The Administrator confirms this at hiring and documents it in the personnel file (STF-03, STF-05).

Before assisting with medications, every staff member receives training on this policy, the five rights of medication safety, reporting errors, and the limits on staff roles, with competency documented.
A staff member who is not authorized never gives a medication. If asked to by a resident, family member, or co-worker, the staff member refuses and notifies the nurse or Administrator.

Staff report any medication error, refusal, adverse reaction, or concern to the nurse or Administrator immediately. The nurse notifies the prescriber as needed (HLT-04) and completes an incident report (SAF-02).
The Administrator or nurse observes medication passes and checks records at least monthly and corrects problems immediately. Findings go to the QAPI committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the roster of authorized persons, verifies licenses, schedules an authorized person on every shift needed, and confirms English proficiency of medication staff.
Assesses self-administration ability, directs LPNs, trains and checks staff competence, and reviews records.
Administers medications on a prescriber's order at the direction of an RN or physician.
Provide only allowed assistance, and report concerns and errors.

documentation: Roster of authorized persons with license verification and medication course records
Self-administration assessment results
Medication administration/assistance records
Prescriber orders and RN or physician direction for LPNs
Staff training and competency records
English proficiency documentation for medication staff
Incident reports for medication errors
Monthly observation and record review results

policies.title: Nursing Services, Skilled Nursing Limits and Dressings
policies.applies_to: Administrator, Director of Nursing/RN supervisor, licensed nurses, medication-authorized staff, personal care staff, contracted nurses and dietitian
policies.purpose: To define the nursing services [AGENCY NAME] provides as a Residential Care Facility, to keep skilled nursing within the limits Ohio law sets, and to make sure dressings and any part-time intermittent skilled nursing are provided only under written procedures, by authorized individuals, with nurse coordination and regular evaluation.
policies.policy:
[AGENCY NAME] is licensed as a residential care facility under ORC Chapter 3721 and OAC Chapter 3701-16. It is not a nursing home. The facility provides personal care, medication administration, special diets and dressings. It provides part-time intermittent skilled nursing only within the limits of Ohio law and this policy.

Staffing for nursing. (1) Under OAC 3701-16-05(F)-(I), whenever the facility administers medication, an RN, a licensed practical nurse who has completed a medication course and acts at the direction of an RN or physician, a physician, or another person authorized by law to administer medication must be on duty. (2) Under OAC 3701-16-05(D), if the facility provides skilled nursing beyond special diets, dressings or medication, it will employ or contract with a registered nurse for onsite supervision, will have a licensed nurse on call, and will maintain enough nursing staff to deliver the care. (3) The facility will have enough nurses to provide dressings or other skilled care it has agreed to provide. A dietitian is required for therapeutic diets (see DL-01).

Dressings. Under OAC 3701-16-09(J), the facility will keep a written list of the dressings it manages (the Dressing Formulary), will have written procedures for them, and will use only authorized individuals to apply them. Each resident receiving dressings is evaluated at least every 7 days to determine whether transfer is needed. Each evaluation is documented in the resident record, and a nurse coordinates the care.

Skilled nursing by facility staff. Under OAC 3701-16-09.1(B)-(C), any skilled nursing the facility provides is covered by written procedures and is delivered only by authorized providers. Each resident is evaluated at least every 7 days for transfer, orders are signed within 14 days, and a nurse coordinates the care. Part-time intermittent enteral feedings may be provided only if the facility has written procedures that state the types of feedings it will manage, documents the resident's weight, and has a dietitian involved.

120-day limit. Under OAC 3701-16-09.1(A) and (D), part-time intermittent skilled nursing is capped at 120 days in any 12 months. Beyond 120 days, the facility will continue only with a written agreement signed by the resident and the physician, and the resident's status will be re-determined at least every 30 days (every 15 days for a hospice resident; see HLT-08).

The facility does not admit or retain residents whose needs exceed statutory skilled-nursing limits (see ADM-06) and will use the discharge process in ADM-07 if a resident's needs can no longer be met.

definitions.definition: Nursing services that require the skills of a licensed nurse and go beyond special diets, dressings and medication administration.
Skilled nursing that is provided on a limited, non-continuous basis and does not exceed the limits set by Ohio law.

A person permitted by Ohio law and by the facility's written procedures to perform the task (for example a licensed nurse, or a person acting under a licensed nurse's or physician's direction as the law allows).
The RN or licensed nurse assigned by the facility to coordinate the care of each resident receiving dressings or skilled nursing.
The facility's written list of the specific dressings it manages.

procedures: The Administrator designates in writing the RN responsible for onsite supervision of nursing services ([RN NAME / CONTRACTED AGENCY]) and posts the name and on-call phone number of the licensed nurse on call ([PHONE]) at each nurses' station or staff area.

The Administrator confirms before each schedule is posted that every shift on which medications are administered has an authorized person on duty (an RN, a medication-course LPN acting at RN or physician direction, a physician, or another person authorized by law). The schedule is kept in the staffing file.

The supervising RN writes and approves the Dressing Formulary, listing each type of dressing the facility will manage. Any dressing not on the list is not applied by facility staff. The Administrator reviews and signs the Formulary annually and when it changes.

The supervising RN writes a procedure for each dressing type on the Formulary and trains authorized staff. Training is documented in the personnel file (STF-05) before the person applies any dressing.

Before beginning dressings or skilled nursing for a resident, the supervising RN confirms that a prescriber's order exists, that the care is within the Formulary or the facility's written skilled-nursing procedures, and that the resident's needs can be met. The RN documents the decision in the resident record.
The RN adds the dressing or skilled service to the resident's service plan (ADM-05) and names the coordinating nurse in the plan.

The coordinating nurse evaluates each resident receiving dressings or skilled nursing at least every 7 days to determine whether the resident needs to be transferred. The evaluation is dated, signed, and filed in the resident record. If a 7-day evaluation is missed, the Administrator is notified the same day and the evaluation is completed immediately.
The coordinating nurse obtains the prescriber's signature on orders within 14 days. Unsigned orders are tracked on the nursing order log and escalated to the Administrator on day 10.

For any resident receiving enteral feedings (part-time intermittent only), the supervising RN confirms the feeding type is on the written list of types the facility manages, records the resident's weight at the intervals the dietitian and prescriber set, and confirms a dietitian is involved before the service starts.

The coordinating nurse keeps a Skilled Nursing Day Log for each resident receiving part-time intermittent skilled nursing. The log counts days of service within the rolling 12-month period and is reviewed by the supervising RN weekly.

When a resident reaches day 100 in 12 months, the RN notifies the Administrator, the resident, the sponsor and the physician in writing and begins planning for either transfer or an extended-care agreement.

To continue skilled nursing beyond 120 days, the Administrator, supervising RN, resident and physician sign a written extended-care agreement before day 121. The RN re-determines the resident's status at least every 30 days (every 15 days if the resident is on hospice) and documents each re-determination.

If a resident's needs exceed what the facility may lawfully provide, the Administrator holds a resident meeting under ADM-04 and ADM-07, discusses alternatives including the Assisted Living Waiver where appropriate, and arranges transfer or discharge. Notices and relocation follow ADM-07.

The supervising RN reports monthly to the Administrator on dressings and skilled services provided, 7-day evaluation compliance, 14-day order signature compliance, and 120-day tracking. Results are reviewed under GOV-04.

responsibilities.duty: Ensures an RN is employed or contracted, a licensed nurse is on call, and nursing staffing is sufficient. Signs the extended-care agreement. Ensures the facility never provides skilled nursing beyond what the law allows.
Writes the Dressing Formulary and procedures, supervises onsite nursing, determines whether new skilled needs can be met, and trains authorized staff.
Coordinates each resident's dressing or skilled care, performs the 7-day evaluations, tracks orders and the 120-day count.
Is reachable at all times for staff questions and urgent nursing needs.
Participates in enteral feeding plans and in therapeutic diets.
Perform only the dressings and tasks for which they are authorized and trained, and report changes in condition (HLT-04).

documentation: Designation of the supervising RN and the on-call nurse schedule
Dressing Formulary and written dressing and skilled-nursing procedures
Staff training and authorization records
Seven-day transfer evaluations in the resident record
Order log with prescriber signature dates
Skilled Nursing Day Log and written extended-care agreements with re-determination records
Enteral feeding types list and weight records, if applicable

policies.title: Change of Condition, Physician Notification and Hospital Transfer
policies.applies_to: All direct care and licensed staff, Administrator, supervising RN
policies.purpose: To make sure that any significant adverse change in a resident's health or function gets immediate intervention, is documented, is communicated to the treating party and the resident's sponsor within required timeframes, leads to a reassessment, and that any transfer to a hospital is safe and coordinated.
policies.policy:
When a resident has a significant adverse change in health status, [AGENCY NAME] staff will take immediate action, document the change in the resident record, give information about the change to the treating party (the treating physician or other health care provider), and notify the resident's sponsor (OAC 3701-16-12(A)). Under ORC 3721.13(A)(34)-(35), the facility will make a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of a significant change in the resident's health within 12 hours.

A change in condition or function that warrants new services or equipment triggers a reassessment sooner than the annual reassessment, and the service plan is updated promptly (OAC 3701-16-08(D)-(E)).

The facility maintains written transfer agreements with hospitals and other facilities that can meet residents' needs (OAC 3701-16-13(W)-(X)). When a resident is sent to a hospital, the current medication list and face sheet go with the resident. Fires, or illness, injury or death resulting from fire or smoke, are reported to the State Fire Marshal and the Ohio Department of Health within 24 hours (see SAF-09 and REC-02).

Call 911 first for any life-threatening emergency. Notification of the sponsor and physician follows, and must never delay emergency care.

definitions.definition: A sudden or marked decline in a resident's physical, mental or functional status, or a new condition, injury or symptom that could threaten health or safety or requires medical evaluation (for example a fall with injury, chest pain, new confusion, uncontrolled bleeding, refusal of food or fluids, or a new skin breakdown).
The resident's treating physician or other health care provider responsible for the resident's care, and emergency responders or a receiving facility when the resident is transferred.
The person identified by the resident, such as an adult relative, friend or guardian, who has an interest or responsibility for the resident's welfare.
A one-page summary of the resident's identifying information, sponsor and emergency contacts, physician, diagnoses, allergies, advance directive status and insurance.

procedures: Any staff member who sees a significant adverse change stays with the resident, takes immediate action within their training (first aid, calling 911 if the situation is life-threatening), and notifies the nurse or supervisor on duty ([PHONE]) at once.
If the situation is life-threatening, staff call 911 first. Staff follow the resident's advance directive or DNR status as documented (RR-06) and give the responders the resident's information.

The nurse or supervisor on duty assesses the resident as far as their licensure and training allow and contacts the resident's physician or other treating party immediately. If the physician cannot be reached, the supervisor calls the on-call physician or the licensed nurse on call.

The person who contacts the treating party gives the resident's name, the change observed, vital signs if taken, current medications, allergies and recent events, and records the name of the person spoken to, the time, and any orders or instructions.
Staff carry out orders received and note them in the resident record. Verbal or telephone orders are written down and sent for signature in line with HLT-03.

Staff make a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor of the significant change as soon as possible, and no later than 12 hours after the change is identified. Notification includes what happened, the action taken and where the resident is. Each attempt is documented with date, time, the number called, and the result. If the sponsor cannot be reached, staff keep trying and the Administrator is told.
The staff member writes a dated and timed note in the resident record before the end of the shift describing the change, the immediate intervention, who was notified, and the resident's response.
If an incident (for example a fall or injury) caused the change, the staff member also completes an entry in the incident log and the Administrator begins an investigation (SAF-02).

If the resident is transferred to a hospital, staff send the current medication list (with last doses given), the face sheet, the advance directive or DNR form if one exists, insurance information, and the name and phone number of the sponsor and nurse on duty. A copy of what was sent is kept in the record.
Staff phone the receiving hospital to give a verbal report, using the facility's written transfer agreement as the standard route, and document the name of the person who received the report.
The nurse or supervisor tells the sponsor which hospital the resident has been sent to and why, and documents it.
The facility holds the resident's bed in line with the admission agreement (RR-04). The supervising RN or Administrator contacts the hospital within 24 hours for status and for discharge planning.

On return from the hospital or when a change persists, the supervising RN reviews the discharge orders, medication changes and care instructions, and reassesses the resident promptly (ADM-04). The service plan and any needed equipment are updated promptly (ADM-05).
If the resident's needs now exceed what the facility may provide, the Administrator follows ADM-06 and ADM-07.

If a fire, or illness, injury or death resulting from a fire or smoke, is involved, the Administrator reports it to the State Fire Marshal and the Ohio Department of Health on their forms within 24 hours (SAF-09, REC-02).
The supervising RN reviews the log of changes in condition and hospital transfers monthly for patterns, and reports trends to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Recognize and immediately report changes, give first aid and call 911 when needed, and document observations.
Contacts the treating party, directs the response, ensures sponsor notification within 12 hours and documentation.
Reassesses the resident, updates the service plan and equipment, reviews returns from hospital.
Maintains transfer agreements, ensures required reports (including fire reports) are filed, and reviews trends.
Keep the face sheet and medication list current so they are ready to travel with the resident.

documentation: Dated and timed notes in the resident record
Record of treating party contact and orders
Record of sponsor notification attempts and time
Incident log entry when applicable
Copy of the medication list and face sheet sent with the resident
Written transfer agreements
Reassessment and updated service plan
Fire report forms and confirmation if applicable

policies.title: Dementia and Memory Care (Special Care Unit)
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervising RN, clinical consultant, special care unit (SCU) staff, admissions staff, activities staff
policies.purpose: To set out how [AGENCY NAME] operates its Special Care Unit for residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness, to ensure the SCU policy is given and explained before admission, and to ensure placement in any secured unit is individualized, never based on diagnosis alone, and consistent with residents' rights and HCBS settings requirements.
policies.policy:
This policy meets OAC 3701-16-07(F)(5), the requirement that a facility give residents seeking a special care unit its written policy on care in that unit, and it contains each of items F(5)(a) through F(5)(l). The policy is given to, and explained to, the resident and sponsor before admission (OAC 3701-16-07(F)-(H)), and is also posted/available on request.

F(5)(a) Mission or philosophy. The mission of the [AGENCY NAME] Special Care Unit is to provide a safe, dignified and homelike setting in which residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness can maintain as much independence, choice and quality of life as possible. Care is person-centered, built on each resident's life history, routines and preferences, and delivered by trained staff who use calm, consistent, non-confrontational approaches.

F(5)(b) Admission criteria and screening. A resident may be admitted to the SCU if (1) the resident meets the facility's general admission criteria and is not in a category the facility cannot serve (ADM-01, ADM-06); (2) a licensed professional determines, after assessment, that the resident's needs are best met in the SCU; and (3) the resident or sponsor signs an updated agreement. Screening includes a review of diagnoses, cognition, behaviors, wandering or exit-seeking, medications, ability to participate in activities, and whether the unit can meet the resident's needs. Placement is never based on a diagnosis alone, and is individualized (OAC 3701-16-08(F)-(G); OAC 3701-16-09(L)). Admission to the SCU is not a condition imposed on any resident who can be safely served elsewhere in the facility.

F(5)(c) Transfer and discharge criteria and procedures. A resident will be moved out of the SCU to a less restrictive area of the facility when the resident's needs no longer require the unit. Transfer or discharge from the facility will occur if the resident's needs exceed the services the facility can provide, or for other reasons permitted by ORC 3721.13 and ORC 3721.16. In that case the facility holds a resident meeting, discusses options including Assisted Living Waiver services, gives notice, and prepares the resident under OAC Chapter 3701-61, ADM-06 and ADM-07.

F(5)(d) Weekly staffing plan. The SCU Weekly Staffing Plan (Attachment HLT-05-A) lists, for each day of the week and each shift, the number and type of direct care staff assigned to the SCU. F(5)(d)(i): the plan differs from the rest of the facility because [NUMBER] staff are assigned to the unit and are not pulled to other areas except in an emergency. F(5)(d)(ii): to provide necessary additional supervision for residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness, there is [NUMBER] staff member(s) present in the unit at all times, with increased observation during [LATE AFTERNOON / EVENING / NIGHT] hours, and staff-to-resident assignments are reviewed whenever resident acuity changes. Staffing is also governed by STF-01, and needs that are documented as met by third parties or refused by the resident need not be counted (OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)-(5)).

F(5)(e) Activities. SCU activities are offered at least [NUMBER] times daily, seven days a week. Types include structured group programs, music, reminiscence, sensory and tactile activities, light exercise and walking, simple household tasks, and one-to-one engagement for residents who do not take part in groups. They are chosen from each resident's assessment and life history so they match remaining abilities, and they differ from the general program through shorter sessions, more individual engagement and evening programming to reduce sundowning. See DL-02.

F(5)(f) Costs of services. The SCU Fee Schedule (Attachment HLT-05-B) lists the cost of each service the facility provides to SCU residents, including base rate, level-of-care or service charges, and any additional charges. It is given to the resident and sponsor before admission and is consistent with the admission agreement (RR-04).

F(5)(g) Specialized staff training and continuing education. Every staff member who provides care in the SCU completes 2 hours of initial training on cognitive impairment within 14 days of starting, and 4 hours of continuing education on that subject each year. If the facility serves both residents with cognitive impairment and residents with serious mental illness, the requirements are 4 hours initial and 8 hours annually (OAC 3701-16-06(E)(3)-(7), (F)-(G)). Personal care staff also complete 8 hours of annual continuing education. Training topics include communication, dementia progression, behavior as communication, redirection, wandering and exit-seeking, dignity and rights, and abuse prevention. See STF-03. A psychologist or physician is on staff or consulting for the facility ([CLINICAL CONSULTANT NAME]) as OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)-(5) requires when residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs or serious mental illness are admitted.

F(5)(h) Assessment and service provision, and change over time. Each SCU resident receives the initial assessment within 48 hours of admission and a reassessment at least annually (within 30 days of the anniversary date), and sooner when a change in condition or function occurs (ADM-04). The service plan is written from the assessment (ADM-05) and revised when needs change, so that the services increase or decrease as the resident's condition changes. Each reassessment includes a review of whether SCU placement and any secured features remain appropriate.

F(5)(i) Behavioral healthcare needs. Staff first look for unmet needs (pain, hunger, toileting, fear, boredom, environment) behind a behavior, and use non-drug approaches first. Individualized behavior support strategies are written into the service plan. The clinical consultant is consulted when behaviors continue, escalate or place anyone at risk. The facility does not use physical, chemical or isolation restraints (OAC 3701-16-09(L); SAF-04). Psychotropic medications are administered only on a prescriber's order (HLT-01, HLT-02).

F(5)(j) Physical environment and design features. The SCU has safe, uncluttered walking paths, good lighting with reduced glare, simple signage and visual cues, a homelike common area, personalized resident rooms, and [a secured outdoor space / access to outdoor space with supervision]. Any locked or delayed-egress features meet building and fire code and are approved by the State Fire Marshal or approved local fire department. Secured units are permitted only if they are individualized, reviewed at each reassessment, code compliant, and not based solely on diagnosis (OAC 3701-16-09(L)). Resident room doors are never locked to confine a resident.

F(5)(k) Family involvement and support. Family and sponsors are invited to the care conference at admission and at each reassessment. The facility provides [FAMILY SUPPORT GROUP / EDUCATION SESSIONS, FREQUENCY] and information about community dementia resources. Family and sponsors are told promptly of changes in condition (HLT-04). Visiting follows RR-01 and SAF-08.

F(5)(l) Additional services and procedures. In addition to services in the rest of the facility, the SCU provides: enhanced exit monitoring and wandering-risk checks (SAF-03), structured daily routines and a consistent staff assignment approach, individualized behavior support plans, extra dining assistance and cueing, and clinical consultant review for residents with complex behaviors.

Waiver and HCBS settings. For residents who receive Assisted Living Waiver services, the SCU meets the requirements of 42 CFR 441.301(c). Any restriction on a resident's freedom of movement or access must be based on an assessed individual need, documented in the person-centered service plan with the resident's (or representative's) informed consent, tried only after less intrusive methods, and reviewed regularly. See GOV-07.

definitions.definition: A designated area of the facility that serves residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness, may include secured features, and operates under the written SCU policy.
A special care unit with locked or delayed-egress exits or other features that limit free exit.
A physician, psychologist, or other licensed health professional qualified to determine whether a resident's needs require SCU placement.
A diagnosed mental illness that significantly affects a person's thinking, mood or behavior and ability to function, as determined by a qualified professional.
The psychologist or physician on staff or consulting for the facility, who advises on residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs or serious mental illness.

procedures: Admissions staff give the resident and sponsor the written SCU policy (this policy, with Attachments HLT-05-A and HLT-05-B) before admission, explain each item F(5)(a) through F(5)(l), answer questions, and document delivery and explanation in the pre-admission checklist (ADM-02).

Before any SCU placement, the supervising RN completes the pre-admission screening (ADM-01), including a search of the Ohio sex offender registry before admission, and confirms the resident is not in a category the facility cannot serve (ADM-06).

The supervising RN obtains a written determination from a licensed professional that the resident's needs are best met in the SCU. The determination must describe the individual's needs and behaviors. A diagnosis alone is not accepted as a basis for placement.
The Administrator reviews the determination and the screening and decides on admission. If the resident can be safely served outside the secured unit, the less restrictive setting is offered first.

The resident (or legally authorized representative) and the facility sign an updated agreement specifying SCU placement, the SCU fee schedule and the services to be provided (RR-04). Advance directive or DNR status is not a condition of admission (RR-06).

The RN completes the initial assessment within 48 hours of admission (using an assessment completed within 90 days before admission where permitted) and finishes the items due within 14 days (ADM-04).

Within the same timeframe the RN and the interdisciplinary team write the service plan, including the resident's routines, preferences, behavior support strategies, activities and any individualized safety measures, and review it with the resident and sponsor (ADM-05).

The Administrator posts the SCU Weekly Staffing Plan, confirms daily that the plan is met, and reviews it whenever resident acuity changes. Staff assigned to the SCU are not reassigned elsewhere except in an emergency.

The Administrator ensures every new SCU staff member completes the initial cognitive impairment training (2 hours, or 4 hours if both populations are served) within 14 days of hire, and every SCU staff member completes the annual continuing education (4 hours, or 8 hours if both populations are served), plus 8 hours of annual continuing education for personal care staff. Records are kept in the personnel file (STF-05).
The Administrator maintains the agreement with the clinical consultant ([CLINICAL CONSULTANT NAME]) and documents the dates of consultations.

SCU staff apply non-drug approaches first for behaviors and document triggers, interventions tried and the result. Persistent or escalating behaviors are referred to the supervising RN, who contacts the physician and clinical consultant. No restraint of any kind is used (SAF-04).
SCU staff conduct exit-seeking and wandering-risk checks as written in the service plan, and follow SAF-03 immediately if a resident is missing.

The activities staff plan the SCU calendar from residents' life histories and abilities, offer programming at least [NUMBER] times daily including evenings, and record each resident's participation (DL-02).

The RN reviews each SCU resident at each reassessment (at least annually, within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner when condition changes) for whether SCU placement and any secured feature remain necessary, whether a less restrictive setting is now appropriate, and what changes are needed to services. The outcome is documented and shared with the resident and sponsor.

For residents who receive Assisted Living Waiver services, the RN documents in the service plan any individualized restriction, the assessed need for it, the less intrusive methods tried, consent, and the plan for review, and shares the plan with the resident's waiver service coordinator (GOV-07).

If the resident's needs exceed the services available, the Administrator holds a resident meeting, discusses options including waiver services, and arranges transfer or discharge under ORC 3721.16, OAC Chapter 3701-61 and ADM-07.

The Administrator confirms annually that locking and egress features meet code and have been approved by the State Fire Marshal or approved local fire department (SAF-06), and that family education offerings are scheduled and recorded.
The QA committee reviews SCU outcomes (behaviors, falls, elopement events, weight loss, staff training completion, family feedback) quarterly (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Approves SCU admissions, maintains the staffing plan, training compliance, clinical consultant agreement, code compliance of the unit, and the SCU policy and attachments.
Screens, assesses and reassesses SCU residents, writes and updates service plans, and coordinates with physicians and the clinical consultant.
Determines the need for SCU placement and consults on behavioral health needs.
Deliver and explain the SCU policy and fee schedule before admission and document it.
Provide person-centered care, use non-drug approaches, monitor for exit-seeking, and complete required training.
Plan, deliver and document SCU programming.

documentation: Signed acknowledgement of receipt and explanation of the SCU policy (ADM-02)
Licensed professional's written determination for SCU placement
Updated resident agreement and SCU fee schedule (Attachment HLT-05-B)
Initial assessment, reassessments and service plans, including SCU placement review at each reassessment
SCU Weekly Staffing Plan (Attachment HLT-05-A) and daily staffing records
Training records for initial and annual continuing education
Clinical consultant agreement and consultation notes
Behavior support documentation, activity participation logs, and family conference notes
Documentation of individualized restrictions for waiver residents
Evidence of fire marshal or local fire department approval of secured features

policies.title: Falls Prevention
policies.applies_to: All direct care staff, supervising RN, Administrator, maintenance staff
policies.purpose: To identify each resident's risk of falling at admission, reduce the risk through individualized interventions, and respond consistently when a fall occurs, including reassessment, documentation and notification.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] assesses each resident's falls risk as part of the initial written health assessment, completed within 48 hours of admission (OAC 3701-16-08(A)-(C)). A fall, or a change in function, triggers a reassessment and an update of the service plan and any needed equipment (OAC 3701-16-08(D)-(E)). Every fall is recorded in the separate incident log with the time, place, date, description of the incident and action taken, and is investigated (OAC 3701-16-12(B)). If a fall causes a significant adverse change, the sponsor and the physician are notified as set out in HLT-04, including a reasonable effort to notify the sponsor within 12 hours. The facility does not use restraints as a fall prevention measure (SAF-04).

definitions.definition: An unplanned descent to the floor or other lower surface, with or without injury, including a resident found on the floor, and whether or not witnessed.

Conditions that raise the chance of falling, such as a history of falls, unsteady gait, dizziness, medications that cause drowsiness or low blood pressure, impaired vision, cognitive impairment, incontinence or urgency, and unsafe footwear or environment.
The separate log the facility keeps of incidents, with time, place, date, description and action taken.

procedures: The RN assesses falls risk as part of the initial assessment within 48 hours of admission, covering fall history, mobility and balance, vision, medications, continence, cognition, footwear and the use of mobility aids. The result is documented in the assessment (ADM-04).

The RN writes falls-prevention interventions into the service plan (ADM-05): for example assistance with transfers and walking, scheduled toileting, assistive devices within reach, appropriate footwear, adequate lighting, call device within reach, and hydration and nutrition support.
Direct care staff are told about each resident's falls-prevention interventions at shift report and the plan is available to them in the resident's care plan.
The RN reviews medications with the prescriber or pharmacist when a resident has a fall or is at high risk, and reports medication concerns to the physician (HLT-01).
Maintenance and housekeeping staff check halls, stairs, bathrooms, floors, handrails, lighting and outdoor walkways at least weekly and remove or report hazards the same day (DL-03).

When a fall occurs, the staff member stays with the resident, does not move the resident if injury is suspected, calls 911 for serious injury or if the resident cannot be safely assessed, and notifies the nurse or supervisor on duty.

The nurse or supervisor checks for injury, takes vital signs as trained, and contacts the treating physician for orders. The facility follows HLT-04 for any significant adverse change, including reasonable effort to notify the sponsor within 12 hours.
Staff record the fall in the incident log the same shift with the time, place, date, description of what happened and the action taken (OAC 3701-16-12(B)), and write a note in the resident record.

The Administrator or designee investigates the fall within 24 hours (or the next business day for weekends), looking at circumstances, footwear, environment, medications and staffing, and documents the findings and corrective steps.

The RN reassesses the resident after any fall, or after a change in function, and updates the service plan and equipment promptly (for example a walker, hip protectors, bed or chair alarms that are not restraints, or a therapy referral). The update is shared with staff and with the resident and sponsor.
Staff monitor the resident for delayed signs of injury (pain, swelling, new confusion, change in mobility) for at least 72 hours after a fall, with checks documented on the monitoring form.

The supervising RN reviews the incident log monthly for patterns by resident, time of day, location and cause, and reports results to the QA committee (GOV-04). Repeated falls by the same resident trigger a team review.
If a resident falls repeatedly and the facility cannot safely meet the resident's needs, the Administrator follows ADM-06 and ADM-07.

responsibilities.duty: Assesses falls risk, writes interventions, reassesses after falls and reviews trends.
Carry out interventions, respond to falls and document them.
Investigates falls, ensures sponsor and physician notification, and acts on trends.
Find and correct environmental hazards.

documentation: Falls risk section of the initial assessment and reassessments
Service plan with falls interventions
Incident log entries (time, place, date, description, action)
Resident record notes, post-fall monitoring forms and notification records
Fall investigation and corrective action records
Monthly falls trend report and QA minutes

policies.title: Skin Integrity
policies.applies_to: Supervising RN, licensed nurses, personal care staff, Administrator
policies.purpose: To prevent skin breakdown, to find skin problems early, to make sure residents with stage III or IV pressure ulcers are not admitted or retained (except hospice), and to make sure dressings are performed under the facility's written procedures.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] does not admit or retain a resident who has a stage III or stage IV pressure ulcer, except that residents receiving hospice care may be retained (OAC 3701-16-07(A)-(C)). The facility also does not admit or retain residents who are bedridden or whose conditions are unstable. Skin is assessed at admission, as part of the initial assessment, and at each reassessment (OAC 3701-16-08(A)-(C)). Dressings are done only under the facility's written dressing procedures, by authorized individuals, with an evaluation of the resident at least every 7 days for transfer, as stated in HLT-03 (OAC 3701-16-09(J)). Any new skin breakdown is reported as a change in condition under HLT-04.

definitions.definition: Localized injury to the skin or underlying tissue, usually over a bony area, from pressure or pressure with shear. Stages range from I (intact skin with redness) to IV (full-thickness tissue loss with exposed muscle or bone).
Any new redness that does not fade, blister, open area, tear, rash, or discoloration.
A pressure ulcer with full-thickness skin loss (stage III) or full-thickness tissue loss with exposed bone, tendon or muscle (stage IV).

procedures: During pre-admission screening (ADM-01) the RN asks about skin condition, pressure ulcers and wounds, and, where possible, views the skin or reviews the referral records. A resident with a stage III or IV pressure ulcer, who is bedridden or whose condition is unstable, is not admitted unless the resident is on hospice and the facility can meet needs (HLT-08).

The RN documents a head-to-toe skin check on admission and as part of the initial assessment within 48 hours, recording any wounds, pressure ulcers (with stage), bruises, rashes and risk factors such as incontinence, immobility, poor nutrition and diabetes.

The RN adds skin protection to the service plan (ADM-05): repositioning needs, support surfaces within what the facility allows, incontinence care, heel and bony-area protection, moisture control, hydration and nutrition, and skin checks during bathing.
Personal care staff look at the resident's skin during bathing and dressing and report new redness, open areas, blisters, swelling or pain to the nurse or supervisor the same shift.

The nurse or supervisor examines the area reported, documents location, size, color, drainage and the resident's pain, and contacts the physician for orders (HLT-04). The sponsor is notified following HLT-04, including reasonable effort within 12 hours of a significant change.

If a physician orders a dressing, it is applied only if that dressing type appears on the facility's written Dressing Formulary and is done by an authorized individual following the written procedure (HLT-03).
The coordinating nurse evaluates each resident with a dressing at least every 7 days for whether transfer is needed, and documents the evaluation, wound status and care provided in the record.

If a pressure ulcer reaches stage III or IV, or the resident's condition becomes unstable, the RN notifies the physician and the Administrator immediately. Unless the resident is on hospice, the Administrator holds a resident meeting and follows ADM-06 and ADM-07 to arrange a safe transfer to a setting that can meet the resident's needs.

The RN completes a skin assessment at each reassessment (at least annually, within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner on a change in condition) and updates the service plan accordingly (ADM-04).
The supervising RN reviews new skin breakdowns monthly and reports to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Assesses skin, determines whether needs can be met, sets prevention interventions and oversees dressings.
Perform skin checks during care and promptly report changes.
Performs 7-day evaluations for residents with dressings.
Ensures no resident is admitted or retained outside the limits (except hospice) and that discharge procedures are followed when needed.

documentation: Pre-admission screening skin information
Initial assessment and reassessment skin documentation
Service plan prevention interventions
Wound and dressing notes and 7-day evaluations
Physician and sponsor notification records
Hospice coordination notes where applicable
Monthly skin breakdown report

policies.title: Hospice and Home Health Coordination
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervising RN, direct care staff, admissions staff
policies.purpose: To honor each resident's right to choose a licensed hospice, to coordinate care with hospice and home health providers, and to apply the limits on skilled nursing correctly, including the exception for hospice residents.
policies.policy:
Each resident has the right to choose a licensed hospice (ORC 3721.13(A)(30)-(33), (36)). The facility does not steer a resident to a particular hospice and does not make the choice of hospice a condition of admission or continued residency. A resident who is receiving hospice care is an exception to the bar on admitting or retaining residents who need skilled nursing beyond the statutory limits (OAC 3701-16-07(A)-(C)). The facility still must be able to meet the resident's needs with the hospice's support, and if it cannot, discharge follows ADM-07. Under OAC 3701-16-09.1(A) and (D), when a hospice resident receives part-time intermittent skilled nursing beyond 120 days in 12 months, a written agreement with the resident and physician is required and the resident's status is re-determined at least every 15 days (every 30 days for other residents).

The facility coordinates its service plan with the hospice and with any home health agency serving the resident, and documents services provided by third parties. Staffing need not count needs that are met by third parties or refused by the resident, provided this is documented (OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)-(5)).

definitions.definition: A licensed program that provides comfort-focused care and support to a resident with a terminal illness and to the resident's family.
An agency that provides skilled nursing, therapy or other health services to a resident in the resident's home, which includes the facility, as ordered by a physician.
Any hospice, home health agency, therapy provider or other outside provider that delivers care to a resident separately from facility staff.
The review required at least every 15 days under the extended-care agreement for a hospice resident receiving skilled nursing beyond 120 days.

procedures: When a resident, sponsor or physician raises hospice, the supervising RN or Administrator gives the resident a list of licensed hospices that serve the area, without recommending one, and explains that the choice is the resident's. The conversation is documented.
The Administrator confirms the chosen hospice is licensed and obtains a copy of its license or confirmation of licensure for the file.

Before hospice services begin, the Administrator and the hospice sign a written agreement (or equivalent coordination document) that sets out each party's responsibilities for personal care, nursing, medications, equipment, supplies, after-hours contact and emergency response.

The supervising RN meets with the hospice nurse within 2 business days after the start of hospice services (and reviews the hospice plan of care) to confirm what the hospice provides, what facility staff provide, and whether the facility can meet the resident's needs.

The RN reassesses the resident, updates the service plan (ADM-05) to align with the hospice plan of care, and gives a copy of the updated plan to the hospice. The hospice's plan of care is filed in the resident record.
The RN confirms that the resident's advance directive and DNR status are known to the hospice and the facility (RR-06).

Facility staff keep the hospice's 24-hour contact number at the nurses' station and call the hospice, not 911, for changes covered by the hospice plan unless the resident's directives or an emergency call for otherwise, and notify the sponsor under HLT-04.

The coordinating nurse tracks skilled nursing days for the resident. If part-time intermittent skilled nursing reaches 120 days in 12 months, the Administrator, resident and physician sign a written extended-care agreement before day 121 and the RN re-determines the resident's status at least every 15 days, documenting each re-determination (HLT-03).
If the facility can no longer meet a hospice resident's needs, even with hospice support, the Administrator holds a resident meeting, involves the hospice, and follows ADM-07 for any transfer.

For residents who use a home health agency, the supervising RN obtains the agency's order and plan of care, confirms the agency's visit schedule, shares relevant observations from facility staff, and documents the visits. The RN reviews home health notes at least [WEEKLY] and updates the service plan as needed.

Facility staff document in the resident record each service provided by a third party (provider, date, service) and the portion of care the third party is responsible for. The Administrator uses this documentation when determining staffing needs under STF-01, counting only needs not met by third parties or refused by the resident, and documenting that determination.
The facility makes sure hospice and home health personnel have access to the resident and a private space, follow infection control (SAF-07) and sign in and out under facility visitor procedures.
When the resident dies, staff follow HLT-09 and coordinate with the hospice on pronouncement, release of the body and notification.

responsibilities.duty: Protects the resident's right to choose a hospice, signs coordination agreements, signs extended-care agreements and decides whether needs can be met.
Coordinates with hospice and home health nurses, updates the service plan, and tracks skilled-nursing days and re-determinations.
Provide the personal care assigned in the shared plan, and report changes to the nurse and hospice.
Explain the resident's right to choose a hospice and not make hospice choice a condition of admission.

documentation: Record of the hospice choice discussion and the list of licensed hospices provided
Hospice licensure confirmation and written coordination agreement
Hospice and home health plans of care and orders
Updated service plan reflecting third-party services
Log of third-party services provided
Skilled Nursing Day Log, extended-care agreement and 15-day re-determinations for hospice residents
Staffing determination notes when third-party needs are excluded

policies.title: Death of a Resident
policies.applies_to: All staff, nurses, the Administrator, and the business office staff who handle resident funds and billing
policies.purpose: To make sure that when a resident dies, [AGENCY NAME] responds with dignity, notifies the right people promptly, protects the resident's property, medications and funds, and completes the financial and regulatory steps that follow a death.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] will treat every death with respect for the resident, the family and other residents. The sponsor and physician are notified promptly and the event is documented in the resident record. Medications are sent out or destroyed only with consent and as required by OAC 3701-16-09(H)-(I). Resident funds receive a final accounting as required by OAC 3701-16-11(B)-(C), and any refund is made according to the written resident agreement required by OAC 3701-16-07(D)-(E). A death caused by fire or smoke inhalation is reported to the State Fire Marshal and the Ohio Department of Health (ODH) within 24 hours on their forms, as required by OAC 3701-16-13(W)-(X). This policy has no separate official checklist item. It is part of the facility's resident-care and financial-protection policies.

definitions.definition: The person or entity the resident has named, or who is legally responsible, to be notified and to act for the resident, such as a family member, guardian or attorney-in-fact.
The executor, administrator of the estate, or other person legally entitled to receive the resident's property, funds and medication decisions after death.
A written statement of all resident funds held by the facility, all charges, payments, deposits and refunds due, and any amount owed, prepared after the resident dies or leaves.

procedures: Staff who find a resident unresponsive or not breathing start the response described in the resident's advance directive or code status (see RR-06) and call 911 unless a valid do-not-resuscitate order is on file. Staff immediately notify the nurse on duty or on call and the Administrator.

If the resident is enrolled in hospice, staff call the hospice agency's 24-hour number right away and follow the hospice plan (see HLT-08). Hospice staff handle the pronouncement and release of the body according to their procedures.

Death is pronounced only by a person authorized to do so under Ohio law, such as a physician, EMS or the hospice nurse. Facility staff do not release a body until that has occurred and the Administrator or nurse confirms the funeral home or coroner is ready to receive the resident.

The nurse or Administrator notifies the resident's physician promptly, and no later than the same shift or the start of the next business day if the death occurs after hours. The nurse also notifies the county coroner when the death is unexpected or when law requires it.

The Administrator or designee notifies the sponsor promptly by telephone, in person if possible, and records who was notified, the date and time, and the person who made the call. If the sponsor cannot be reached, staff keep trying and use the emergency contacts in the record, and the attempts are recorded.

If the resident receives Assisted Living Waiver services, the Administrator notifies the resident's waiver case manager as soon as possible, and no later than the next business day, so that service authorizations can be ended. The business office stops billing for any service for dates after the date of death (see GOV-05).

If the death results from a fire or smoke inhalation, the Administrator reports it to the State Fire Marshal and ODH within 24 hours of the death on the agencies' required forms, and follows SAF-09. The Administrator keeps a copy of the transmitted forms and proof of the report.

If the death is unexpected, follows a fall or other incident, or if staff suspect abuse, neglect or exploitation, the Administrator secures the area as directed by law enforcement, completes the incident log entry under SAF-02, and follows SAF-01.

The nurse or a staff member who was present writes a note in the resident record. It includes the time found, observations, actions taken, who was called and when, who pronounced death, and when and to whom the body was released.

Medications: the nurse removes the resident's medications from the active medication area right away and keeps them locked. Medications are not given to other residents. They are sent only with an authorized representative who consents, or destroyed with the written consent of the authorized representative and with two staff witnesses, as required by C29 and HLT-01. Controlled substances are counted and handled under HLT-10. The medication disposition is recorded on the medication record with the date, drug, amount and signatures.

Personal property: two staff members, one of them a supervisor, inventory the resident's belongings. The inventory is compared to the admission inventory and signed. The room is secured. Belongings are released only to the authorized representative against a signed receipt. The facility does not discard or give away belongings, and does not remove items without the representative's consent unless the agreement or the law provides otherwise.

Resident funds: within 5 business days of the death, the business office closes any funds held for the resident and prepares the final accounting required by OAC 3701-16-11(B)-(C). Funds that were held in the separate interest-bearing account are accounted for with interest. The Administrator reviews and signs the final accounting.

Charges and refunds: the business office prepares a final itemized bill and calculates any refund of prepaid charges or deposit as stated in the written resident agreement (OAC 3701-16-07(D)-(E); see RR-04). The facility's internal target is to issue the final accounting, any refund and the final bill within 30 days of the death. Any longer period required by the agreement or by law is followed instead. Funds and refunds are paid only to the authorized representative or the estate, and a copy of the supporting letters or authority is kept in the file.

The Administrator makes sure that no staff member who is the resident's guardian or attorney-in-fact (other than a related person, see C36) takes part in the handling or release of the resident's funds or property.

The Administrator or designee tells other residents in a sensitive, appropriate way, supports roommates and staff who were close to the resident, and offers a memorial opportunity if residents or family wish.

After the death, the Administrator makes sure the room is cleaned and turned over only after the family has removed belongings or has agreed in writing that the facility may do so, and after any required cleaning for infection control (see SAF-07).

The resident's record is completed, closed and kept for the required retention period (see REC-01). The Administrator reviews every death within 7 days for care and incident issues and reports trends to the quality committee (see GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Directs the response, notifies the sponsor, physician and waiver case manager, makes required reports (including the 24-hour fire-related report), signs the final accounting and reviews each death.
Directs clinical response, secures and documents medications, notifies the physician and hospice, and writes the clinical record entry.
Call for help and 911 as required, follow the advance directive, care for the resident with dignity, and write an accurate statement of what they observed.
Stop billing after the date of death, prepare the final accounting, final bill and any refund, and release funds only to the authorized representative.

documentation: Death note in the resident record, with times, actions and people notified
Notification log for the sponsor, physician, hospice, coroner and waiver case manager
Medication disposition record with witness signatures
Signed personal property inventory and release receipt
Final accounting of resident funds, final itemized bill and refund record
Copy of the State Fire Marshal and ODH reports and proof of transmission, if the death was fire-related
Incident log entry, when applicable
Death review note and trend report to the quality committee

policies.title: Controlled Substance Security and Theft Prevention
policies.applies_to: All staff who handle, store, administer, count, or have access to areas where medications are kept; the Administrator; nurses
policies.purpose: To prevent the misappropriation, theft and diversion of residents' controlled substances, and to make sure the facility meets its duty under state and federal law to protect them.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] complies with state and federal controlled-substance law and has these written policies and procedures to prevent misappropriation or theft of controlled substances. This policy meets the resident-medications item on the official checklist: OAC 3701-16-09, item (5) of the resident-medications paragraph (item 09-(5)). The paragraph letter was not visible in the excerpt used to prepare this manual, so the Administrator will confirm it against the full text of OAC 3701-16-09 at the next policy review (see GOV-03). All prescription drugs, including controlled substances, are kept locked, are not repackaged or relabeled, and are tracked on a medication list and administration record (OAC 3701-16-09(H)-(I)). Staff may only remind, hand over, open containers or physically assist residents who self-administer, and may not fill pill organizers. Administration is limited to an RN, a qualified LPN, a physician or another authorized person acting on a prescriber's order (OAC 3701-16-09(E)-(H)). The shift count log and two-person reconciliation described below are controls chosen by [AGENCY NAME] to protect residents. They are not requirements of the rule, but the facility treats them as mandatory facility procedure.

definitions.definition: A drug regulated under federal or Ohio controlled-substance law, for example opioid pain relievers, benzodiazepines and some sleep and stimulant medications.
Taking, using, selling, giving away or otherwise misdirecting a resident's medication for any purpose other than the resident's prescribed treatment.
