The facility provides a daily newspaper or makes community brochures available each day in a common area. Staff replace outdated materials when they are no longer current. The planner records which option is used.

The planner keeps a current, written list of community activities, with dates and places, and information on how residents can get there (including the transportation options in DL-04). The list is posted and given to residents at admission and whenever it is updated.

Staff offer residents an invitation to each activity and honor a refusal. A refusal is recorded on the attendance record, with the reason if the resident gives one. Staff do not pressure, coerce or penalize residents who decline.

For residents with cognitive impairment, the planner provides activities that match their abilities. These may include small groups, sensory and reminiscence activities, music, movement and structured routines. Activities for residents in a special care unit follow HLT-05.

For residents with serious mental illness, the planner works with the resident's service plan and treating providers so that activities support rather than conflict with treatment. Staff report any behavior change to the nurse or Administrator under HLT-04.

Staff keep activity areas and supplies clean, safe and accessible. Staff supervise activities with a risk of injury, and they arrange assistive devices, seating and lighting so residents with impaired mobility, vision or hearing can take part.
For outings, staff follow DL-04 and SAF-03. They count residents on departure and on return and record who attended.
Volunteers and outside entertainers are screened and oriented by the Administrator before working with residents (STF-02 and STF-06). A staff member is present for all volunteer-led activities.

The planner records attendance and each resident's response on the attendance record at the time of each activity. Staff review each resident's participation at least quarterly and at reassessment. The planner takes steps if a resident is isolating or declining.

The Administrator reviews the calendar, attendance and resident feedback quarterly. Resident council or resident suggestions are considered in planning. Results are reported to the QAPI process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Designates planners, makes sure they are trained, provides budget and supplies, and reviews the program quarterly.
Assesses interests, prepares and posts the calendar, provides the newspaper or brochures and the community information, and keeps attendance records.
Invite and assist residents to take part, honor refusals, and report changes in mood, participation or behavior.
Advises on activity adaptations when a resident's health or cognition changes.

documentation: Written designation of activity planner(s) and their training records
Monthly activity calendars
Daily attendance and participation records, including refusals
Record of daily newspaper or community brochures provided
Community activity and transportation information list
Resident interest information in the service plan
Quarterly program review notes and QAPI reports

policies.title: Housekeeping, Laundry, Maintenance and Building Environment
policies.applies_to: Administrator, maintenance, housekeeping and laundry staff, all personal care staff, and contractors
policies.purpose: To keep the building clean, safe, comfortable and in compliance with Ohio physical plant requirements, and to define the laundry services the facility provides.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] maintains a clean, safe and sanitary building. It holds a certificate of occupancy and complies with the Ohio plumbing code, the Ohio fire code and the electrical safety requirements of OAC 3701-16-13(A)-(I) and (V). Bathing fixtures have thermostatic mixing devices. Where the facility controls hot water, it is kept between 105 and 120 degrees F (OAC 3701-16-14). Resident-activated call systems are installed in resident rooms and bathrooms. The facility provides at least one toilet, one sink and one tub or shower for every eight residents. For new units the facility meets the minimum floor area of 100 square feet for a single room and 80 square feet per person in a shared room, with no more than four persons per room (OAC 3701-16-14). Laundry services are specified in the resident agreement as required by OAC 3701-16-11(E). Egress routes are kept clear. Door hold-open devices are used only if they release on power loss or fire alarm activation.

definitions.definition: A valve that limits and blends hot and cold water at a bathing fixture to prevent scalding.
The document issued by the local building authority that allows the building to be used as a residential care facility.
A system that lets a resident summon staff from the resident's room or bathroom.
Hot water supplied from fixtures, heaters or mixing devices that the facility operates or can adjust.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the current certificate of occupancy on file and posted or available as required by GOV-02. The Administrator calls the local building authority before any structural change, change of use or addition of beds, and does not use the changed space until approval is received.

The Administrator maintains a written preventive maintenance schedule. It covers the plumbing, heating and cooling, electrical systems, call system, fire alarm and sprinklers, elevators, appliances and exterior. Maintenance staff record each task and date on the maintenance log.

Maintenance staff test the water temperature at a representative set of bathing and hand-washing fixtures at least weekly and after any plumbing work. They record the readings and adjust or repair equipment so that facility-controlled hot water stays within 105-120 degrees F. Any reading outside this range is reported to the Administrator the same day, and affected fixtures are taken out of service until corrected.

Maintenance staff inspect thermostatic mixing devices at each bathing fixture at least quarterly and after any plumbing repair. A failed device is removed from service, and the fixture is not used by residents until the device is repaired or replaced.
The Administrator uses licensed contractors for plumbing, electrical, fire protection and heating and cooling work where Ohio law requires. Contractor invoices and inspection reports are filed.

Staff test the resident-activated call system in every resident room and bathroom at least monthly and record the results. Defective call devices are repaired or replaced within 24 hours, and staff make hourly checks on affected residents until repair. Staff never remove or disable a call device.

The Administrator keeps a floor plan showing each room's measurements, the number of occupants and the count of toilets, sinks and tubs or showers. The Administrator confirms the 1-to-8 fixture ratio before admission above current census and before any renovation. New units must meet the minimum floor area and occupancy limits (100 square feet for a single room, 80 square feet per person shared, maximum four per room).

Staff keep exits, corridors and stairways free of obstructions at all times. Maintenance staff check exit paths daily and check that doors open without special knowledge or keys. Any hold-open device is inspected monthly to confirm it releases on loss of power or alarm activation. Defective devices are removed.

Maintenance staff inspect electrical cords, outlets, space heaters and appliances monthly. Staff remove damaged equipment and do not use extension cords as permanent wiring. Resident-owned appliances are checked at move-in under RR-05.

Housekeeping staff clean resident rooms, bathrooms and common areas on a written schedule at least weekly, and sooner when soiled. They use infection control practices in SAF-07, including approved disinfectants, color-coded supplies and proper handling of blood or body fluids.

Chemicals are stored in a locked or inaccessible area, labeled, and accompanied by safety data sheets. They are not stored with food or medications. Staff must complete chemical-handling instruction at orientation (STF-03).

Laundry services provided by the facility (for example, linens, towels and personal clothing, frequency, and any limits or charges) are written in the resident agreement (RR-04). Staff launder in a manner that prevents cross-contamination, separate soiled from clean linen, and label or otherwise track personal clothing to prevent loss.

Staff report spills, hazards, broken equipment and temperature complaints to maintenance immediately. Maintenance staff make repairs promptly. A hazard that threatens resident safety is corrected or the area is blocked off the same shift. Staff also record how it was resolved.

The Administrator conducts a documented walk-through of the building at least monthly. Findings are corrected and reported to the QAPI process (GOV-04). The Administrator keeps fire marshal, ODH and other inspection reports on file with corrections (GOV-02).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains certificate of occupancy, approves contractors and repairs, verifies space and fixture requirements, and conducts monthly walk-throughs.
Perform and log preventive maintenance, water temperature and mixing device checks, call system tests and exit inspections.
Clean and disinfect on schedule, store chemicals safely, handle laundry per the resident agreement and infection control.
Report hazards and equipment problems immediately, and respond to resident calls.

documentation: Certificate of occupancy
Maintenance and repair logs
Water temperature log and mixing device inspection records
Call system test log and repair records
Floor plan with room measurements and fixture counts
Monthly building walk-through reports
Contractor invoices and inspection reports
Cleaning schedules and chemical safety data sheets
Resident agreement laundry provisions

policies.title: Transportation
policies.applies_to: Administrator, drivers, personal care staff and residents
policies.purpose: To make sure residents have information about and access to community transportation, that any facility-provided transportation is safe, and that residents can be transported to receiving facilities in an evacuation.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] gives each resident information about community activities and how to get to them (OAC 3701-16-11(A)). The facility's written disaster plan includes transport of residents to receiving facilities during an evacuation (OAC 3701-16-13(J)). If the facility transports residents in a facility vehicle or in a staff member's vehicle, it follows this facility standard. Drivers hold a valid driver's license, and vehicles are insured and maintained in safe condition. Whether transport is provided, how it is arranged and any charges are stated in the resident agreement (RR-04). Residents are never required to use facility transportation.

definitions.definition: Transportation provided or arranged by [AGENCY NAME] using a facility-owned, leased or staff-operated vehicle.
A location named in the disaster plan to which residents are moved when the facility is evacuated.
Public transit, paratransit, senior transportation programs, medical transport and volunteer driver services in the area.

procedures: The Administrator maintains a written list of community transportation resources (public transit, paratransit, senior ride programs, and non-emergency medical transport), with contact information, hours and eligibility. This list is given to each resident at admission, is posted in a common area and is updated at least every six months. Staff may help residents book rides on request.

At admission, staff tell the resident and representative which transportation, if any, the facility provides, any limits and any charge. The terms are recorded in the resident agreement (RR-04). Medical appointment transportation needs are recorded in the service plan (ADM-05).

If the facility provides transportation, the Administrator keeps a copy of each driver's valid driver's license and checks it at hire and at least annually. The Administrator also reviews the driver's motor vehicle record at hire and annually, and does not assign anyone whose license is suspended or who is otherwise unsafe to drive.

The Administrator keeps current proof of liability insurance that covers each vehicle used and its use for resident transport. If a staff member's personal vehicle is used, the Administrator confirms and files proof of that driver's insurance and the Administrator's written approval before any resident is transported.

Maintenance staff inspect each facility vehicle before use (tires, lights, brakes, seat belts, wheelchair securements and lift) and record the inspection. A vehicle with a safety defect is not used until repaired. Preventive maintenance is done on the manufacturer's schedule.

Drivers and escorts receive instruction on safe loading, wheelchair and mobility device securement, seat belt use, emergency procedures and first aid. Drivers must complete orientation and training in STF-03 before driving residents. A trained first-aid staff member is on the vehicle or immediately available.

Before each trip, staff confirm the resident wishes to go, review any needs in the service plan (mobility aids, oxygen, behaviors, medications due) and bring needed medications or supplies, with medication help provided only under HLT-02. Staff record on a trip log the date, destination, driver, vehicle, residents and departure and return times.
Staff count residents at departure, at each stop and on return. A resident who is missing or not returned on time triggers the response in SAF-03.
Residents are secured with seat belts, and wheelchairs are properly secured in the vehicle. Staff never leave residents unattended in a running or locked vehicle. No one smokes in a facility vehicle.

If an accident, injury, breakdown or other incident occurs, the driver secures the scene, calls 911 if needed, cares for residents and notifies the Administrator immediately. An incident report is completed under SAF-02, and family or representatives are notified under HLT-04 and RR-01 as applicable.

For evacuation, the Administrator keeps the disaster plan current with how residents with impaired mobility will be moved. The plan names the receiving facilities, the transport providers or vehicles to be used, and the means of transporting residents' medications, records and supplies. The Administrator confirms the agreements with receiving facilities and transport providers at least annually (SAF-05 and SAF-09).
The Administrator reviews trip logs, incident reports, driver records, insurance and vehicle inspections at least quarterly and reports findings to the QAPI process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Maintains the community transportation list, driver and insurance records, vehicle safety program and evacuation transport arrangements.
Hold a valid license, complete training, inspect vehicles, secure residents, keep trip logs and report incidents.
Help residents arrange transportation, prepare residents and supplies, and count residents on trips.
Maintain vehicles and perform repairs.

documentation: Community transportation resource list and distribution record
Resident agreement transportation terms
Driver license and motor vehicle record copies
Proof of vehicle insurance
Vehicle inspection and maintenance records
Trip logs and resident counts
Incident reports for transport events
Disaster plan transport arrangements with receiving facilities

policies.title: Staffing Levels and Supervision
policies.applies_to: Administrator, operator, scheduling staff, all personal care staff and other staff
policies.purpose: To make sure the facility always has enough qualified staff on duty to meet residents' assessed needs, carry out the evacuation plan and provide first aid, in compliance with OAC 3701-16-05.
policies.policy: Ohio does not set a fixed staff-to-resident ratio for residential care facilities. [AGENCY NAME] therefore sets staffing from residents' assessed needs. At least one qualified personal care staff member is on duty at all times (OAC 3701-16-05(C)(1)). When only one person is on duty, another qualified staff member is designated on call. The overnight staff person may be on call instead of on site only if the call system requirements of OAC 3701-16-14(B)(5) are met. Staffing is sufficient to meet assessed care, supervision and emotional needs, and also dietary, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and activities needs. The staff needed to carry out the evacuation plan are present at all times, and a personal care staff member trained in first aid is on site at all times (OAC 3701-16-05(C)(2)-(3)). Needs that are met by third parties or refused by the resident need not be counted in the staffing basis if this is documented (OAC 3701-16-05(C)(4)). The Administrator or operator keeps a coverage schedule for vacations, emergencies and long absences (OAC 3701-16-05(E)). [AGENCY NAME] does not admit more residents than it can serve with consistent nursing coverage and other appropriate staffing for the volume and needs of residents (OAC 3701-16-05(L)). Residents are never mandated, coerced or persuaded to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication or manage the facility.

definitions.definition: A staff member who has completed orientation, fire training and the personal care competency and training required by OAC 3701-16-06 (see STF-03), and who is old enough to work under the rule.
Designated by name, reachable at all times by the on-duty person, and able to reach the facility fast enough to respond to an emergency, as set out below.
The written plan setting who covers each shift and who covers when staff are absent for vacation, emergency or a long absence.
The documented calculation of staff needed, built from resident assessments and service plans, evacuation needs and non-care tasks.

procedures: The Administrator sets minimum staffing for each shift on a written staffing plan. The plan is built from the current resident assessments and service plans (ADM-04 and ADM-05), the evacuation plan, and the staff required for dietary, housekeeping, laundry, maintenance and activities. The plan is not based on a fixed ratio.

At least one qualified personal care staff member is on duty on every shift, including nights, weekends and holidays. The scheduler checks each posted schedule against this requirement before it is posted.

The Administrator decides whether the overnight person will be awake on site or on call. On-site, awake overnight staffing is the default. The overnight person may be on call only if the Administrator has first confirmed in writing that the resident call system meets OAC 3701-16-14(B)(5), and re-confirms after any call system change or failure.

Whenever only one person is on duty, the schedule names another qualified staff member who is on call. That person's phone number is posted at the staff station. The on-call person must answer within [NUMBER] minutes and be able to arrive within [NUMBER] minutes. The Administrator verifies this at the time of designation.

The Administrator uses the evacuation plan (SAF-05 and SAF-06) to identify how many staff are needed to evacuate residents with impaired mobility or cognition on each shift, and staffs each shift to meet that number. The Administrator revises the plan if the census or resident mobility changes.
The scheduler makes sure that at least one personal care staff member with current first-aid training (STF-03) is on site on every shift. Staff first-aid status is shown on the schedule.

The Administrator reviews the staffing plan at least monthly, and also when there is a new admission, a significant change in a resident's condition, a change in the number of residents who need extra help, or an incident that suggests staffing is inadequate. The review and any changes made are documented.

When any need is met by a third party (for example hospice, home health or family) or refused by the resident, the nurse or Administrator documents this in the resident's record and service plan. Only then is the need left out of the staffing basis.

Before accepting any admission, the Administrator documents that the facility can serve the person with consistent nursing coverage and other appropriate staffing for the resident volume and needs (ADM-01). If staffing cannot meet this standard, the admission is deferred or declined.

If the facility admits residents with late-stage cognitive impairment, behavioral needs or serious mental illness, the Administrator keeps a psychologist or physician on staff or under written consulting agreement. The agreement names the clinician and states how the clinician reviews residents and advises staff (HLT-05).

The Administrator or operator keeps a written coverage schedule. It names who covers for the Administrator and for each shift during vacations, emergencies and long absences. It is updated when staff or assignments change, and is available to every scheduler and on-call person.

When a scheduled staff member calls off, the supervisor on duty contacts replacement staff in the order set out in the coverage schedule, and uses the on-call person if needed. A shift is never left without a qualified staff member. The supervisor notifies the Administrator the same day of any shortfall and records what was done.

No resident is asked, required, coerced or persuaded to supervise other residents, provide personal care, administer medication or manage the facility. The Administrator corrects any such practice immediately and reports it to the QAPI process (GOV-04).

Staff are supervised by the Administrator or a designated supervisor. Staff under age 18 work only with on-site supervision by an adult over 18 (STF-03). New staff do not work alone with residents until orientation and fire training are complete.

The Administrator keeps personnel-compliance records on the forms provided by the ODH director (see STF-05), including training, first-aid, and qualification dates, and makes them available to surveyors on request.

Staff-resident concerns about short staffing may be reported to the Administrator without retaliation. Resident and family concerns follow RR-02. The Administrator reviews staffing complaints, incident trends (SAF-02) and call response times as part of QAPI (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets and reviews the staffing plan, designates on-call coverage, decides overnight coverage, keeps the clinical consultant arrangement, and maintains the coverage schedule and compliance records.
Builds schedules that meet minimum coverage, first-aid and evacuation requirements, and handles absences.
Remains reachable and responds within the set time when called.
Provides resident assessment information that drives the staffing basis, and documents third-party or refused services.
Provides resources to staff the facility consistent with this policy (GOV-01).

documentation: Written staffing plan with staffing basis calculation
Posted and worked schedules, showing first-aid-trained staff and on-call designations
Written determination that the call system meets OAC 3701-16-14(B)(5) (if overnight on-call is used)
Coverage schedule for vacations, emergencies and long absences
Documentation of third-party or refused services affecting the staffing basis
Monthly staffing review notes
Clinical consultant agreement (if applicable)
Personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms
Call-off and shortfall records

policies.title: Background Checks and Employee Registries
policies.applies_to: Administrator, hiring staff and all applicants and employees in direct-care positions
policies.purpose: To keep people who are barred by Ohio law from working in direct care from being employed by the facility, and to check registries and licenses before hire and during employment.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 3701-16-06(L)(1)-(5) (hiring exclusions for direct-care positions). [AGENCY NAME] does not employ any person in a direct-care position (a position that involves direct, hands-on or unsupervised access to residents) if any of the following applies: (1) the person has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to an offense that disqualifies the person under ORC 3721.121(C)(1); (2) the person does not provide the completed forms or fingerprints required under ORC 3721.121(B)(2) for the criminal records check; (3) the Ohio nurse aide registry has a finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property against the person; (4) the nurse aide registry of another state has such a finding against the person; or (5) a professional license held by the person has been the subject of action for abuse, neglect or misappropriation. Before any employment offer is made final, the facility completes the required criminal records check and registry and license checks. The Administrator reads the current text of ORC 3721.121, including the list of disqualifying offenses and any rehabilitation provisions, before finalizing the written hiring procedures of the facility, and updates this policy if the statute differs from the procedures below.

definitions.definition: A job in which the employee provides care or services to residents or has routine, unsupervised access to them, including personal care staff, nursing, dietary, housekeeping and maintenance staff who work in resident areas, as determined by the Administrator under ORC 3721.121.
An offense listed in ORC 3721.121(C)(1) that bars employment in direct care.
The registry of nurse aides and any recorded findings of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of resident property, maintained by Ohio and by other states.
The check of an applicant's criminal history, including fingerprints, under ORC 3721.121.

procedures: The Administrator designates the staff members who may carry out background checks and limits access to the results to those who need to know. Results are kept confidential and are stored in a locked or access-controlled file separate from the general personnel file.

The employment application asks each applicant to disclose any criminal convictions and pending charges, any finding on a nurse aide registry in Ohio or another state, and any action against a professional license. The application states that the offer of employment is conditional on the checks required by this policy.

Before the employee has any direct-care duties, the Administrator gives the applicant the forms required under ORC 3721.121(B)(2) and arranges for fingerprinting. If the applicant does not complete the forms or the fingerprints, the applicant is not hired (OAC 3701-16-06(L)). The date forms were given and the date completed are recorded.

The Administrator submits the criminal records check as required by ORC 3721.121 and reviews the results when received. The Administrator compares the results with the disqualifying offenses in ORC 3721.121(C)(1). A person with a disqualifying offense is not employed in direct care. The Administrator does not use this policy to apply any exception unless the statute expressly allows it and the Administrator has documented the basis in writing.

The Administrator checks the Ohio nurse aide registry for every applicant for a direct-care position, whether or not the person is a nurse aide, and prints or saves the result with the date checked. A finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation of property bars employment.

For applicants who have lived or worked in another state, or who report certification elsewhere, the Administrator checks that state's nurse aide registry and records the result. A finding of abuse, neglect or misappropriation on another state's registry bars employment.

For applicants who hold a professional license (for example nursing), the Administrator verifies the license on the issuing board's public lookup and records the result. A license action for abuse, neglect or misappropriation bars employment (see also OAC 3701-16-06(J)). Current licensure is also verified before any licensed professional works for the facility.

As a facility standard, and because the facility participates in Medicaid under GOV-07 and GOV-05, the Administrator also checks the federal and Ohio Medicaid exclusion lists before hire and at least monthly for all staff. A person on an exclusion list is not employed or retained.

A person is not given any unsupervised access to residents, and is not scheduled for direct-care duties, until the check is complete and has cleared. If a check is pending, the applicant is not scheduled as direct care and does not work alone with residents.

If a check bars employment, the Administrator informs the applicant according to the applicable law, does not hire the person for any direct-care position, and files the record. The Administrator keeps the reason for the exclusion confidential.

The Administrator checks the nurse aide registry and license status again for each direct-care employee at least annually, and whenever there is an allegation of abuse, neglect or misappropriation involving the employee. The date and result are recorded.

Employees must tell the Administrator within [NUMBER] business days if they are charged with or convicted of any offense, or if a registry finding or license action occurs. The Administrator reviews the matter and, if it bars employment, ends the employee's direct-care duties immediately.

If an employee is found to have a disqualifying offense or a registry or license finding after hire, the Administrator removes the employee from direct care immediately and acts under ORC 3721.121 and the applicable reporting rules. Allegations of abuse, neglect or misappropriation are reported under SAF-01 and REC-02.

The Administrator holds all background check results as confidential records, keeps them as set out in STF-05 and REC-01, and makes them available to ODH surveyors on request. Results are not shared except as the law allows.

The Administrator audits a sample of personnel files at least twice a year to confirm that every direct-care employee has a completed criminal records check, registry results and license verification on file, and reports findings to the QAPI process (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Ensures every hiring exclusion in OAC 3701-16-06(L)(1)-(5) is checked before direct-care work, keeps results confidential, and reads ORC 3721.121 before finalizing procedures.
Distribute forms, arrange fingerprinting, run registry and license checks, and record dates and results.
Answer application questions truthfully, complete forms and fingerprints, and report any new charge, conviction, registry finding or license action.
Supports enforcement of hiring exclusions and does not override them (GOV-01).

documentation: Employment application with disclosure questions
Records of forms provided and completed and fingerprinting dates
Criminal records check results (confidential file)
Ohio nurse aide registry check printout with date
Other state's registry check results, where applicable
Professional license verification
Exclusion list checks (at hire and monthly)
Annual re-check records
Hiring determination and notice records
Personnel file audit reports

policies.title: Hiring, Orientation and Ongoing Training
policies.applies_to: Administrator, supervisors, all personal care staff, other employees, activity planners and volunteers
policies.purpose: To make sure every staff member is old enough, qualified and trained before working alone with residents, and receives continuing training that meets OAC 3701-16-06.
policies.policy: This policy meets OAC 3701-16-06(I)(1)-(5) (orientation within three working days), OAC 3701-16-06(K)(1)-(2) (annual staff training on resident rights), and OAC 3701-16-06(E)(1)-(7) and (F) (first aid, personal care competency, special population training, annual continuing education and therapeutic diet training). Each staff member completes orientation and training applicable to the job within three working days of hire. It covers: (1) the physical layout of the facility; (2) the staff member's job responsibilities; (3) the facility's policies and procedures; (4) how to secure emergency assistance; and (5) residents' rights. No staff member is alone with residents until orientation and fire training are complete. Each year, and as needed, staff are trained on each resident right under ORC 3721.13(A), including (1) residents' rights and the staff's responsibility in implementing them and (2) the staff's obligation to give residents with similar needs comparable service. Personal care staff complete first-aid training within 60 days of hire (E(1)) and complete the personal care competency before working unsupervised (E(2)). Special population training (E(3)-(7)) and 8 hours of annual continuing education apply as set out below. Personal care staff are at least 16 years old; staff under 18 work only with on-site supervision by an adult over 18. The Administrator is at least 21 years old (OAC 3701-16-06(D)). Staff who assist with medication must be able to read, write and understand English. Professionals used by the facility hold current Ohio licenses where required (OAC 3701-16-06(J)).

definitions.definition: A day on which the staff member is scheduled to work. Orientation must be completed within three of the staff member's working days of hire.
Completion of personal care training taught by a registered nurse or licensed practical nurse, an ODH-approved nurse aide training program, or Medicare home health aide training.
Residents with cognitive impairment and residents with serious mental illness.
Annual in-service or outside training hours recorded for each staff member.

procedures: Before hire, the Administrator verifies the applicant's age: personal care staff must be at least 16, and the Administrator must be at least 21. Staff under 18 are scheduled only when an adult over 18 is on site to supervise them, and the schedule shows who the supervisor is. The Administrator checks background requirements under STF-02 before any direct-care duties.

For staff who may assist with medications, the Administrator confirms that the person can read, write and understand English, and records how this was verified. Authorization to assist with medication follows HLT-02.

Before working unsupervised, each personal care staff member must show proof of one of the following: RN or LPN-taught personal care training, an ODH-approved nurse aide program, or Medicare home health aide training (OAC 3701-16-06(E)(2)). Proof is placed in the personnel file. Until proof is received, the person does not provide personal care without direct supervision. If the facility trains the person itself, the training is taught by an RN or LPN, and the instructor signs the competency checklist.

Each new employee completes orientation within three working days of hire, using a written orientation checklist. The checklist covers each of the following: (1) a walk through the physical layout, including exits, fire equipment and resident areas; (2) the employee's job responsibilities; (3) the facility's policies and procedures; (4) how to secure emergency assistance, including 911, the on-call person and the Administrator; and (5) residents' rights under ORC 3721.13(A) (RR-01). The employee and the trainer sign and date the checklist.

Fire training is completed before the employee is alone with residents and includes the fire plan, alarm and extinguisher use, evacuation routes and the employee's assignment (SAF-06). The scheduler does not assign any new staff member alone with residents until the orientation checklist and fire training are both signed.

Orientation also includes abuse, neglect and exploitation reporting (SAF-01), infection control (SAF-07), incident reporting (SAF-02), confidentiality (RR-07), emergency procedures (SAF-05), staff boundaries (STF-06), and job-specific topics such as dementia care, elopement response and food safety.

Each personal care staff member completes first-aid training from the American Red Cross, American Heart Association or an equivalent provider within 60 days of hire (OAC 3701-16-06(E)(1)). The Administrator records the date, provider and expiration. The scheduler makes sure that a staff member with current first-aid training is on site every shift (STF-01), and does not rely on a staff member who has no current training.

Where the facility serves residents with cognitive impairment or serious mental illness, personal care staff complete 2 hours of initial training for each population within 14 days, and 4 hours of continuing education per population each year (4 hours initial and 8 hours yearly if both populations are served), as set out in OAC 3701-16-06(E)(3)-(7). The Administrator sets the facility's standard that training is completed within 14 days of hire and before assignment to any resident with those needs, where practicable.

All personal care staff complete 8 hours of continuing education each year (OAC 3701-16-06(E)). The Administrator tracks each requirement separately and does not count the same hours toward more than one requirement unless the Administrator has confirmed in writing that the rule permits it.
Activity planners complete training for the cognitive impairment and mental illness populations the facility serves (OAC 3701-16-06(D); DL-02).

Staff who plan or prepare therapeutic diets receive training from a dietitian before they begin preparing or serving therapeutic diets (OAC 3701-16-06(F); DL-01). The dietitian's name, date and topics are recorded.

Each calendar year, every staff member receives training on each resident right under ORC 3721.13(A). The training explains (1) the rights of residents and the staff's responsibility in implementing them, and (2) the staff's obligation to give residents with similar needs comparable service. The Administrator also gives this training as needed, for example after a rights complaint, a survey finding or a change in law. Attendance is recorded with the date, trainer, topics and signature.

The Administrator verifies that each licensed professional used by the facility (for example nurse, dietitian, therapist) holds a current Ohio license where required, checks the license at hire and at renewal, and does not allow a professional to practice with a lapsed license (OAC 3701-16-06(J)).

The Administrator keeps a training matrix showing each staff member's hire date, orientation, fire training, first aid, personal care competency, special population hours, annual CE hours, rights training and license expirations. The matrix is reviewed monthly. Staff whose training is overdue are given a due date, and the Administrator removes them from tasks requiring that training until it is complete.

Training records are kept in the personnel file (STF-05) on the forms the ODH director provides where required (OAC 3701-16-05(K)). Training results, including competency problems, are reported to the QAPI process (GOV-04) at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Verifies age, qualifications and licenses, ensures every training requirement is met on time, keeps the training matrix, and removes untrained staff from tasks.
Conducts orientation and fire training, completes and signs the orientation checklist, and observes competency.

responsibilities.role: Registered nurse or licensed practical nurse
responsibilities.duty: Teaches personal care training and signs competency verification where the facility provides it.
Trains staff in therapeutic diets before preparation or service.
Complete required training on time, keep certificates and report license or certification changes.

Signed orientation checklist (layout, job duties, policies, emergency help, resident rights) with date
Fire training record
First-aid certificate with provider and date
Proof of personal care competency (RN/LPN-taught, ODH-approved aide program or home health aide training)

policies.title: Employee Health and TB Screening
policies.applies_to: All paid staff, including administrator, acting administrator, direct care, dietary, housekeeping, maintenance, and contract or agency personnel who work in the facility.
policies.purpose: To protect residents and staff from communicable disease, to keep impaired workers away from residents, and to document that each worker was examined before working, as OAC 3701-16-06(A)-(C) requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] meets OAC 3701-16-06(A)-(C) (official checklist item A-D, Personnel Health Policies) as follows. (1) No staff member works during the communicable stage of a transmissible disease unless the staff member's duties and precautions are modified so that transmission is minimized. (2) No staff member works while impaired by alcohol or drugs. (3) Every paid worker has a health examination by a health professional within 30 days before starting work or on the first day of work, and the facility keeps a copy of the exam. TB screening follows the facility's written TB control plan, which is built on OAC 3701-15-03 and described in SAF-07. The Administrator confirms the current TB screening requirements with ODH before the plan is finalized and whenever the rule changes. Staff with occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious materials are also covered by the federal bloodborne pathogens standard, 29 CFR 1910.1030.

definitions.definition: The period during which a person with a transmissible disease can pass it to others, as determined by the treating health professional, the infection prevention designee, or public health guidance.

Unable to perform job duties safely because of alcohol, illegal drugs, or lawfully prescribed or over-the-counter medication, as shown by observed behavior, odor, speech, coordination, or a test result.
A licensed physician, advanced practice registered nurse, or physician assistant, or another licensed professional acting within his or her scope of practice, who performs the pre-employment exam.
The trained staff member named under the infection control program (SAF-07) and reported to ODH (REC-02).

procedures: Before the offer becomes final, the Administrator tells each applicant in writing that a health exam by a health professional is required, and that it must be dated within the 30 days before the first day of work or completed on the first day of work.

The Administrator or designee gives the applicant the facility's exam form [HEALTH EXAM FORM]. The form records the date, the examiner's name and credential, a statement that the worker is able to perform the job's duties, and the TB screening result required by the TB control plan.

The Administrator or designee reviews the completed exam before the worker's first shift. If it is not complete, the worker does not begin unsupervised duties and the start date is rescheduled, or the exam is completed on the first day before any resident contact.

A copy of the exam is placed in the worker's personnel-compliance file (STF-05). Any medical detail beyond the fit-for-duty statement and TB result is kept in a locked, separate confidential employee health file.

The infection prevention designee applies the TB screening steps in the written TB control plan (OAC 3701-15-03) to each new hire. The designee tracks follow-up dates and records them on the staff health tracking log.

New staff receive written instructions at orientation (STF-03) listing the symptoms and diagnoses that must be reported to the supervisor before a shift or when they appear. Examples are fever, vomiting, diarrhea, an undiagnosed rash, active TB, and a draining or infected skin lesion.

A staff member who has symptoms or a diagnosis of a transmissible disease calls the supervisor or on-call person before the shift, and does not come to work until the supervisor has spoken with the Administrator or infection prevention designee.

The Administrator or infection prevention designee decides, using the treating professional's advice and public health guidance, whether the worker (a) stays home through the communicable stage, or (b) works with modified duties and precautions that minimize transmission, such as no food preparation, no direct personal care, or a mask and gloves. Modified duties are never assigned if they would expose residents to risk. Staff are not penalized for reporting illness.

A worker who stayed home for a communicable illness returns only after the treating professional clears the worker, or after the designee confirms that the communicable stage has ended. The clearance is filed in the confidential employee health file.
Outbreaks, such as suspected influenza, norovirus, COVID-19, or TB, are handled under SAF-07, and the Administrator makes any required public health report.

Every supervisor watches for impairment. If a supervisor reasonably suspects impairment from alcohol or drugs, the supervisor removes the worker from resident contact immediately and tells the Administrator or on-call person. A second member of management witnesses the observations when possible.

The Administrator arranges safe transportation for the worker, who is not permitted to drive when impairment is suspected. The Administrator arranges replacement coverage so staffing under STF-01 is maintained.

The supervisor writes a factual description of the signs observed, the time, and the witnesses. The Administrator applies the facility's drug and alcohol testing and discipline rules, up to termination.

Staff who take prescribed medication that may affect their ability to work safely may confidentially tell the Administrator so duties can be adjusted. The Administrator does not require disclosure of the diagnosis.
If a resident was harmed or placed at risk by an impaired or ill worker, the Administrator follows SAF-01 and SAF-02 for investigation and reporting.
The Administrator reviews the staff health tracking log monthly and reports exam compliance and communicable-illness exclusions to the QA committee (GOV-04) at least quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Requires and verifies the pre-employment exam, decides on exclusion or modified duties with the designee, handles impairment cases, and makes sure files are complete.
Applies the TB control plan to each worker, tracks screening dates, advises on exclusion and return to work, and keeps the staff health tracking log.
Remove suspected impaired workers from resident contact, receive illness calls, and report to the Administrator at once.
Obtain the exam before starting, report symptoms and diagnoses before working, and come to work free of impairment.

documentation: Pre-employment health exam copy in the personnel-compliance file
TB screening results and follow-up, as required by the TB control plan
Staff health tracking log
Illness exclusion and return-to-work notes
Confidential employee health file, locked and kept apart from the general personnel file
Impairment observation report and Administrator's action note

policies.title: Personnel Records
policies.applies_to: Administrator, acting administrator, and all paid staff and contract personnel; the Administrator and any designated record keeper.
policies.purpose: To keep a complete, current personnel-compliance file for each worker so that the facility can show a state surveyor that every worker met health, training, orientation, and credential requirements before working with residents.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps personnel-compliance records on the forms the ODH director provides (OAC 3701-16-05(K)). Each worker has a personnel-compliance file that holds the health exam (within 30 days before or on the first day of work, OAC 3701-16-06), the first-aid certificate (within 60 days of hire), the personal care competency documentation completed before the worker works unsupervised, the orientation sign-off (within 3 working days, and before the worker is ever alone with residents), the background check results, continuing education (CE) records and credentials. Ohio licenses of professionals are verified before work begins and kept current. Files are kept on site and are available to surveyors on request.

definitions.definition: The file or forms, using the director-provided format, that show each worker met the health, training, orientation, background check, and credential requirements.
The worker's hire date each year, used to track CE and other recurring items.
Working with residents without another qualified, fully cleared staff member present.

procedures: The Administrator designates a personnel record keeper in writing: [RECORD KEEPER NAME AND TITLE]. The Administrator remains accountable for the files.
Before a worker's first shift, the record keeper opens a file using the director-provided compliance forms, with a checklist cover sheet for each required item and its due date.

Before the first shift, the file must hold: the signed application and job description, proof of age as needed, the pre-employment health exam (STF-04), and the completed background check and registry results (STF-02).

Within 3 working days of hire, the worker completes orientation. The orientation covers physical layout, job duties, policies and procedures, how to secure emergency help, and resident rights. The worker, the trainer, and the date sign the orientation checklist, which is filed.
The worker also completes fire training before working alone. The record keeper confirms that orientation and fire training are both signed off before the worker is scheduled alone with residents.

The record keeper enters the hire date and calculates the 60-day first-aid deadline on the tracker. A copy of the first-aid certificate from the Red Cross, the American Heart Association, or an equivalent provider is filed within 60 days of hire. Staff who lack a certificate at day 45 are scheduled for the next class.

Before working unsupervised, each personal care worker's file must show completion of personal care training taught by an RN or LPN, an ODH-approved aide program, or Medicare home health aide training. The file holds the certificate or the nurse's signed competency checklist.

For professionals such as RNs, LPNs, nursing home administrators, therapists, and dietitians, the record keeper verifies the Ohio license on the licensing board's online verification system before the first shift. A printout or screenshot with the date is filed. Verification is repeated at each renewal and at least annually.
The record keeper tracks CE hours and each worker's anniversary date. The Administrator's own CE is tracked under STF-07. Certificates are filed within 7 days of completion.

The record keeper runs a compliance check of every file on the first business day of each month. Missing or expiring items are listed on a deficiency report to the Administrator, who sets a correction date within 14 days.
A worker whose required item is overdue is not scheduled alone. If the item is the exam, orientation, or personal care competency, the worker is removed from unsupervised duty until it is cured.
The Administrator keeps the staffing schedule and time records that show who was on duty, and checks them against the files.

Personnel files are stored in a locked cabinet or access-controlled electronic system. Only the Administrator, the record keeper, and designated managers may view them. Confidential employee health information is kept in a separate locked file.

When a surveyor asks, the Administrator produces the requested files promptly. Files are kept for the length of employment and afterwards for [PERSONNEL RECORD RETENTION PERIOD], which the Administrator sets after consulting counsel.
The Administrator reports personnel-file compliance rates to the QA committee (GOV-04) quarterly.

responsibilities.duty: Keeps overall accountability, reviews monthly deficiency reports, resolves gaps, and makes files available to surveyors.
Builds and maintains files on the director-provided forms, tracks due dates, verifies licenses, and runs the monthly check.
Do not schedule a worker alone until the record keeper confirms clearance.
Provides complete documents, attends training, and brings in certificates and renewals on time.

documentation: Director-provided personnel-compliance forms
Health exam, first-aid certificate, personal care competency record, and orientation sign-off in each file
Background check and registry results
CE tracker and certificates
License verification printouts and renewal dates
Monthly personnel-file compliance report and deficiency correction notes

policies.title: Staff Conduct and Professional Boundaries
policies.applies_to: All employees, contractors, volunteers, and students; the Administrator and governing body in enforcing it.
policies.purpose: To protect residents from exploitation, coercion, and boundary violations, to uphold residents' rights under ORC 3721.13, and to keep the facility's staff safe, sober, and professional.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] expects every staff member to treat residents with dignity and to keep professional boundaries. Staff may not coerce a resident to assign assets (OAC 3701-16-11). Staff may not serve as a resident's guardian or attorney-in-fact unless related to the resident. Residents are never used as staff: no resident is mandated, coerced, or persuaded to supervise residents, give personal care, administer medication, or manage the facility (OAC 3701-16-05(E)). Staff may not work while impaired by alcohol or drugs (OAC 3701-16-06). As a facility standard, staff are prohibited from giving or taking gifts, loans, or any financial dealings with residents or their families. Residents' rights under ORC 3721.13(A), including freedom from abuse, privacy, and civil rights, cannot be waived (ORC 3721.13(C)). Violations lead to discipline up to termination and may be reported to authorities.

definitions.definition: The limit that separates a staff member's role as a paid caregiver from personal, financial, romantic, or social relationships with a resident.
Taking or using a resident's money, property, or labor for the benefit of someone other than the resident without informed consent.
A person given authority by a power of attorney to act for another person.
As defined in STF-04.

procedures: At orientation (STF-03), each new staff member receives this policy, reads it, and signs an acknowledgment. The signed form is filed in the personnel-compliance file (STF-05).

Staff are trained at orientation and annually on residents' rights, dignity, and boundaries. Training uses concrete examples such as accepting a cash gift, borrowing a resident's car, or friending a resident on social media.

Staff do not accept money, gifts, loans, or property from residents or their families. A staff member who is offered a gift politely declines. Shared perishable items such as a box of cookies for the whole unit may be accepted on behalf of the team after the Administrator is told.
Staff do not borrow from, lend to, sell to, or buy from residents, and do not use a resident's belongings, accounts, credit cards, or identity for personal use.

Staff do not coerce, pressure, or persuade a resident or family member to sign over assets, change a will or beneficiary, or add the staff member to an account. Any request of that kind from a resident is reported to the Administrator the same day.

Staff do not act as guardian or attorney-in-fact for a resident unless they are related to the resident. A staff member who is asked to take such a role tells the Administrator. The Administrator documents the relationship before any appointment is accepted.
Staff do not handle resident funds except under RR-05 and a witnessed written authorization. They never hold a resident's bank card or PIN for personal convenience.

Residents do not work as staff. The Administrator and supervisors never ask, assign, or encourage residents to supervise other residents, give personal care, give medications, or manage the facility. A resident who volunteers for an ordinary social activity, such as setting up a game, may do so freely and without pressure, and may stop at any time.

Staff keep relationships with residents professional. Romantic, sexual, or exploitative relationships are prohibited. Staff do not share personal phone numbers, visit residents off duty without Administrator approval, or post about residents on social media (RR-07).

Staff respect resident rights under ORC 3721.13(A): they knock before entering, protect privacy during care, honor choices of physician and pharmacist, and never limit a resident's communication or visitors except under RR-01 and SAF-08.
Staff report to work free of impairment. A supervisor who suspects impairment follows STF-04 and removes the worker from resident contact at once.

A staff member who sees or suspects a boundary violation, exploitation, or abuse reports it right away to the Administrator, or to the on-call person if the Administrator is unavailable, and follows SAF-01. Retaliation against a reporter is prohibited.

The Administrator investigates each report within 24 hours. Staff under investigation may be removed from resident contact. The Administrator documents findings and actions, and makes required reports to authorities (SAF-01, REC-02).
Substantiated violations lead to discipline up to termination. The Administrator reports to the licensing board, the state registry, or law enforcement as the law requires.
The Administrator reviews boundary complaints and outcomes with the QA committee (GOV-04) each quarter.

responsibilities.duty: Trains staff, investigates reports, enforces discipline, and refuses assignments of authority that violate this policy.
Model professional conduct, watch for violations or impairment, and report concerns immediately.
Follow the boundaries in this policy, decline gifts and financial dealings, and report violations.
Adopts this policy and reviews its enforcement through QA reports.

documentation: Signed staff acknowledgment of this policy in the personnel-compliance file
Orientation and annual training records on residents' rights and boundaries

Disciplinary records

policies.title: Administrator Qualifications and Continuing Education
policies.applies_to: The Administrator, the acting administrator, and the governing body that appoints them.
policies.purpose: To make sure the person responsible for daily operation is qualified, is trained, and is on site as Ohio requires.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME]'s Administrator is at least 21 years old and qualifies under OAC 3701-16-06(H) by one of the following: a nursing home administrator license; 3,000 hours of operational responsibility; 100 credit hours in gerontology or health care; a bachelor's degree; or a licensed health professional credential. The governing body checks the exact text and any conditions of OAC 3701-16-06(H) before appointment. The Administrator completes 9 hours of continuing education every year. The Administrator is responsible for daily operation, is on site at least 20 hours per week between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m., and is reachable at other times (OAC 3701-16-05(A)-(B)). The facility designates an acting administrator, age 21 or older, to cover absences.

definitions.definition: The person designated by the operator who is responsible for the daily operation of the facility.
A person at least 21 years old designated in writing to act when the Administrator is absent.
Training hours related to the administrator's duties, such as aging, resident care, regulations, safety, and management, with proof of completion.
A record of the dates and hours the Administrator is physically at the facility between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m.

procedures: Before appointing an Administrator, the governing body (GOV-01) reviews proof of age (21 or older) and documentation of the qualifying pathway under OAC 3701-16-06(H), such as the nursing home administrator license, records of 3,000 hours of operational responsibility, transcripts or certificates showing 100 credit hours in gerontology or health care, a bachelor's degree, or a license as a health professional.

The governing body checks the current text of OAC 3701-16-06(H) with ODH or counsel and writes in the minutes why the person qualifies. The proof is filed in the Administrator's personnel-compliance file (STF-05).
Any professional license is verified on the licensing board's online system before appointment and at each renewal.
The operator notifies ODH of the Administrator's name when a license application or change is made, using the director-provided forms (GOV-02, REC-02).
The Administrator is physically on site at least 20 hours each week between 8 a.m. and 6 p.m. The Administrator records arrival and departure times on the on-site hours log daily.
The Administrator can be reached by phone at all other times. The after-hours number [PHONE] is posted at the nurses' station and given to all staff.

The governing body designates in writing an acting administrator who is 21 or older, is oriented to the facility, and knows the emergency procedures. The name and phone number are posted and given to staff.

The Administrator or operator sets a coverage schedule (OAC 3701-16-05(E)) that includes vacations, emergencies, and long absences. The schedule names who is acting administrator and who is on call each day. The Administrator reviews and updates it quarterly.

The Administrator hands over to the acting administrator before every absence. The handover covers open incidents, resident changes in condition, pending admissions and discharges, and contact numbers.

If the Administrator will be absent for an extended period, or leaves, the governing body immediately names a qualified acting or replacement administrator and notifies ODH as required by REC-02 and GOV-06.

The Administrator completes at least 9 hours of CE every year. The Administrator picks courses relevant to the role, such as dementia care, infection control, resident rights, medication safety, emergency preparedness, and regulatory updates.
The Administrator files each CE certificate in the personnel-compliance file within 7 days of completion and updates the CE tracker with the anniversary date.
The governing body reviews the hours log and CE tracker every quarter. If the Administrator is behind on CE at the 9-month point, the governing body requires a completion plan within 30 days.
The Administrator brings all concerns about on-site hours, qualifications, or CE shortfalls to the governing body immediately. The governing body takes corrective action and records it in minutes.

responsibilities.duty: Appoints a qualified Administrator and acting administrator, verifies qualifications, approves the coverage schedule, and reviews hours and CE quarterly.
Is responsible for daily operation, keeps the on-site hours log, completes 9 hours of CE yearly, remains reachable, and prepares handovers.
Is 21 or older, is oriented, and assumes administrator duties during designated absences.
Files proofs of qualification and CE, and tracks anniversary dates.

documentation: Proof of the Administrator's age and qualifying pathway
License verification, if any
On-site hours log
Coverage schedule and acting administrator designation
CE tracker and certificates
Governing body minutes showing appointment and quarterly review

policies.title: Resident Records and Retention
policies.applies_to: All staff who create, use, or store resident records, paper or electronic; Administrator, nursing and care staff, and records custodian.
policies.purpose: To keep complete, accurate, confidential resident records, to protect privacy as ORC 3721.13(A) and HIPAA require, and to retain and produce records properly.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] keeps a record for each resident. The record holds the initial assessment (written within 48 hours of admission, with the items in OAC 3701-16-08(C)(11)-(12) within 14 days), annual reassessments (within 30 days of the anniversary date) and change-in-condition reassessments, the service plan, the medication list and medication administration record, notes of significant changes in health status and interventions, incident notations, and signed acknowledgments. Incidents are also entered in a separate incident log (OAC 3701-16-12). Resident records are confidential under ORC 3721.13(A) and are protected under HIPAA, including the privacy documentation standards in 45 CFR 164.530. Menus are kept 3 months. Drill records, fire inspection reports, and monthly fire safety records are kept 3 years. The retention period for resident records is [RESIDENT RECORD RETENTION PERIOD], which the Administrator sets after confirming it with counsel before the manual is final.

definitions.definition: The paper or electronic file holding the documents about a resident's admission, assessment, services, medications, health changes, and acknowledgments.
A separate log of incidents with time, place, date, description, and action taken.
The record of each medication given or assisted, with date, time, dose, and initials.
The staff member designated by the Administrator to manage file storage, access, and retention.

procedures: The Administrator designates a records custodian in writing: [RECORDS CUSTODIAN NAME AND TITLE].

On the day of admission, staff open a record that contains the admission agreement and signed acknowledgments (RR-04, ADM-02), the resident rights acknowledgment, advance directive information (RR-06), and emergency contacts and physician information.

The nurse or qualified assessor completes the written initial assessment within 48 hours of admission. The items required within 14 days (OAC 3701-16-08(C)(11)-(12)) are completed by day 14. An assessment done within 90 days before admission may be used if it is current and reviewed. Dates and the assessor's signature are on each page. See ADM-04.

Reassessments are done at least annually within 30 days of the anniversary date, and sooner on a change in condition or function that calls for new services or equipment. Each documents diagnoses, diet, weight, medications, and function.
The service plan (ADM-05) is signed and dated, and updated after each reassessment. Superseded versions are kept in the record.

Each resident's current medication list and MAR are in the record (HLT-01, HLT-02). Telephone orders are taken only by a licensed nurse and signed by the prescriber within 14 days. The signed order is filed. Medication records are reviewed each month for completeness.

On a significant adverse change in health status, staff arrange immediate intervention, enter a note in the record, give information to the treating party, and notify the resident's sponsor (HLT-04). The note shows the time, what was observed, who was told, and the outcome.

For every incident, staff write an entry in the separate incident log with the time, place, date, description, and action taken, and the Administrator investigates (SAF-02). A brief factual notation is also made in the resident's record.

Entries are legible, dated, timed, and signed or initialed with the writer's title. Corrections are made by a single line through the error with the date and initials. Records are never altered after the fact. Late entries are labeled as such.

Records are kept confidential under ORC 3721.13(A). Paper records stay in a locked cabinet or room. Electronic records have individual passwords, role-based access, automatic log-off, and backup. Staff access only the records they need to do their jobs.

The facility releases resident information only with the resident's or authorized representative's written authorization, or when the law allows or requires disclosure. Requests are directed to the Administrator and logged. See RR-07.

Residents and authorized representatives may review the resident's record on request, with a staff member present. The Administrator responds within a reasonable time, and no one is charged for review of a record in the facility's possession [unless stated in the admission agreement under RR-04].
When a resident transfers or is discharged, the facility sends needed information, such as the current medication list and a health summary, and keeps the original record.

Menus as served are kept for 3 months. Fire drill records, fire inspection reports, and monthly fire safety records are kept 3 years (SAF-06, DL-01). The records custodian files them in separate labeled binders or folders and checks them quarterly.

The custodian keeps closed resident records in a locked, access-controlled space for [RESIDENT RECORD RETENTION PERIOD]. HIPAA-required privacy documentation is retained as 45 CFR 164.530 requires. Where Medicaid waiver participation requires a longer period (GOV-07), the longer period applies. Destruction is by shredding or secure electronic deletion, and a destruction log is kept.
Resident records are available to ODH surveyors during inspection. The Administrator presents them, and surveyors may copy them as the law allows.
If the facility closes or changes operator, the Administrator follows GOV-06 to preserve records and notify residents of where records are kept.
The records custodian audits ten resident records each quarter for required elements, dates, and signatures, and reports results to the QA committee (GOV-04).

responsibilities.duty: Sets the retention period with counsel, oversees confidentiality, and approves release of records.
Maintains record organization, storage, retention, destruction logs, and quarterly audits.
Completes assessments, reassessments, and health-change notes on time.
Document accurately and promptly, protect confidentiality, and never remove records without authorization.

documentation: Resident records with assessments, reassessments, service plans, medication list and MAR, health-change notes, incident notations, and signed acknowledgments
Separate incident log
Release-of-information log and authorizations
Quarterly record audit results
Menu records (3 months), drill, fire inspection and monthly fire safety records (3 years)
Record destruction log

policies.title: Required Reports to the State
policies.applies_to: Administrator, acting administrator, infection prevention designee, operator and governing body; all staff for triggering events.
policies.purpose: To make sure [AGENCY NAME] makes every required report and application to ODH and the State Fire Marshal correctly and on time, and keeps a record of each one.
policies.policy: [AGENCY NAME] makes the following reports. (1) OAC 3701-16-12(C)(1), checklist item C(1), Infection control program: the facility designates one or more infection prevention and control designees and submits each designee's name and contact information, including email, on the ODH-prescribed electronic system within 10 days of appointment, and again within 10 days of any change. (2) OAC 3701-16-13(J)(6), checklist item J(6), Disaster plan: the Administrator notifies the ODH director by email or phone when normal business services are interrupted by an emergency or disaster involving the facility. (3) OAC 3701-16-13(W), checklist item W, Fire reporting: any fire, fire damage, or illness, injury, or death from fire or smoke inhalation is reported to the State Fire Marshal and ODH within 24 hours on their forms. (4) OAC 3701-16-03(M)(1)-(3), checklist item M(1)-(3), Closure notice: the notice to the director includes (1) an address where the operator can be reached, (2) a plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, and (3) assurances that residents go to the most integrated and appropriate setting, taking account of their needs, choice, and best interests. The notice is given at least 90 days ahead where practicable, and no less than 60 days ahead. The facility also files its license renewal application and fee, a change-of-operator application at least 60 days ahead, and personnel-compliance records on director-provided forms (OAC 3701-16-05(K)).

definitions.definition: The trained person or persons named by the facility to lead the infection control program.
A loss or serious disruption of normal facility services caused by an emergency or disaster, such as loss of power, water, heat, or the building.
The Director of the Ohio Department of Health, acting through the Bureau of Regulatory Operations (Licensure Unit).
A transfer of the facility's operation to a new operator, which requires an application to ODH.

procedures: The Administrator keeps the Regulatory Reporting Calendar and Contact Sheet. The Sheet lists the ODH Licensure Unit at (614) 466-7713 and liccert@odh.ohio.gov, the State Fire Marshal and local fire department contacts, and the ODH electronic system login holder. The Sheet is updated every quarter.

Infection prevention designee (item C(1)): On the day the governing body or Administrator names or replaces a designee, the Administrator logs the date, and enters the designee's name and contact information, including email, into the ODH-prescribed electronic system no later than 10 days after appointment. The same is done within 10 days of any change.
The Administrator saves the confirmation from the system and files it in the regulatory file. The designee's training record (SAF-07, STF-03) is filed in the personnel-compliance file.

Business interruption (item J(6)): When an emergency or disaster interrupts normal services, the Administrator or acting administrator notifies the ODH director by email or phone as soon as the residents are safe, and in all cases without delay, using the contact on the Contact Sheet.

The notice states the facility name and address, the nature of the emergency, the number of residents affected, actions taken (shelter in place, evacuation, receiving facility), and a call-back number [PHONE]. The Administrator records the date, time, method, and the ODH person reached on the Required Report Log (SAF-05).
The Administrator updates ODH when services are restored or when residents are relocated, and keeps a record of those updates.

Fire reporting (item W): After any fire, fire damage, or illness, injury, or death of a resident or staff member from fire or smoke inhalation, the person in charge calls 911 first if needed, secures resident safety, and tells the Administrator at once.

Within 24 hours of the event, the Administrator submits the report to the State Fire Marshal and to ODH on their forms. Each is sent and the confirmation is kept. The Administrator also follows SAF-06 and SAF-09, and records the date and time of submission on the Required Report Log.

Closure notice (items M(1)-(3)): If the operator decides to close the facility, the governing body approves the closure and the Administrator prepares the written notice at least 90 days before closure where practicable, and no less than 60 days before.

The closure notice to the director contains (1) an address where the operator can be reached after closure, (2) a plan for transfer and adequate relocation of all residents, including who will help each resident move, and (3) assurances that each resident will go to the most integrated and appropriate setting, taking account of the resident's needs, choice, and best interests. The Administrator follows GOV-06 and ADM-07 for resident and family notices and relocation.

Change of operator: A proposed new operator must file the application with ODH at least 60 days before the change. The Administrator confirms the filing date on the calendar and tracks the application to completion. See GOV-02 and GOV-06.

Initial licensure: The initial application is filed at least 60 days before the proposed opening, with the CPA-signed 3-month solvency statement, a certificate of occupancy (R-4, I-1, or I-2), and the fire and heating reports. The fee is $320 per 50 beds or part thereof of licensed capacity, paid with the application and non-refundable. See GOV-02.

License renewal: The Administrator files the renewal application and the annual fee ($320 per 50 beds or part thereof) before the license expires. The date is entered on the calendar 120 days out, with a 30-day reminder.
Personnel-compliance records are kept on the forms the director provides (STF-05) and are available on request.

The Administrator checks the Required Report Log monthly to confirm that every reportable event has been reported and that deadlines were met. Late or missed reports are reviewed with the governing body, and the cause is corrected.

The Administrator presents a summary of reports made to the QA committee quarterly (GOV-04). All copies and confirmations are kept in the regulatory file for at least [REGULATORY REPORT RETENTION PERIOD].

Makes reports during the Administrator's absence.
Gives the Administrator accurate contact information and tells the Administrator of any change at once.
Call 911 as needed, then notify the Administrator immediately of any fire, smoke event, or service interruption.
